author: EDRi
title: EU transforms Frontex into a high-tech deportation command centre
content:
On 27 October 2026, the European Commission tabled a new Regulation for Frontex, the EU's border agency, expanding its powers and refocusing its mandate on deportations, preventing arrivals, and surveillance beyond EU territories and into social media. This would effectively turn Frontex into the EU's deportation agency, equivalent of ICE in the United States.

By Protect Not Surveil Coalition (guest author) · November 19, 2026

At the centre of this reform is a budget that would almost double to nearly €12 billion for 2028–2034, leading to a massive expansion of the EU security and surveillance industrial complex. Frontex will test and deploy new technology to repress migrants, funnelling billions of taxpayer money to surveillance, security and defence contractors. EU’s hostile border security regime has for years produced systemic and massive human rights violations of migrants, refugees and racialised people, and those who stand in solidarity with them. This proposal will accelerate that.

The proposal operationalises the recently adopted Deportations Regulation and deepens Frontex’s position as the central actor of a Europe-wide deportation machine. This will make the agency responsible for collecting and analysing data from Member States in order to “predict” deportation needs, and allocating resources to them. Frontex will now have a “Deportation Coordination Centre” that is expected to act at all stages of the deportation procedure, from detecting and identifying people that may be expulsed, booking or arranging flights and escorts, to monitoring their “reintegration” in the destination country.

Alarmingly, it expands Frontex’s powers to deport outside of the EU’s borders. Based on a simple status agreement, Frontex will be able to deport people from one third country to another, with the aim of preventing people from even reaching the EU. This will likely mean sharing sensitive data with third countries and countries of origin, where individuals may be at risk of persecution or harm.

The Frontex mandate reform comes in a package with a proposal to digitalise the management of deportation cases. The border control agency is given a key role in the harmonised technical design of EU and national digital systems, to exchange data on deportations, including sensitive data transfers to third countries (biometric data, travel documents and history, grounds for deportation, health data, etc.), and automate certain steps of the procedure, such as adding deportation orders in the Schengen Information System (SIS) to detect people.

With this reform, Frontex’s practice of “debriefing interviews” is codified, particularly during the screening procedure introduced by the Migration Pact. The agency conducts these covert “voluntary” interrogations of people immediately after they disembark or cross the border. During these interviews, the agency extracts data from migrants deemed to be “suspects” of “cross-border crime”, without the possibility for migrants to seek legal counsel. Debriefing interviews have been rightfully criticised for their absence of fundamental rights monitoring and their unfairness as they take place when a person is detained and lacks privacy.

A new “Online Monitoring and Response Centre” will also surveil social media platforms to identify “suspicious behaviours or trends” in people’s movements at the EU borders, and before that, in the countries of origin and transit. Aggregated data collected online will be fed into Frontex’s “risk analysis” to guide border forces’ deployment and reaction. Social media monitoring was already declared as carrying high-risk for violating the fundamental rights of people affected, and was banned by the European Data Protection Supervisor in 2019 when first implemented by the EU Agency for Asylum.

Frontex will also seek designation as a trusted flagger under the Digital Services Act (DSA), allowing the agency to report pieces of online content to platforms for removal, effectively giving the agency extrajudicial powers to police the internet. It may also recommend national authorities to issue binding take-down notices. Frontex depriving people from finding legal support, sharing their stories or expressing solidarity is undoubtedly a serious infringement of freedom of expression.

All information collected during debriefings and online monitoring activities will contribute to Frontex’s border surveillance intelligence gathering called “European situational …

author: Andrea DiP
title: Países europeus adotam “modelo Trump” e criam centro de deportação em Ruanda
content:
Na última segunda-feira (16/11), cinco países europeus anunciaram que irão criar um centro de deportação em Ruanda, que deve funcionar a partir de 2027. Áustria, Dinamarca, Alemanha, Grécia e Holanda querem intensificar as remoções de imigrantes que tiveram os vistos negados na Europa ou não tiveram seus pedidos de refúgio aceitos e não podem voltar aos seus países de origem. Ruanda, em troca, deve receber verbas dos governos europeus para construir e gerir os centros, que ficarão na capital, Kigali.


O acordo vem na sequência de uma recente reforma da União Europeia que permitiu a criação de centros fora do bloco. Em uma coletiva de imprensa conjunta realizada em Viena na segunda-feira, o chanceler austríaco Christian Stocker afirmou que os cinco países desejavam “aliviar a pressão” sobre os sistemas europeus de asilo e impedir que traficantes organizassem viagens mortais pelo Mediterrâneo. Em comunicado escrito, o governo holandês afirmou que os cinco países vão repatriar, na primeira fase do acordo, apenas homens solteiros.


O anúncio foi recebido como um escândalo por organizações de direitos humanos, que publicaram um comunicado dizendo que os planos permitem que pessoas sem direito de permanecer na UE sejam enviadas para países com os quais não têm nenhuma ligação. “Essas políticas transferem as pessoas, e a responsabilidade por sua segurança e direitos, para fora da vista do público e além do escrutínio”, diz a carta, assinada por 45 ONGs de quize países. 


A escolha de Ruanda também preocupa. A Human Rights Watch (HRW) apontou para o “histórico de repressão à dissidência, detenção arbitrária, maus-tratos em centros de detenção” do país e o apoio de Ruanda a um grupo armado antigovernamental na República Democrática do Congo. “Centros de deportação fora do território europeu são a mais recente expressão cínica do esforço da União Europeia para transferir suas responsabilidades para outros países”, afirmou, em um comunicado, Clementine de Montjoye, pesquisadora sênior sobre a África e especialista em Ruanda na organização HRW. 


“Pagar a Kigali para sediar um programa de deportação não só causaria sofrimento e danos aos deportados, como também financiaria e proporcionaria influência política a um governo responsável por graves violações dos direitos humanos no próprio país e no exterior”, disse o pesquisador em entrevista ao jornal Le Monde Diplomatique. 


O anúncio marca a conclusão de uma iniciativa da UE para aumentar as deportações, lançada em 2024, à medida que a migração se torna um tema cada vez mais explorado por partidos de extrema-direita em vários países.


Com eleições se aproximando em vários países da Europa, os partidos de direita e centro direita tentam abocanhar parte desse eleitorado da extrema-direita que comprou a ideia (nada nova) de que as crises políticas, econômicas e o aumento da criminalidade são culpa dos imigrantes e que tudo estaria resolvido com deportações em massa. 


Eu conheço bem essa retórica e a sua eficácia. Em uma recente conferência de centro-direita que acompanhei em Berlin, um pesquisador apresentava divergências e convergências dentro do Parlamento Europeu sobre diversos temas; o único que unia da extrema-direita ao centro era o combate à imigração. 


Na Alemanha, por exemplo, já há algumas eleições o partido de extrema-direita AfD tem baseado suas campanhas em planos de deportação em massa, colocando nas caixas de correio de bairros com alto índice de imigrantes papéis que imitam “passaportes só de volta”. Nas eleições de 2024 para chanceler, ficaram famosos vídeos em que jovens da AfD cantavam músicas sobre “deportar aos milhões”. Em 2025, eu também me infiltrei em um congresso da AfD cujo tema principal eram os 10 anos de abertura das fronteiras do país pela ex-chanceler Angela Merkel e, diziam, o “fato” que a experiência multicultural havia falhado e enchido a Alemanha de “criminosos”, “terroristas” e pessoas que não se integram à cultura local e apenas se aproveitam dos benefícios sociais. Tudo baseado em dados falsos, vídeos sensacionalistas e até um ranking de crimes cometidos por cada nacionalidade. 


O plano europeu segue a mesma lógica de deportação para países terceiros – aqueles com os quais o imigrante não tem qualquer relação – que o

governo Trump

 tem aplicado desde 2025.  Os Estados Unidos têm acordos com mais de uma dúzia de países africanos (alguns sigilosos inclusive), como Ruanda, Uganda, Camarões, Gana, além de outros na América Latina …

author: Stelinsky
title: Επιστολή «προς τον αδελφό ελληνικό λαό»
content:
Στα τέλη Αυγούστου του 2026 δημοσιεύτηκε μία επιστολή 300 μεταναστών που βρίσκονταν εκείνη την περίοδο έγκλειστοι στο καμπ της Σιντικής. Παραθέτουμε εδώ κάποια αποσπάσματα, θέλοντας ο λόγος των ίδιων των ανθρώπων να ακουστεί:

«Εσείς ακούσατε για εξέγερση στη Σιντική. Τι συνέβη και γιατί; Είμαστε στον καταυλισμό της Σιντικής. Είμαστε εδώ 14 μήνες.

Θέλουμε να βγούμε έξω και να κερδίσουμε τα προς το ζην. Είμαστε κουρασμένοι. Είμαστε παγιδευμένοι εδώ και 14 μήνες […].

Πού είναι οι οργανώσεις ανθρωπίνων δικαιωμάτων; Πού είναι οι οργανώσεις για τη δικαιοσύνη; Ζούμε εδώ με φαγητό που μόλις και μετά βίας επαρκεί για τη μέρα. Λάβαμε ένα πιάτο ρύζι, δύο μπιφτέκια και τρία αυγά για ολόκληρη την ημέρα.

Είμαστε εξαντλημένοι και πολλοί από εμάς σκέφτονται την αυτοκτονία. Αυτοί οι άνθρωποι έχουν δει τον θάνατο στη θάλασσα και έχουν υποστεί ταπεινώσεις και εξευτελισμό στα στρατόπεδα εδώ […].

Ναι, θέλουν να μας απελάσουν. Δεν μπορούμε να επιστρέψουμε στην πατρίδα μας. Υποφέρουμε, παρακαλούμε βοηθήστε μας, παρακαλούμε σώστε μας […].

Οι άνθρωποι εδώ είναι σαν ωρολογιακές βόμβες, αλλά κανείς δεν μας προσέχει. Είμαστε συντετριμμένοι σωματικά, ψυχολογικά και ηθικά. Έχουμε χάσει τόσα πολλά και κανείς δεν νιώθει τον πόνο μας […].

Ζούμε υπό καθεστώς καταπίεσης για πάνω από έναν χρόνο. Είδαμε τον πόνο στη Λιβύη, είδαμε τον θάνατο στη θάλασσα και είδαμε τον εξευτελισμό και την καταπίεση στο κλειστό κέντρο της Σιντικής. Χωρίς ρούχα και φαγητό, χωρίς μια αξιοπρεπή ζωή. Το μόνο που κάναμε ήταν να ονειρευόμαστε και να αγαπάμε την Ευρώπη […]».

Τα «κέντρα φιλοξενίας», δεν είναι παρά οι σύγχρονες φυλακές του πλεονάζοντος προλεταριάτου. Από τα σύνορα και τα αστυνομικά τμήματα μέχρι τα δικαστήρια, τα κέντρα κράτησης και τις φυλακές, οι μετανάστ(ρι)ες έρχονται αντιμέτωποι και αντιμέτωπες με ένα πλέγμα νομικών, διοικητικών και κατασταλτικών μηχανισμών, απειλητικών προς την ίδια τους την ύπαρξη.

Η αλληλεγγύη είναι όπλο ταξικό και διεθνιστικό. Ο αγώνας για την καταστροφή των στρατοπέδων συγκέντρωσης και το γκρέμισμα των συνόρων είναι κομμάτι του ευρύτερου αγώνα για την κοινωνική απελευθέρωση, ενάντια σε κράτος και κεφάλαιο. Στους αγώνες αυτούς, ο φασισμός αποτελεί την πιο πιστή εφεδρεία του συστήματος και το μακρύ χέρι της κρατικής καταστολής, σπέρνοντας μίσος σε μια προσπάθεια να διαιρέσει τις καταπιεσμένες.

Στεκόμαστε πάντα απέναντι στη θανατοπολιτική των κλειστών συνόρων, των δολοφονικών επαναπροωθήσεων και του συστημικού ρατσισμού και αντιλαμβανόμαστε τις εξεγέρσεις των μεταναστών μέσα στα camps ως ρωγμές στο μονοπώλιο της κρατικής βίας, ως φάρους αξιοπρέπειας. Δεν αντιμετωπίζουμε τους μετανάστες ως παθητικά θύματα που χρήζουν φιλανθρωπίας, αλλά ως ταξικά μας αδέλφια και υποκείμενα των κοινών μας αγώνων. Στεκόμαστε δίπλα στους μετανάστες της Σιντικής που διεκδικούν τα αυτονόητα αναδεικνύοντας τα βασανιστήρια και την εξαθλίωση που τους επιβάλλει το κράτος και ο φασισμός.

Ντόπιες και μετανάστριες να ενώσουμε τις οργές μας και να τσακίσουμε τη ρητορική μίσους σε κάθε γειτονιά, σχολείο και χώρο εργασίας. Οι εξεγερμένοι μέσα στα κολαστήρια είναι η δική μας φωνή πίσω από τα συρματοπλέγματα, και η δική μας δράση στους δρόμους οφείλει να είναι η δική τους ανάσα.

Μέχρι το ξήλωμα του τελευταίου συρματοπλέγματος.

author: Fabrizio Floris
title: The Sahara was never a border
content:
In July, Algeria and Mali reinstated their ambassadors and reopened their airspace to each other, more than a year after Algerian forces shot down a Malian drone near the border town of Tin Zaouatine.

Al Jazeera reported the thaw

; Agence France-Presse (AFP)

added

 that rebel advances in northern Mali had accelerated it, and that restoring cross-border security cooperation was a priority. In September, Algeria’s prime minister was

received in Bamako with military honors

. 

The reconciliation is about a border that both governments say they cannot control.

Farther east, on the Algeria–Niger frontier, the same logic works differently. The Niger-based NGO, Alarme Phone Sahara, counted more than 34,000 people

expelled from Algeria to Niger in 2025

, a record, up from 31,404 in 2024 and 26,031 in 2023. Migrants who are not Nigerien are left at a desert spot known as Point Zéro and they walk about 15km to Assamaka.

Both stories treat the Sahara as a line to be secured: a front to be held, a space to be cleared of the wrong people. Judith Scheele’s

Shifting Sands: A Human History of the Sahara

 (2025) is a sustained argument that this is the wrong picture. An anthropologist at the

École des hautes études en sciences sociales

, Scheele

combines historical archives, including many Arabic-language accounts, with decades of fieldwork

 and interviews with Saharans themselves. Edward Said taught us that places are imagined before they are governed; Fernand Braudel, that seas link as much as they divide. Scheele applies both lessons to a desert.

Scheele’s Sahara is a human world. The book moves from a city-building civilization in Libya’s Fezzan, contemporary with the Roman Empire, through the caravan trades that carried gold, salt, textiles, and enslaved people to the borderlands of Algeria, Mali, Niger, Chad, and Libya that she knows from her own travels.

The caravan of gold and spice is the image that outsiders inherited, and Scheele asks readers to separate Saharan from trans-Saharan trade: the second is the part that crosses the region and so leaves traces in archaeological sites and in sources written beyond it. Most Saharan trade, she suggests, was in staples, the cereals, dates, salt, cloth, dried meat and skins that groups such as the Arba’a and the Tubu carried. The fabled gold was something the explorer René Caillié never saw in Timbuktu.

The trade in staples survives, and it remains, in Scheele’s phrase, “relatively democratic”: anyone with a four-by-four, some capital and enough cousins along the road can become a carrier or trade on their own account, and negotiate with Malian customs officials. She also notes that the advance of trade routes, and the political rivalries that followed in the Maghreb, pushed North Africans deeper into the desert until they had little choice but to become trans-Saharan traders. Mobility, here, was as much pressure as opportunity. In northern Mali, she visits al-Khalil in 2009 and finds its trade booming. The oldest permanent house there dates from 1993 and began as a store for arms for the separatist rebellion of the early 1990s. Commerce, rebellion and settlement, in the Sahara, are often built with the same walls. What these cases share is a desert that is never empty. It is inhabited not by permanent settlements alone but by routes, encounters, negotiations, and obligations.

Scheele applies the same method to the subjects that dominate the headlines. Slavery, racism, religious militancy, terrorism and desertification each get their own treatment, and in each case, as a

reviewer for


Foreign Affairs


notes

, she shows how familiar narratives often grow out of outsiders’ fantasies of the desert as an inhospitable, impermeable barrier. She does not romanticize that circulation. The same routes carried enslaved people, reproduced racial hierarchies and concentrated wealth in few hands. Nor did colonial rule invent every division: Saharan societies had their own rivalries and territorial distinctions. But colonial administrations hardened them into borders drawn around distant capitals, and began to treat older routes as marginal, illicit, or dangerous. Independent states inherited that architecture, and with it a contradiction: communities keep depending on cross-border movement, while official policy reads that movement as a failure of control.

This is why emptiness is never an innocent description. Calling an inhabited space empty lets existing relationships …

author: Karen Gullo
title: European Commission Plan to Give Frontex Trusted Flagger Status Is A Threat to Free Speech
content:
EFF and 27 other human rights organizations

called

 on the European Commission today to retract a dangerous proposal granting its border agency Frontex to request that national authorities issue takedown orders for social media content and giving it “trusted flagger” status under the Digital Services Act (DSA), the EU regulation governing online platforms and content moderation in the region.

The extraordinarily improper proposal not only disregards the provisions of the DSA but also places a mechanism of enforcement overreach in the hands of a law enforcement agency that has

failed to safeguard people

 against serious human rights violations at EU borders.

Under the

proposal

, Frontex has the power to “monitor publicly accessible social media content, detect developments relevant to external border management, and support action against illegal online content linked to border-security risks.” Granting Frontex trusted flagger privileges on top of its existing mandate risks creating a powerful mechanism for over-enforcement, stifling the free expression of migrants, asylum seekers, and other marginalized groups. We warned the Commission of these risks in a

letter

.

The DSA is supposed to make online platforms more accountable and protect users’ fundamental rights, not give the EU power to sic its border police on people for exercising their right to free expression.

EFF and other rights organizations have for years

sounded alarms

about potential abuse under the DSA’s trusted flagger provision, which gives “Digital Services Coordinators” the ability to award entities—including law enforcement agencies—a privileged channel to alert online platforms about illegal content. We’ve taken the firm position that law enforcement cannot be trusted to properly flag illegal content. In July, we

told

 the Commission that giving law enforcement trusted flagger status could undermine fundamental rights and said that police agencies like Frontex should not be made trusted flaggers. 

The EU proposal gives Frontex decision-making power over free expression that is not envisaged under the DSA. First, content removal orders can only be issued by relevant national authorities. The DSA does not foresee a role for entities like Frontex to request such orders. Second,

trusted flaggers

 notify platforms of suspected illegal content—platforms must prioritize these notices and they have sole responsibility to decide to remove content. It’s not flaggers’ role to request removal orders from national authorities. Combining these powers blur enforcement and flagging functions, which the Commission’s own

draft guidelines

 on trusted flaggers explicitly caution against. 

“The risk of Frontex utilizing its power as both a Trusted Flagger and authority that can demand removal orders, to surveil user-generated speech, and over-flag content under the guise of  ‘border security risk’ is clear. This will likely result in platforms over-censoring content and chilling the speech of already marginalized groups, particularly those from migrant and asylum-seeking communities,” the letter says. 

We urge the Commission to rescind the proposal. It undermines the DSA, threatens fundamental rights of citizens and non-citizens, and is enforcement overreach that does not align with international human rights standards.

author: anred
title: Embarcación: cuando la destrucción del monte prepara el terreno para la catástrofe
content:
El violento temporal que azotó a Embarcación, en la provincia de Salta, el jueves 12 de noviembre dejó alrededor de 150 personas que necesitaron atención médica, viviendas dañadas, escuelas afectadas y árboles, postes y tendidos eléctricos derribados. Pero detrás de la devastación provocada por las lluvias y los fuertes vientos hay una historia que no comenzó con la tormenta: décadas de desmontes, avance de la frontera agropecuaria y explotación de los bienes comunes que transformaron profundamente el territorio.

Por Adrián Flores, para Red Eco Alternativo.


Salta – La localidad de Embarcación, en el departamento General José de San Martín, fue el epicentro de un fenómeno meteorológico de enorme intensidad. Las precipitaciones, las ráfagas de viento y la actividad eléctrica provocaron voladuras de techos, caída de árboles y postes de media tensión, cortes de electricidad y daños en establecimientos educativos. La magnitud del temporal obligó a desplegar operativos de emergencia y suspender las clases en las escuelas afectadas.


La violencia de esta tormenta también debe leerse en el contexto de los fenómenos climáticos extremos asociados a El Niño, cuya intensidad puede incrementar las precipitaciones y elevar el riesgo de inundaciones en distintas regiones. El escenario del Súper Niño vuelve todavía más preocupante esta situación. Pero estos fenómenos no actúan sobre territorios intactos: encuentran ecosistemas profundamente degradados por décadas de explotación.


Aquí se cruzan dos dimensiones de una misma crisis. Por un lado, un modelo de producción y consumo capitalista basado en la explotación intensiva de la naturaleza, que contribuye al calentamiento global. Por otro, la expansión de la frontera agropecuaria, los desmontes y la destrucción de los bosques nativos, que reducen la capacidad de los territorios para absorber y regular las lluvias.


En Embarcación, ambas dimensiones convergen dramáticamente. La misma matriz extractivista que impulsa la destrucción del monte profundiza las condiciones para que los fenómenos meteorológicos extremos se conviertan en catástrofes sociales. Las tormentas tienen causas meteorológicas, pero sus consecuencias están profundamente condicionadas por las decisiones económicas y políticas que transforman los territorios en mercancías.


Topadoras sobre territorios ancestralesMientras Embarcación enfrenta las consecuencias del temporal, las comunidades originarias del departamento San Martín continúan resistiendo el avance de los desmontes y el despojo territorial.


A principios de enero de 2026, en Misión Chaqueña, una comunidad wichí de más de 2.000 habitantes ubicada a 48 kilómetros de Embarcación, sus integrantes detectaron nuevamente a personas que derribaban árboles y quemaban sectores del bosque nativo. La respuesta fue inmediata: decenas de mujeres se organizaron y cortaron el camino para impedir el avance sobre su territorio ancestral.


El conflicto involucra al empresario agrícola salteño Claudio Ferrari, quien desde 2023 pretende apropiarse de una franja de monte que rodea a la comunidad. Aquel año, trabajadores vinculados al empresario comenzaron a abrir picadas, talar árboles y colocar postes para alambrar la zona. Ferrari sostuvo que había comprado esas tierras, aunque, según el abogado que acompaña a la comunidad, no presentó documentación que respalde sus pretensiones.


La defensa del territorio también tuvo consecuencias represivas. El miércoles 7 de enero de 2026 fueron detenidos Leonardo Pantoja y Marta Herrera cuando se presentaron en un destacamento policial para denunciar la tala del monte y las amenazas atribuidas al empresario. Marta fue liberada, mientras Greenpeace reclamó la inmediata libertad de Pantoja.


La comunidad cuenta con carpeta técnica, relevamiento georreferenciado y registro de Asuntos Indígenas. Sin embargo, sus integrantes denuncian obstáculos para acceder a la Justicia y señalan que el empresario pretende avanzar sobre tierras ocupadas ancestralmente por el pueblo wichí.


No se trata solamente de una disputa por la propiedad de la tierra. Es la defensa de un territorio que sostiene la identidad, la cultura y las condiciones materiales de vida de generaciones.


3.300 hectáreas arrasadas en territorio wichíLa dimensión de la destrucción quedó nuevamente expuesta en octubre de 2026, cuando Greenpeace difundió una denuncia realizada junto con comunidades wichí por el desmonte de más de 3.300 hectáreas de bosques nativos en el área …

author: Steven Methven
title: Cuts to Benefits Are Not the ‘End to Neoliberalism’ We Were Promised
content:
Tomorrow, the government will publish the Milburn report. That’s a long-awaited review into Britain’s one million young people not in employment, education or training – the so-called NEETs. Its contents, though, won’t come as a huge surprise, with its author, Tony Blair-era health secretary Alan Milburn, taking to the Sunday morning news rounds to pitch his plans while others briefed its contents to the press.


They’re trying to get ahead of what could be

a significant rebellion

 amongst backbench Labour MPs. And who can blame the rebels? After all, with swingeing cuts incoming, they’re the ones who’ll have to explain to young voters with disabilities and other health issues – as well as angry parents – why their lives are apparently worth less than those just a few years older than them.


In politics, life comes at you fast. But not so fast that we can’t remember what prime minister Andy Burnham pledged just four months ago – an

end to neoliberalism in this country

. That’s a tricky term to define, and while Burnham mentioned deregulation, privatisation and the fantasy of trickle-down economics as its major symptoms, there’s a simpler understanding near at hand. Neoliberalism is when a state decides that corporations, rather than citizens, are its clients.


Far from killing neoliberalism off, there’s more than an element of it in Milburn’s NEET plans. 


The shape of his proposals are familiar, the usual carrot-and-stick approach to welfare aimed at the bottom line, rather than the underlying conditions that put people in need of it. First, the cuts. Milburn will recommend that under-25s will

no longer be able to claim sickness and disability benefits

. Instead, there’ll be a one-stop “youth allowance”, capped at the standard rate of universal credit. So that will be a sharp cut to those who might expect to receive the additional universal credit health element. 


Personal independence payments will also be restricted: under 25s will no longer be able to access PIP. Instead, they’ll be able to

apply to “local funds” for help

 with specific “short-term expenses,” though those with the most severe needs will have their existing entitlements protected. 


Who knew that disability or debilitating illness take on a special reality when a person turns 25? Obviously, they don’t. But that ever-present national thought is at the heart of these proposed cuts: the problems – even the health problems – of the young are always a little bit unserious. They won’t be helped by empathy or care, that thought goes on, but only discipline and downplaying.


In his

government report released last month

, professor Peter Fonagy lists in detail the material conditions driving the mental health crisis in the country’s youth. Increased poverty, insecurity and crippling housing costs. Atomisation, loneliness and lack of opportunity. Growing existential dread around the climate, technology and the political future. An education system impoverished by alienation, comparison and intense scrutiny. 


Burnham has called the number of young people on existing benefits

“a moral failure”

. And it’s a profound one for sure. But it’s not their moral failure. It’s ours.


So will our collective failure be addressed in this review?


Unlikely. Instead, what’s been briefed is that the new, pared-back youth allowance will likely be contingent on recipients engaging with programmes aimed at getting them back into work. And while the scope of the cuts are crystal clear, that positive package remains vague. The papers have been told there’ll be investment for employment advisers, mental health support and internships, backed up by – potentially –

a new legal duty on the government

 to furnish every young person with a route into work. 


Great – but maybe let’s get that in place before the cuts? 


No, no. Young people must always get the stick first. And business? It’s the carrot for them.


“I think we should subsidise wages,”

Milburn told Laura Kuenssberg

 on Sunday, “Because young people today are walking into the workplace often with a mental health problem, ADHD or anxiety, and if you’re a small business, that’s a cost that you’ve got to absorb. The state has a responsibility to help them with that.”


The state has a responsibility to help

businesses

 to solve the social problems caused by the state relying on businesses to solve the social problems caused by the state relying on…


Stop the merry-go-round, it’s making us sick.

author: Unknown
title: Passer de la théorie à l'action : comment lutter contre le capitalisme énergétique vert ?
content:
Le capitalisme vert incarné par les énergies dites «

 

renouvelables

 

» est un impensé de la lutte pour la protection de l'environnement. Il repose sur une colonisation des consciences où la «

 

transition énergétique

 

» tient lieu de cheval de Troie pour faire accepter l'inacceptable : la destruction effective de l'environnement. Il est nécessaire de questionner ce mécanisme symbolique et de revenir à une lutte radicale et concrète contre l'exploitation humaine et des écosystèmes sous toutes ses formes.


Vantée sans relâche par les élites comme

LA

 solution au changement climatique, la transition énergétique est surtout

LA

 solution pour continuer à faire du «

 

business as usual

 

». Il est toujours question de faire du pognon en poursuivant la même logique d'extraction maximaliste des ressources naturelles. Malgré les beaux discours, la société thermo-industrielle se maintient en se «

 

greenwashant

 

». Plus pervers que le pétrole et le nucléaire, le photovoltaïque et l'éolien s'imposent par la colonisation des consciences avant celle des terres.


Penser les conséquences des énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

»


Face au bulldozer de la doxa de la transition énergétique, le chercheur Vincent Mignerot donne les bases d'une autodéfense intellectuelle. Assez rare pour être noté, Vincent Mignerot est

un chercheur autodidacte

 dont les thèses ont obtenu une forme de reconnaissance officielle par l'intelligentsia académique. Cette double caractéristique lui a donné la liberté nécessaire pour développer une pensée non-polluée par le préformatage universitaire et suffisamment étayée scientifiquement pour ne pas pouvoir être écartée d'un revers de la main par les mandarins des facs, les premiers chiens de garde du système dominant.


Vincent Mignerot est un penseur important, car il remet en cause le présupposé fondamental sur lequel repose la fiction de la transition énergétique :

les énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

» ne remplacent pas les énergies fossiles

. Au contraire, elles s'y ajoutent et ne font que faciliter l'exploitation des puits de pétrole jusqu'à la dernière goutte. On dilue le pétrole et le nucléaire avec les énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

» pour toujours plus de gabegies énergétiques :

SUV

 électriques,

IA

, cryptomonnaies… Plus de dope pour plus de junkies

 

!


Pour le dire de manière moins imagée : 30 ans de fable marketing sur les énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

» ne tiennent pas face à la

réalité mesurable

. La consommation d'énergie par habitant ne fait qu'augmenter et le bilan carbone fait de même. Pourtant, les énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

» se sont développées… pour le plus grand bénéfice de Total et compagnie (devenu TotalEnergies par volonté d'y associer la nouvelle poule aux œufs d'or «

 

renouvelables

 

»)

 

!


L'autre apport important de Vincent Mignerot est de considérer notre société capitaliste comme une société «

 

thermo-industrielle

 

», qui en conséquence répond aux lois de la thermodynamique, dont celle de l'entropie.


Quand

les thuriféraires de la transition énergétique

 évoquent des énergies «

 

renouvelables

 

», ils induisent dans la conscience collective l'idée d'un système fermé qui s'autoentretient et donc serait vertueux. Or, un panneau photovoltaïque ou une pale d'éolienne, ça s'use… «

 

Pas d'inquiétude

 

», vous répondront les transitionnistes, «

 

grâce au recyclage et à l'énergie produite par les autres éoliennes, on peut faire du neuf avec du vieux sans produire de

CO2

 

». Si le propos est volontairement caricatural par souci d'explicitation, il s'agit bien de l'idée qui se diffuse dans tous les cercles de la société capitaliste (

les partis politiques classés à gauche n'y échappant pas

), et sans remise en question.


C'est là que l'application par Vincent Mignerot des lois de la thermodynamique à notre société capitaliste permet de souligner une fausse impression. Dans le quotidien, le système capitaliste (occidental) apparaît très stable : il n'y a pas de manque d'énergie ou de ressources. Les prix peuvent être très élevés (par exemple celui de l'essence à cause de la guerre contre l'Iran déclenchée par Trump et Netanyahou), mais il n'y a pas de pénurie à l'échelle de la société (notre propos n'est pas ici d'aborder la question sous l'angle social et de la répartition des richesses au sein de la société, enjeu essentiel qui mérite une analyse à part entière).

author: dev
title: Quel monde de merde voulons-nous ?
content:
En manifestation, sur les réseaux sociaux, lors d'une compétition Hyrox, de la dernière biennale d'art contemporain à Venise ou encore sur les étals des librairies, la merde répand partout sa couleur et ses formes sans que nous parvenions nécessairement à comprendre les effluves sous-jacentes de ce

Zeitgeist

 fécal. Cette excrétion contemporaine, que Sigmund Freud qualifiait déjà, à l'orée du XX

e

 siècle, de « reste de terre » pour dire la honte et le rejet moderne qui lui était lié, raconte l'émergence d'un nouveau front socio-écologique et d'une bataille politique d'ampleur. En période de coulée brune, de ravages provoqués par les dernières mutations du Kkpitalisme, peut-être y aurait-il un autre monde de merde à revendiquer et à construire ? Quelques réflexions scatopolitiques par l'auteur et chercheur Cy Lecerf Maulpoix qui vient de faire paraître,

Fécal, Chronique d'un reste de terre

 aux éditions Trou Noir

.


Fascisme anal


Avant même que la chanson

Caca sur Bardella

 scandée lors dernières manifestations ne devienne obsédante, il existait déjà une rumeur, une petite musique courant sur ce dernier depuis quelques années. On croisait l'anecdote sur X, parfois taguée sur les murs après des manifestations, on en parlait autour d'un verre pour faire rire ses ami.es. Jordan Bardella se serait chié dessus à l'université. Une diarrhée foudroyante en cours de licence. La rumeur enfle et le récit imprègne d'autant plus nos consciences et nos imaginaires. Qu'y a-t-il de plus avilissant qu'un corps qui se chie dessus ? Rien de mieux qu'un relâchement public de sphincter pour faire tomber une figure politique d'envergure, qui plus est quand il s'agit d'un corps fasciste, d'apparence ultra-disciplinée, tiré à quatre épingles.


Plus qu'une

schadenfreude

 adressée à un ennemi politique, la caricature fécale s'inscrit inévitablement dans une longue histoire, antérieure au shitposting, visant des élus ou des figures d'autorité. Le pape, Louis XVI ou George Bush en ont fait les frais au cours de ces derniers siècles. Désacraliser les figures de pouvoir en les ramenant à leur corporéité, à leur « reste de terre », est peut-être vieux comme le monde, or, le motif articulant merde et violence fasciste dit possiblement autre chose. Citons par exemple les rumeurs de guerre portant sur les goûts scatophiles d'Adolf Hitler, les nombreuses photographies de soldats nazis en train de chier prises dans les années 1930-1940, qui ont fait l'objet d'un ouvrage il y a moins de dix ans

 [

1

]

, ou encore, bien plus récemment, en octobre 2025, cette vidéo IA de Donald Trump balançant des tonnes de merde depuis le cockpit d'un avion militaire sur des manifestants pendant les marches

No Kings

. Toutes disent à leur manière la force répulsive et fascinante de la merde, sa capacité d'avilissement et de dégradation.


Publiée en octobre 2025, la vidéo IA de Trump avait de quoi surprendre et captiver. Quelle autorité, quel tyran, quel homme politique s'était autorisé avant lui une telle association régressive (la Corée du Nord avait par exemple envoyé des ballons emplis de merde très concrets sur la Corée du Sud en 2024) ? Dans son ouvrage

Pénétration terminale

 (Audimat), sorti il y a quelques jours, la chercheuse et artiste Cindy Coutant y lit l'indice d'une culture technologique masculiniste et/ou technofasciste fière de sa décharge, d'une politique excrémentielle structurelle. Le corps du chef fasciste, de Trump à Elon Musk, de l'enfant-roi en position hégémonique sur son trône suspendu dans les airs ou depuis l'immatérialité du cloud, dispose des puissances alchimiques ultimes, celles de transformer la merde en arme autoritaire de délégitimation et d'écrasement massive. Le chef fasciste ne craint pas la merde, il se l'approprie. C'est ce que décrivait déjà Georges Bataille en 1933, dans

La structure psychologique du fascisme

en 1933. La société « homogène », productive et utile, rejette hors d'elle ce qui lui est impur ou inutilisable, des déchets et excréments jusqu'au sacré et à la dépense improductive. Cet « hétérogène » est l'objet de son hétérologie (ou scatologie). Le chef fasciste se pose en figure souveraine de cet hétérogène, capable de capter au profit de l'ordre autoritaire les pulsions collectives obscures et les jouissances secrètes ou taboues que le monde productif refoule.


Parce que le tyran détient le pouvoir d'imposer sa propre scatopolitique, de diffuser sa propre “économie de la mort”

author: WoMin
title: Africa Can Survive Without Capitalism: Feminist School on Land and Nature Commons
content:
From 2

nd

 to 6

th

 November 2026, WoMin in collaboration with the office of

Justice, Peace and Integration of Creation Franciscans Africa

 (JPIC – FA), hosted 35 women activists from Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania gathered in Nairobi for the

East African Feminist School on Land and Nature Commons

.


Drawn from four distinct community struggles – pastoralist women, forest community women, women farmers and fisherfolk – the participants came together to share their experiences of resisting the dispossession of communal land and nature commons.


As part of the recommendations emerging from the

Women’s Land Convergence

, the school sought to strengthen participants’ feminist analysis, foster cross-border solidarity, and build collective strategies towards a future beyond capitalism.


Nowhere is the drive for capitalist expansion seen more clearly than in the rush to dispossess African communities of their land and ways of life, for corporate mineral extraction, corporate food production, agrofuels, agro-industrial crops and other profit-driven ventures.


It was within this gathering that Josephine, a participant from Uganda, made a powerful declaration: “Africa can survive without capitalism.” Her words captured the political spirit of the school and the conviction shared by women whose everyday struggles challenge the destructive logic of capitalist development, especially through local solutions that have existed for centuries, such as agroforestry, artisanal fishing, intercropping, shifting cultivation, indigenous seed saving and sharing, community forest management, and peasant agroecology.


As those first and hardest hit by economic exploitation driven by profit-focused development projects, African women, continue to be at the forefront of building alternatives while remaining firmly at the centre of climate justice struggles today, even as they Face brutal oppression and violence,


Women’s Voices, Struggles and Aspirations


As the school started, the women described their challenges to the capitalist system, including constant confrontations with oil and mining corporations, local resistance to land, food and seed grabbing, and community actions against institutions of capitalist globalisation. They also shared their desire to transform the difficult struggles they wage constantly against capitalism and build a spirit of resilience and solidarity grounded in communal ownership, collective care, solidarity and respect.


Josephine, a participant from Uganda, shared with emotion and sensitivity that she hoped “to unite with other women to defend nature commons which brings peace to community. Which feeds the children and sends them to school”.


Priscilla, from Tanzania, another participant, said she hoped “

to build her knowledge around the good African culture and believe that united women together in the past in terms of communal land ownership and relationship”.


Centuries of mega-extraction have looted Africa’s land, forests, water and underground minerals, with a new wave of extraction driven by the energy transition, artificial intelligence and war. Governments continue to justify the destruction of these shared resources as development through mining projects, carbon markets and energy projects, while denying the rights of communities to say no and expropriating women’s labour without compensation.


Over five days, women told tales of exploitation and dispossession again and again, from so many different contexts: from women in farming communities whose health has been broken through endless hours of labour, toiling under harsh climate conditions; women in extractive communities condemned to the stress of perpetual insecurity and pollution; and members of communities evicted at gunpoint to make way for the next big capitalist venture on their land.


The Gendered Burdens of Extractive Capitalism


As capitalism continues to lurch from crisis to crisis, African women’s bodies continue to carry many of the burdens of the privatisation of The Commons, patriarchal modes of production, militarism and imperialism, as well as the ecological defence of the planet.


Women carry unpaid care work essential for communities to survive. The labour of care includes housework, preparing meals, caring for persons with disabilities, people who are ill or elderly family members, and birthing, raising and educating children. author: Reddebrek
title: Carl Steuermann (Otto Rühle) - La Crise Mondial (1931)
content:
Pour la quatrième fois, le capitalisme allemand annonce sa banqueroute. La première fois, celle-ci se montra sous l’uniforme des soldats vaincus, à leur retour du front. La guerre mondiale était perdue, le rêve de domination mondiale était cruellement brisé. Le peuple souffrait, en proie à la famine, à la misère, à l’épuisement, au désespoir, mais il ne voulut pas admettre la banqueroute de l’économie. Il renvoya le messager de Job et chanta : « L’Allemagne, l’Alle­ magne au-dessus de tout ! » La seconde annonce suivit de près la première. Celui qui la fit parla avec la voix de la révolution. En effet, l’armée effondrée, ce fut la révolution. « Socialisme ou chute dans la barbarie ! » tel fut le mot d’ordre. « Il n’est d’autre salut que l’orientation à l’Est, le sys­ tème des soviets, la dictature du prolétariat, la socia­ lisation ! » La terreur s’empara de la bourgeoisie et la paralysa. Sans y croire elle-même, secouée de tremble­ ments, elle put à peine articuler : « Reconstruction ! Nous nous relèverons ! » Vibrant d’enthousiasme et d’espoirs, l’écho des masses lui répondit : « Oui, recons­ truction !» Et la révolution fut réprimée dans le sang. La troisième fois, la banqueroute fut annoncée sur

les ruines de l’inflation. Il sembla que c’était réelle­ ment la fin. Des millions d’hommes devenus des men­ diants sombrèrent dans le néant d’une existence sans ressources. Mais avec le courage du désespoir ils se cramponnèrent au fétu de paille d’une dernière ten­ tative : « L’Allemagne ne peut pas, ne doit pas périr !... » Et voici que, pour la quatrième fois, on nous annonce la banqueroute, et c’cst le cri de détresse de l’économie mondiale qui nous en avertit. Les Bourses s’écroulent, les fondements de l’industrie branlent ; c’est une suite d’effondrements. La panique gagne de proche en proche. Plus de vingt millions d’hommes sont jetés à la rue, sans pain, et demandent du travail. La moitié du genre humain presque vit de secours publics. Partout dominent les dettes, la corruption, la fail­ lite... Une atmosphère de fin du monde. Qu’allons- nous devenir ? se demandent les uns aux autres les hommes perplexes et impuissants. « Cela ne peut pas continuer ainsi ! » assure la sagesse des rues. Nul ne sait quel conseil donner. Chacun sait seulement ou a le sentiment infaillible que, cette fois-ci, c’est sérieux ; c’est vraiment la faillite. Il n’y a plus ni aide, ni espoir à attendre. Le capitalisme a fait son temps. C’est la fin, en effet. Mais y a-t-il une fin sans recom­ mencement ? Un déclin sans renaissance ? L’histoire mondiale continue. Et tant qu’il y aura des hommes animés du désir de vivre, ces hommes travailleront, créeront, produiront pour se maintenir en vie. Ce n’est pas l’économie qui meurt, c’est le capitalisme ; c’est la forme économique dominante aujourd’hui en Amérique, en Europe, et dans les régions du monde les plus évoluées, qui est condamnée à mort. C’est la fin d’un système, non la fin de l’économie tout court.

La crise constitue un tournant. L’effondrement est suivi de renaissance ; du chaos s’élabore un ordre nouveau. Nous ignorons encore tout du rythme, du genre et de l’envergure des événements qui nous attendent. Nous ignorons la durée et les phases du processus par lequel nous devrons passer. Nous ne nous représentons pas encore les luttes que nous devrons soutenir, ni les sacrifices qu’une évolution implacable exigera de nous. Nous allons à tâtons dans l’inconnu. Une seule chose nous semble certaine : c’est que le grand système économique qui succédera nécessaire­ ment au capitalisme sera le socialisme. Il est vrai que la route est longue qui mène vers lui. C’est vraisem­ blablement une route pénible, ardue, semée d’obstacles et comportant beaucoup d’arrêts et de paliers, beau­ coup d’étapes et de haltes intermédiaires. Si les signes ne sont pas trompeurs, l’étape pro­ chaine de cette transformation de l’humanité est une variété du capitalisme d’État. L’histoire qui nous emporte dans son tourbillon met le cap dans cette direction. Suivons-la !

author: La Zarzamora
title: Comunicado Público de pu weichafe que siguen defendiendo la Mapu
content:
Damos a conocer un pensamiento, un actuar de individuos personas convencidas, comprometidas en las luchas dignas de zonas, territorios a lo largo de esta franja de tierra que denominaron Chile.

Queremos hacer un llamado a todas las personas, agrupaciones, comunidades, hogares, a los familiares de los presos políticos, a los que defienden la naturaleza, la ñuke mapu, contra este gobierno y sistema fascista, que solamente busca conseguir sus propios objetivos y privilegios sin importar el daño que hacen en general.

También enviamos este mensaje por la preocupación que tenemos hacia los territorios que están amenazados por la destrucción del monstruo capitalista, que no se cansa de destruir los espacios naturales y espacios donde viven personas que habitan en armonía con su entorno.

Desde acá decimos que avanzaremos hacia la unidad de los distintos pensamientos de lucha y métodos, que aplican y desarrollan un caminar de esfuerzo y sacrificio para llegar a vivir en una sociedad digna y autónoma. No nos canzaremos de organizar para pelerarle a estas bestias hambrientas del poder económico (de la elite nacional e internacional), porque estamos convecidos que podemos avanzar hacia una liberación en el Wall Mapu, una lucha de siglo en siglo, que resiste y se reconstruye año a año, década tras década.

Somos parte de un movimiento que ha optado por la lucha de autodefensa, la lucha armada legítima y ancestral, continuando el caminar con los costos que sean necesarios. Sabemos que el sabotaje y los ataques a sus infraestructuras, los debilita, los preocupa, les duele ser tocados por personas que entregan sus vidas por el camino que eligen, preparándose y articulándose para encontrar nuevos objetivos, como lo son quienes colaboran con el enemigo y venden sus almas al capitalismo.

Entregamos nuestra voluntad a los procesos que nos preparan para no equivocarnos, para no caer en sus garras, que aprietan y no sueltan fácilmente.

Debemos tener mucho cuidado, ellos están modificando y preparando sus leyes para hacer temer a la gente que lucha, aunque sabemos que ni eso frenará nuestro avance, ya que la unidad es más fuerte y hermosa a la vez. Contamos con experiencia, la que compartiremos y entregaremos en su momento a las nuevas generaciones.

A las personas que que quieren luchar les damos ánimo, sigan estudiando lo que sea para aportar a una fuerza futura, que destruya toda expresión capitalista.

Ejemplo de ello ha sido la franja Lafkenche, la zona de Malleco y otros territorios en donde sus weichafes tomaron las armas para defenderse del avance del monopolio capitalista, forestales de Angelini, Matte y el latifundio.

Ante esto, el estado vió con preocupación como perdían el territorio que nos usurparon, por lo que decidió nuevamente realizar un avance militar para obtener el control absoluto. Pero esto no nos asusta, ya que sabemos que en algún momento se le dará frente y este retrocederá, tal como lo han hecho anteriormente en lugares donde estuvieron instalados y fueron expulsados por la fuerza de la gente que decide luchar.

Hoy encarcelan a personas de estos territorios, a personas que han participado de la lucha por la tierra y todo lo que esto conlleva.

En el caso conocido como “Caso Grollmus” ocurrido el año 2022, detuvieron a varios integrantes de comunidades mapuche lavkenche y les condenaron en su conjunto a mas de 1000 años de prisión, en un hecho de racismo histórico sin antecedentes. Sabemos que no hay pruebas materiales, que se basan en relatos de testigos protegidos y que tienen presa a gente totalmente inocente. Esperamos su pronta libertad.

Sabemos también que la justicia está condenando al mapuche por luchar y a todos los que deciden enfrentar al gran capital; a los poderosos les decimos que tengan mucho cuidado porque nos levantaremos con mas odio y venganza hacia su sistema represivo, tanto dentro como fuera de las diferentes cárceles chilenas, en donde nuestros hermanos mapuche y de lucha, se mantienen custodiados por gendarmería.

A los funcionarios de gendarmería les decimos: No se equivoquen con nuestros presos comuneros mapuche, compañeros anarquistas, subversivos y comunistas reales. A todos les tenemos inmenso cariño y respeto por sus trayectorias. Reaccionaremos, cobraremos a altos y bajos mandos por sus decisiones. Nos dejaremos caer en sus casas, porque contamos con información de ellos.

Que estas palabras lleguen al CP Biobío, El Manzano, Temuco, Angol, Valdivia y Santiago.

Algunos actos …

author: Unknown
title: Russell Means - Revolution and American Indians: “Marxism is as Alien to My Culture as Capitalism”
content:
Author

: Russell Means

Title

: Revolution and American Indians: “Marxism is as Alien to My Culture as Capitalism”

Date

: July, 1980

Source

: https://www.filmsforaction.org/news/revolution-and-american-indians-marxism-is-as-alien-to-my-culture-as-capitalism/


The following speech was given by Russell Means in July 1980

, before several thousand people who had assembled from all over the world for the Black Hills International Survival Gathering, in the Black Hills of South Dakota. It is Russell Means's most famous speech.*


A member of the Oglala Lakota tribe, he was perhaps the most outsized personality in the American Indian Movement, beginning with the 1973 occupation of Wounded Knee. He also had an acting career beginning with his role as Chingachgook in Last of the Mohicans. He passed away Oct 22nd, 2012 at the age 72.


 The only possible opening for a statement of this kind is that I detest writing. The process itself epitomizes the European concept of "legitimate" thinking; what is written has an importance that is denied the spoken. My culture, the Lakota culture, has an oral tradition, so I ordinarily reject writing. It is one of the white world's ways of destroying the cultures of non-European peoples, the imposing of an abstraction over the spoken relationship of a people.


 So what you read here is not what I've written. It's what I've said and someone else has written down. I will allow this because it seems that the only way to communicate with the white world is through the dead, dry leaves of a book. I don't really care whether my words reach whites or not. They have already demonstrated through their history that they cannot hear, cannot see; they can only read (of course, there are exceptions, but the exceptions only prove the rule). I'm more concerned with American Indian people, students and others, who have begun to be absorbed into the white world through universities and other institutions. But even then it's a marginal sort of concern. It's very possible to grow into a red face with a white mind; and if that's a person's individual choice, so be it, but I have no use for them. This is part of the process of cultural genocide being waged by Europeans against American Indian peoples' today. My concern is with those American Indians who choose to resist this genocide, but who may be confused as to how to proceed.


 (You notice I use the term American Indian rather than Native American or Native indigenous people or Amerindian when referring to my people. There has been some controversy about such terms, and frankly, at this point, I find it absurd. Primarily it seems that American Indian is being rejected as European in origin--which is true. But all the above terms are European in origin; the only non-European way is to speak of Lakota--or, more precisely, of Oglala, Brule, etc.--and of the Dineh, the Miccousukee, and all the rest of the several hundred correct tribal names.


 (There is also some confusion about the word Indian, a mistaken belief that it refers somehow to the country, India. When Columbus washed up on the beach in the Caribbean, he was not looking for a country called India. Europeans were calling that country Hindustan in 1492. Look it up on the old maps. Columbus called the tribal people he met "Indio," from the Italian in dio, meaning "in God.")


 It takes a strong effort on the part of each American Indian not to become Europeanized. The strength for this effort can only come from the traditional ways, the traditional values that our elders retain. It must come from the hoop, the four directions, the relations: it cannot come from the pages of a book or a thousand books. No European can ever teach a Lakota to be Lakota, a Hopi to be Hopi. A master's degree in "Indian Studies" or in "education" or in anything else cannot make a person into a human being or provide knowledge into traditional ways. It can only make you into a mental European, an outsider.


 I should be clear about something here, because there seems to be some confusion about it. When I speak of Europeans or mental Europeans, I'm not allowing for false distinctions. I'm not saying that on the one hand there are the by-products of a few thousand years of genocidal, reactionary, European intellectual development which is bad; and on the other hand there is some new revolutionary intellectual development which is good. I'm referring here to the so-called theories of Marxism and anarchism and …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Fiyi: El niño, la crisis hídrica y el negocio millonario del agua
content:
Fiyi está siendo golpeada por una gran sequía asociada al fenómeno de El Niño y vuelve a poner en emergencia a miles de ciudadanos de este archipiélago del Pacífico. Pero mientras 6 de cada 10 habitantes no tienen acceso al agua potable, la empresa Fiji Water explota una fuente subterránea de aguas, considerada entre las más puras del mundo. El objetivo: abastecer mercados internacionales.


Por Adrián Flores para Red Eco


Este conjunto de Islas suelen aparecer en las postales turísticas como un paraíso de playas y aguas transparentes. Sin embargo, lejos de esa imagen, miles de personas atraviesan una situación muy diferente: conseguir agua segura se ha convertido en un problema cotidiano.


La sequía que afecta al archipiélago, está llevando al límite al precario sistema de abastecimiento. Los datos permiten ver la magnitud el problema. Según UNICEF y la Organización Mundial de la Salud, en 2022 solamente el 42 % de la población de Fiyi tenía acceso a servicios de agua potable gestionados de manera segura. Esto significa que casi seis de cada diez habitantes no alcanzaban ese estándar. Aunque una proporción mucho mayor contaba con algún servicio básico, eso no necesariamente garantizaba agua segura y sin contaminación.


Los informes difundidos durante noviembre muestran la gravedad del actual escenario. El periódico The Fiji Times, publicó el 1 de noviembre que 19 de las 44 fuentes de abastecimiento monitoreadas por la Autoridad del Agua de Fiyi se encontraban en niveles críticos.


El Gobierno realiza operativos de emergencia con camiones, plantas de tratamiento y embarcaciones para abastecer a las comunidades insulares. Los pronósticos tampoco son alentadores: si continúa la falta de lluvias, hasta el 82 % de las fuentes monitoreadas podría alcanzar niveles críticos.


La crisis ya golpea la salud. En la isla de Batiki se registró un aumento de casos de diarrea que motivó la intervención del Ministerio de Salud. Los productores agrícolas enfrentan pérdidas de cultivos y dificultades para mantener el ganado.


La crisis climática golpea sobre una estructura que no estaba preparada para responder. Y mientras miles de familias dependen de operativos de emergencia para acceder al agua, en el mismo territorio funciona una industria que convirtió ese recurso en un producto de exportación.


Fiji Water, el gran exportador de agua para las élites del mundo


En el valle de Yaqara, sobre la isla de Viti Levu, se encuentra la planta de Fiji Water. Desde allí se extrae agua que luego es embotellada y comercializada en distintos países.


La empresa pertenece a The Wonderful. Su negocio se construyó alrededor de una característica que funciona como argumento comercial: el origen natural del agua y su procedencia de un acuífero de Fiyi.


No hay elementos para atribuirle a Fiji Water la responsabilidad directa por toda la crisis hídrica del país. Los problemas de infraestructura, la desigualdad en el abastecimiento y las condiciones climáticas tienen una historia propia. Pero resulta inevitable preguntarse por las prioridades que establece el modelo capitalista donde una actividad industrial puede expandirse para abastecer mercados internacionales mientras una parte de la población sigue sin contar con agua segura.


Desfinanciamiento mas sequía


Las dificultades del sistema público no se explican únicamente por la sequía. Según datos del Departamento de Comercio de Estados Unidos, alrededor del 47 % del agua se pierde por filtraciones en las redes de distribución antes de llegar a los hogares, en un país donde miles de personas padecen interrupciones del servicio.


En este contexto, la información sobre las regalías de Fiji Water resulta particularmente significativa. La empresa matriz declaró en 2025 que sus operaciones en Fiyi, junto con las de su compañía hermana de transporte marítimo, aportaban anualmente en regalías al Estado, el equivalente a unos 43 millones de dólares estadounidenses. Esto representa un tercio de lo que el Estado destina al mantenimiento de la red pública de agua.


La comparación permite observar – y no de manera caprichosa – que el negocio privado aprovecha un recurso natural del territorio y obtiene ingresos de su comercialización internacional de centenares de millones (aproximadamente 500 millones de dólares en el 2023) mientras que paga regalías en una suma que ni siquiera sirve para mantener la precaria red de distribución.

author: Unknown
title: Socialist Strategy within the Architecture of Power
content:
The artwork in this dossier, produced by Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research, depicts three forms of power: social power in magenta, governmental power in yellow, and systemic power in cyan. Where these forms overlap, new colours emerge, representing their different configurations and interconnections within a broader architecture of power. This composition invites us to consider how power is organised, contested, and transformed through processes of emancipation.


When a radical government takes office with a mandate for transformation, the next morning it will have to confront banks that remain in private hands, mines under corporate control, private mainstream media, and public administration governed by inherited procedures. Capital can postpone investment, transfer money abroad, close factories, hoard essential goods, dismiss workers, and speculate against the currency. The havoc wrought on the economy and population can then be presented as proof that transformation is impossible, all while the government is held responsible for a crisis produced or intensified by forces beyond its control.


This reality reveals a central problem for socialist strategy. Taking governmental office can be an important step toward systemic transformation, but misunderstanding these two forms of power as one and the same can have dangerous consequences. A clear analysis of where power resides and how its different forms interact is necessary to avoid patterns that have plagued revolutionary processes across the world.


An electoral victory may be mistaken for a revolutionary event when a left-wing party has taken office even though the wider state apparatus, the economy, and the institutions that shape common sense remain largely beyond its control. Conversely, a socialist movement may possess considerable social strength without being able to translate that strength into governmental authority or changes to the structures of the state and economy.  The ruling class exercises power through its control over production and the structures that reinforce it, while the working class exercises collective power through strikes, demonstrations, and the organisations it builds through struggle. To use a single word – power – for all these different capacities can confuse political strategy. In this dossier, we therefore distinguish three related forms of power as an analytical framework for debate and discussion:


Social power

 is the organised capacity of a class or political bloc to act collectively, reproduce material life, and contest the ruling class’s command over society. It is built through institutions of struggle and cooperation such as trade unions, peasant and women’s organisations, cooperatives, community structures, cultural and media projects, political education, and political parties. Through these institutions, a class or political bloc can struggle to reshape common sense and establish moral and intellectual leadership.


Governmental power

 is the capacity to assume governmental authority, whether through elections, insurrection, or another political rupture, and to use executive, legislative, and administrative institutions to pursue a programme. It provides access to important instruments of administration and policy but does not, by itself, amount to control of the state or the wider system.


Systemic power

 is the capacity to transform the class character and institutional form of the state, bring the major means of production and the social surplus under democratic authority, and reorganise the relations through which society reproduces itself. It includes state power but cannot be reduced to it because capitalist social relations are reproduced beyond the formal institutions of the state – through property, finance, the world market, colonial relations, culture, and social reproduction – and many of these relations exceed the reach of any single government or national state.


These forms are analytical distinctions, not sealed compartments, and do not constitute a fixed sequence. They overlap, develop unevenly, and can pull in opposite directions. Governmental power may become a bridge between organised social power and systemic transformation. It may also weaken popular organisation and reconcile it to the existing system. The central strategic question is therefore not which form of power matters but how the three can be connected in a process of emancipation.


Social Power

author: Freedom Editor
title: To remember Durruti: “Solidarity is the best incentive”
content:
Ninety years since the death of Buenaventura Durruti, the greatest military leader of the Spanish Revolution

Born into the working class on 14 July 1896 in Leon, Buenaventura Durruti became a mechanic by trade and a prominent local union organiser of the socialist Unión General de Trabajadores (UGT, General Union of Workers). Expelled from UGT after the August 1917 general strike for his militancy, he left Leon and joined the mass anarcho-syndicalist union, the Confederación Nacional del Trabajo (CNT, National Confederation of Labour), and became an anarchist. He soon became a leading activist within the movement, playing a key role in the resistance to Franco’s coup of July 1936 and the subsequent social revolution.

The Trotskyist Felix Morrow proclaimed in his Revolution and Counter-Revolution in Spain that Durruti was “the greatest military figure produced by the war” while, of course, dismissing anarchism by suggesting he was “no theoretician, but an activist leader of masses… his words express the revolutionary outlook of the class-conscious workers”. This ignores that Durruti’s words, activity, and outlook did not spring out of thin air but rather were informed by and reflected his anarchist politics, history, activity, and vision—which in turn reflected his experiences and needs as a member of the CNT and the working class.

While undoubtedly remembered as a man of action, indeed his exploits across Spain, Europe and South America are legendary, Durruti read anarchist literature and press, took part in the debates within the Spanish anarchist movement, and was a noted public speaker. However, it is for his role in the Spanish Revolution and Civil War that he is best remembered.

When the military did revolt on 17 July 1936, Durruti took a leading part in organising the resistance in Barcelona amongst the various CNT unions and defence committees. A general strike was called, weapons seized, and 19 July saw the army defeated by the people armed.

The long desired social revolution swept the city and other parts of free Spain – as anarchists had long argued, workers seized the workplaces, peasants the land, popular assemblies and revolutionary committees were formed. The collectivised economy benefited all rather than the owning class, while also providing weaponry to the militias (with workplaces refashioned to do so). Non-economic social relationships likewise began to transform, and anarchist women organised the Mujeres Libres to empower women and fight the sexism that permeated Spanish society and, sadly, the anarchist movement.

Anarchist theory, which had always argued that a social revolution could only be defended by the people armed, was also applied when the CNT organised militias to liberate those areas of Spain under military control. Other unions and parties did likewise, although unlike those the CNT militias were run by their members with elected officers and committees, all sharing the same living conditions. As Durruti argued:

“I don’t believe – and everything happening around us confirms this – that you can run a workers’ militia according to classic military rules. I believe that discipline, co-ordination, and planning are indispensable, but we shouldn’t define them in terms taken from the world that we’re destroying. We have to build on new foundations. My comrades and I are convinced that solidarity is the best incentive for arousing an individual’s sense of responsibility and a willingness to accept discipline as an act of self-discipline.”

As the Durruti column marched towards Zaragoza, liberated villages and towns started the process of transforming society and the economy by forming collectives. These voluntary groups turned the land, machinery and other resources into common property, to be managed, worked, and benefited from by all rather than a few landlords or capitalists. For Durruti, the war and the revolution were inseparable:

“Our comrades on the front know for whom and for what they fight. They feel themselves revolutionaries and they fight, not in defence of more or less promised new laws, but for the conquest of the world, of the factories, the workshops, the means of transportation, their bread and the new culture.”

With the Republican government preferring to arm the rearguard (against the revolution) over the CNT militias, the Aragon Front stagnated. Yet the CNT militias were recognised as being the best fighters, as shown by part of the Durruti being sent to Madrid …

author: Unknown
title: Рассказ анархистки-трансдевушки, сбежавшей после вербовки ФСБ
content:
Это статья Ивана Асташина, вышедшая в октябре в The Insider.

Примечание редакции avtonom.org: Мы не рекомендуем подписывать какие-либо соглашения с силовиками, но считаем, что всегда следует действовать по обстоятельствам и допустимо спасать себя, если это можно сделать без причинения вреда окружающим.

В январе 2025 года сотрудники ФСБ пришли с обыском к 18-летней трансдевушке из Тюмени, нашли в ее телефоне переписку с «Боевой организацией анархо-коммунистов» (БОАК) и стали угрожать ей уголовным делом и многолетним сроком. Под давлением она согласилась на сотрудничество. Силовики поручили ей знакомиться с ЛГБТК-людьми, входить к ним в доверие и пытаться получить компрометирующую информацию. В разговоре с The Insider она рассказала, как выглядит вербовка, как ей удалось обмануть ФСБ и покинуть страну без связей, денег и загранпаспорта.

15 января 2025 года я проснулась от того, что на меня орет и дергает за плечо человек в маске. Я тогда жила у родителей, они открыли дверь сотрудникам ФСБ. Те пришли с ордером от прокурора и почему-то сказали, что ищут СВУ.

Мне толком никаких бумаг не дали рассмотреть: ордером помахали перед лицом и сразу убрали. Дома были два следователя, понятые и еще один фсб-шник в балаклаве и бронежилете. Изъяли компьютер, телефон и переносную камеру.

Когда я отказалась разблокировать телефон, фсб-шник в маске несколько раз ударил меня по спине. Бил и спрашивал: «Кашлять хочешь?» Я говорю: «Нет». Он снова бьет.

Потом мне натянули шапку на лицо, вывели в подъезд, посадили в машину и отвезли в городское управление ФСБ на Советской, 40. Это было часов в шесть утра. Там меня подняли на третий или четвертый этаж и почти до вечера опрашивали.

Здание ФСБ на Советской, 40 в Тюмени, URA.RU

Сначала спрашивали, не хочу ли я сама им что-нибудь рассказать. Потом унесли телефон в другой кабинет, а минут через пятнадцать принесли обратно — все пароли уже были сбиты.

Следователей было двое, причем они максимально тупо разыгрывали «злого» и «доброго». Один орал, угрожал и смотрел, что у меня в телефоне. Второй задавал вопросы по тому, что ему говорил первый о содержимом моего телефона.

Я решила: раз доступ к телефону у них все равно уже есть, то все, что они могут там найти о деятельности нашей инициативы, я возьму на себя. Сказала, что листовки клеила одна, граффити рисовала тоже одна.

Граффити, сделанных героиней материала с единомышленниками, Тюмень, август 2024 года

А потом вспомнила, что кое-что не успела удалить. Но было уже поздно: они нашли переписку с БОАК — Боевой организацией анархо-коммунистов. Мы переписывались по электронной почте. Там обсуждались инструкции по анонимным звонкам и то, как налаживать товарищеские контакты для инициативы. В одном из писем еще упоминалась «тачка фашистов».

Именно эту переписку они потом назвали основанием для дела об «обучении террористической деятельности». Когда они ее нашли, то сразу заулыбались и сказали: «Ну все, теперь тебе точно п***ец».

При этом они продолжали искать. Кроме фотографий листовок, моего маленького канала левой направленности человек на 30 и этой переписки, особо ничего не нашли. Пытались добиться, чтобы я призналась в чем-нибудь помимо листовок, граффити и переписки с БОАК.

Например, они почему-то считали, что я собиралась устроить акцию против главаря тюменской «Русской общины», направленную против его автомобиля. Я сказала, что максимум речь шла о том, чтобы порезать шины, а потом я вообще от этой идеи отказалась — вот машина и стоит целая.

Откуда силовики могли получить информацию

В самом управлении меня уже не били, там было в основном психологическое давление и неудобные условия. Например, я сидела не на стуле, а на системном блоке от своего компьютера. Они показывали на сейф в углу кабинета и рассказывали, что запихивают туда людей. Говорили, что одного человека якобы продержали там три дня и вообще не выпускали.

Они показывали на сейф в углу кабинета и рассказывали, что запихивают туда людей

Еще сказали, что если бы поймали меня не в Тюмени, а на оккупированных после полномасштабного вторжения территориях Украины, то вообще убили бы. Тот, который играл «злого», угрожал бросить меня в камеру, где меня будут насиловать пять человек.

Где-то к вечеру меня отвезли обратно домой и, можно сказать, передали отцу с рук на руки. Никаких документов опять не выдали. Формально никакого домашнего ареста не было, но устно сказали: из квартиры никуда не выходить, иначе меня заберут в СИЗО.

Телефон, компьютер и камера остались у них …

author: Thunderbird
title: Will anarchist book fairs remain safe spaces for anarchists?
content:
The context of the incident at the anarchist book fair in Brno (so-called Czech Republic).


Author


pocketedition.nublogs.org


    Submitted by

Thunderbird

 on November 23, 2026


On October 3, 2026, at the Anarchist Book Fair in Brno

1


, a person collaborating with Pocket Edition

2


 was subjected to aggressive behavior by a member of the Brno-based AFA group and several other individuals. It was clear from the aggressors’ statements that their intention was to physically assault the person in question, intimidate them, and force them to leave the book fair. Similar incidents have also occurred in the past at a concert at Club 007

3


 and at the Book Fair in Prague

4


. In our view, therefore, this is not an isolated incident, but a deeper and long-standing problem that cannot be dismissed as a trivial dispute.


We cannot expect the responsibility for resolving this problem to fall solely on the direct participants in these dramatic situations or on the groups that organize the events where such incidents occurred. Although the prompt and empathetic response of the Brno Book Fair’s organizing team helped mitigate the effects of the aggression this time and ensure that the victim had a safe haven from the aggressors, we believe that a comprehensive solution to this problem must also include, in the future, the active participation of the public attending book fairs and the entire anarchist movement, which presents such events as a significant part of its own safety infrastructure. Therefore, this statement is a public call to action, not a message addressed only to a narrow circle of specific individuals.


Brief Description of the Conflict at the Anarchist Book Fair in Brno


The person who was attacked at the book fair in Brno was helping to handle technical matters at the Pocket Edition booth. The organizing team had provided this project with a space to display its publications, and it was listed on the website among the participants and distributors. In the early evening, in the courtyard, a person associated with AFA very rudely and literally ordered the person in question to leave the book fair, claiming he had no business being there. It was evident from his verbal remarks and “body language” that he was determined to escalate his behavior to physical aggression. However, other people present prevented the physical assault.


The person who was attacked responded with a loud statement: “You’re invading my personal space, and I feel threatened. Back off and stop communicating with me aggressively.” The aggressor replied, “I don’t give a damn about your personal space.” This was followed by further verbal aggression and an attempt to physically attack the victim who then moved from the courtyard inside the building to the Pocket Edition distribution table. The aggressor immediately followed them, along with several slightly less aggressive individuals. The most active aggressor continued to intimidate and threaten physical assault. Together with the others, he justified his behavior with speculative accusations that we’ve heard before, but we don’t know of anyone who has helped clarify what happened and/or who initiated it.


“Police officers” without uniforms and “judges” without robes


Accusing and punishing someone based on speculation presented as fact is a despicable practice we know all too well from the police, prosecutors, and judges. However, the so-called anarchists and anti-fascists mentioned here take this practice to an even more extreme level. Unlike our institutional enemies, they do not rely on expert analyses or forensic science, nor do they seek factual evidence to clarify events. It is enough for them if someone says, “That person placed a fake explosive at the festival” or “This person sent a threatening message to someone online under a false name.” All it takes is to say such things, and the “court case” is immediately closed without anyone having to prove anything concrete. The person against whom the accusation is made is immediately deemed guilty and ready for punishment. Hi can then be unhesitatingly intimidated, beaten, stigmatized, slandered, ostracized, and expelled from public events… Everything is permissible because these “police officers” without uniforms and “judges” without robes are not bound by any rules, only by the “law of the strongest” and the “power of the loudest.” However, their power comes not only from physical prowess accompanied by terrifying …
