author: Marx-lover
title: The ELF and Eco-Activism
content:
This is a review of a book by the journalist Matthew Wolfe entitled Fires in the Night: The Earth Liberation Front, the FBI, and a Secret History of Eco-Sabotage, published in 2026. It's a good book!

Increasingly, it seems like it’s only a matter of time before civilization collapses. It might happen because of nuclear war, but the more likely cause is ecological chaos. Carbon emissions continue to rise and global warming is accelerating; the destruction of ecosystems, from forests to marine environments, is accelerating; countless species of animals and plants are going extinct every year because of human activity. A century from now, when the climate is much warmer than today and nature even more severely degraded, billions of people may be dying from floods, famines, scorching temperatures, lack of access to water, wars over natural resources, the collapse of urban infrastructure, and other catastrophes.

The global ruling class is doing little else but working to hasten the apocalypse, for example by expanding the use of fossil fuels and maniacally investing in data center construction. All the pleading of scientists, activists, and the general public that politicians take decisive action against global warming has availed little. The question “What is to be done?” has never, in all of history, been more urgent.

In his new book Fires in the Night, the journalist Matthew Wolfe narrates the history of a group of people in the 1990s and early 2000s who gave a bold answer to that question: the only kind of action that can meet the moment is eco-sabotage. Arson was their favorite method. The protection of animals was one of their major interests, so in addition to burning, say, car dealerships that sold gas-guzzling SUVs, they also targeted slaughterhouses, lumber companies, a large ski resort that was planning to expand into an old-growth forest, the university office of a biologist who was thought to be researching genetic engineering, and even Forest Ranger stations that were seen as complicit in timber sales. The FBI branded these people the country’s foremost domestic terrorism threat, and by 2007 most of them were in prison.

Wolfe’s book is of interest not only because it is based on incredibly meticulous research that makes it possible for Wolfe to tell the personal stories and motives of the core of activists who constituted the Earth Liberation Front (ELF)—or rather its most active cell, in Eugene, Oregon—as well as the stories of some of the federal officials and police officers whom they eluded for years. It’s a gripping and suspenseful tale, told without bias. But equally importantly, the book raises the same questions that, in a different way, Andreas Malm’s How to Blow Up a Pipeline raised in 2021: is economic sabotage in defense of the environment justified, and if so, what forms of sabotage and under what circumstances? Wolfe doesn’t answer these questions, but the history he relates demands they be taken seriously. It isn’t hard to argue that the ELF’s actions were misguided and accomplished little or nothing, but neither is it hard to argue that some kinds of eco-sabotage are defensible or even imperative.

Most readers, in any event, could probably empathize with the ELF activists (“Elves”) and even respect them for putting their lives on the line and for strictly adhering to their principles. They were always very careful to ensure that no animals or humans would be harmed by their property destruction—although it’s true that risks and uncertainty are inevitable in cases of arson. The Elves were young and idealistic, mere teenagers and twenty-somethings who met each other through the anarchist and radical environmentalist circles in Eugene. They had heard of something called the Earth Liberation Front in the UK and Europe, a decentralized, leaderless network of “cells” of anonymous eco-saboteurs, and in 1996 a few of them decided to start a new cell in the U.S. For the next five years, a dozen or so people would be behind most of the ELF incidents that the government and mass media dubbed “ecoterrorism”—despite the fact that not a single person was ever killed or injured.

Given their youth and relative inexperience, the Elves’ achievements were impressive. Always acting at night, deploying rather sophisticated incendiary devices they had built themselves, they caused over $100 million in property damage. In 1998, a single young man—known to his comrades only as “Avalon”—was able to burn down …

author: L214
title: Budget 2027 : ce que les députés ont décidé pour les animaux
content:
Dernier budget de l’État avant la présidentielle, le projet de loi de finances pour 2027 est une occasion décisive de réorienter l’argent public vers un autre modèle agricole. Quel est le bilan des débats parlementaires et des décisions gouvernementales pour les animaux ?

Depuis le 13 octobre, l’Assemblée nationale a examiné en séance publique le projet de loi de finances pour 2027. Dans un contexte marqué par les canicules, les sécheresses et les incendies de l’été, le Gouvernement a annoncé plus d’un milliard d’euros pour « relancer la production agricole ». Face au dernier budget avant la présidentielle, les députés avaient un choix à faire : continuer à financer le modèle intensif ou investir dans une agriculture qui nous protège, nous et les autres animaux.

Avec Le Sauvetage du siècle, L214 défend des mesures concrètes pour atteindre la réduction de moitié du nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030 : aider les éleveurs volontaires à sortir de l’élevage intensif ou de la pêche, développer les cultures végétales pour nous nourrir, taxer la publicité pour les produits animaux, ou encore soutenir les cantines pour qu’elles proposent une plus grande offre végétale.

Pourtant la quasi-totalité de ces propositions a été rejetée :

L’amendement I-3588 (Marianne Maximi, LFI) visant à réserver le suramortissement fiscal des projets d’avenir agricole aux élevages avec accès au plein air, rejeté par 50 voix contre 14,

L’amendement I-3467 (Anne Stambach-Terrenoir, LFI) cherchant à exclure du crédit d’impôt recherche les dépenses visant à intensifier les productions animales, rejeté par 101 voix contre 53,

L’amendement I-295 (Claire Lejeune, LFI) proposant de porter à 35 % l’impôt sur les sociétés pour les élevages intensifs soumis à autorisation, rejeté par 60 voix contre 27.

Un seul amendement favorable aux animaux a été adopté : l’amendement I-2017 de Romain Courbon (Socialistes), travaillé avec l’association QUATRE PATTES, qui crée un crédit d’impôt de 25 % pour les investissements favorisant la sortie des cages, l’accès au plein air et la réduction des densités. Il a été adopté par 10 voix contre 7.

Les débats ont aussi révélé la difficulté d’aborder sereinement la question de notre consommation de viande. Lors de l’examen du budget de la Sécurité sociale, Sandrine Rousseau (Écologiste et social) a défendu une taxe sur la viande ultra-transformée. Cette mesure a été qualifiée par Laurent Jacobelli (Rassemblement national) d’ « amendement le plus risible », malgré les impératifs pour les animaux, la santé publique et la transition écologique. L’amendement a été rejeté par 84 voix contre 14.

Le projet de loi de finances ayant finalement été rejeté par l’Assemblée nationale, aucun de ces amendements ne figurera dans le texte, en cours d’examen par le Sénat. La seconde partie du budget, consacrée aux dépenses, n’a pas pu être débattue à l’Assemblée. Encore une fois, les intérêts des animaux sont largement ignorés.

Pour la cinquième année consécutive, des députés ont tenté de s’attaquer aux associations qui révèlent les conditions d’élevage, de transport et d’abattage des animaux. Leur méthode : supprimer les réductions d’impôt sur les dons qui leur sont faits. Autrement dit, sanctionner les donateurs des associations pour entraver leur travail d’information.

Heureusement, tous les amendements examinés à l’Assemblée nationale ont été rejetés :

L’amendement I-1603 (Stéphanie Galzy, RN) : suppression de la réduction d’impôt pour les dons à une association condamnée pour intrusion, violation de domicile ou entrave à l’activité économique, rejeté le 15 octobre par 68 voix contre 58,

L’amendement I-1798 (Kévin Mauvieux, RN) : retrait de la réduction d’impôt pour toute association condamnée définitivement, quel qu’en soit le motif, rejeté le 15 octobre par 50 voix contre 44,

L’amendement I-357 (Corentin Le Fur, DR) : extension des infractions entraînant la perte des avantages fiscaux, rejeté le 16 octobre par 49 voix contre 38,

L’amendement I-1280 (Christelle d’Intorni, UDR) : même extension, élargie aux délits de presse, dont la diffamation, rejeté le 16 octobre par 47 voix contre 37.

D’autres amendements de même nature ont été retirés ou n’ont pas été défendus en séance. Un amendement de protection proposé par Romain Courbon (Socialistes), qui visait à interdire toute restriction de la réduction d’impôt pour des motifs portant atteinte à la liberté associative, a en revanche été rejeté par 58 voix contre 36 (scrutin n° …

title: Animal Rising Disrupts National Pig Awards in Central London Following Campaigner Arrests
content:
Animal Rising campaigners disrupted the National Pig Awards at the Royal Lancaster Hotel in central London this evening (16 November), while protesters outside blocked the main entrance. Police were called to the venue.

Despite enhanced security, six campaigners reached the event and were subsequently apprehended before being ejected from the hotel at approximately 7 pm. Around 70 protesters gathered outside as attendees arrived, holding placards reading “Free Luna” and “End Factory Farming”.

The group publicly declared its intention to shut down the awards last week, calling for Red Court, a pig factory farm in Suffolk, to release Luna, a mother pig whose life of confinement was filmed continuously for over a month by Animal Rising earlier this year. [1]

The investigation documented squalid conditions and illegal piglet thumping on the Red Tractor Assured farm. [2] Over 40,000 people have since signed a petition calling for Luna’s release to a sanctuary. [3]

The group filmed Luna confined in a narrow farrowing crate for five weeks, unable to turn around or take more than a step forward. A sanctuary has since offered her a home for the rest of her life. [4]

Red Court confirmed last week that Luna is once again in a farrowing crate. If the farm refuses to release her, she will remain there for approximately another month, confined with her newborn piglets, before she is removed and re-inseminated.

The farm has also rejected a proposed £5,000 donation to You Are Not Alone, an East Anglian charity supporting farmers’ mental health, in exchange for Luna’s release. [5]

Earlier today, Animal Rising announced that a third campaigner, Michelle Farnham, had been arrested on suspicion of burglary following the open rescue of three piglets (Leila, Nova and Maia) from Red Court.

Before the rescue, Animal Rising reported serious welfare concerns at the farm to the police, RSPCA and Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA).

APHA, the body responsible for enforcing farmed animal welfare, informed Animal Rising that the farm’s conditions, including the illegal thumping of a piglet, were normal.

Farnham attended Stoke Newington Police Station at 10 am this morning. Her fellow rescuers, Thomas Cusick and Liam Shaughnessy, had previously reported themselves to the police and been arrested. [6]

Farnham, 26, Animal Rising’s Campaign Lead, attracted national attention in September when she spent 21 days and nights locked in a farrowing crate in Trafalgar Square, highlighting Luna’s story and the suffering of animals in factory farms. High-profile visitors included Chris Packham and Green MP Adrian Ramsay. [7]

Animal Rising is campaigning for a government commitment to end UK factory farming by 2040.

author: Tobias Schalyo
title: PETA x Adventsome – vegane Adventskalender: Infos zur Verlosung und die Gründer:innen im Interview
content:
Werbung | Die

Weihnachtszeit

 rückt näher und mit ihr die Vorfreude auf kleine tägliche Überraschungen. Gemeinsam mit Adventsome verlosen wir von PETA Deutschland daher drei vegane Adventskalender voller

pflanzlicher Snacks

 und Infos zur Unterstützung gemeinnütziger Projekte. Der vegane Adventskalender zeigt, wie vielfältig, lecker und kreativ die Weihnachtszeit sein kann – mit vielen rein veganen Überraschungen. 


Über unsere Social-Media-Kanäle verlosen wir insgesamt drei vegane Adventskalender von Adventsome im Wert von jeweils 149 Euro. Mit etwas Glück können Sie sich oder Ihren Liebsten eine ganz besondere tierfreundliche Vorweihnachtszeit schenken. 


Teilnahmezeitraum: 13.11.2026 bis 16.11.2026

 


Inhaltsübersicht


									Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


									Alle Infos zur PETA x Adventsome-Verlosung


									Lust auf noch mehr vegane Adventskalender?


Interview mit Adventsome: Lea und Josias im Gespräch zum veganen Adventskalender


Wir haben mit den Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome – Lea und Josias – ein Interview geführt, um die Menschen hinter dem Projekt und den Gedanken hinter dem veganen Adventskalender vorzustellen: Welche Motivation treibt sie an, welche Rolle spielen Tiere bei Entscheidungen und wie kann ein Adventskalender über die Weihnachtszeit hinaus etwas bewegen? 


Lea und Josias – die Gründer:innen des Start-ups Adventsome.


PETA: Nehmt uns mit an den Anfang: Wie wurde aus eurer persönlichen Begeisterung für Adventskalender die Idee zu Adventsome?


Gab es einen bestimmten Moment, in dem ihr dachtet: „Genau so einen Kalender möchten wir selbst entwickeln“?

 


Adventsome:

 Die Idee kam uns, als wir uns 2017 gegenseitig Adventskalender schenken wollten, aber uns keiner wirklich begeistern konnte. Wir wünschten uns einen, der uns mit jedem Türchen aufs Neue überrascht, ganz viele unterschiedliche Produktkategorien vereint und in einer sinnvollen Verpackung kommt, die nicht nach 24 Tagen im Müll landet. Die zwei Kalender, die wir daraufhin selbst bastelten, haben uns im Dezember so viel Freude bereitet, dass wir beschlossen haben, diese auch mit anderen zu teilen. Ein Jahr später brachten wir unsere ersten 500 Adventskalender auf den Markt, die wir damals alle selbst neben der Uni verpackten – das waren ganze 12.000 einzelne Geschenke! 


PETA: Weihnachten verbinden viele Menschen mit Mitgefühl und Nächstenliebe. Welche Rolle spielen Tiere für euch dabei – und wie hat das eure Entscheidung für einen vollständig veganen Adventskalender geprägt?

  


Adventsome

: Wir lieben Tiere, haben selbst auch zwei

Katzen adoptiert

 und uns jahrelang im Tierschutz engagiert. Mit Adventsome möchten wir daher keine Produkte unterstützen, für die Tiere leiden müssen. Gleichzeitig finden wir es spannend, wie vielfältig das vegane Sortiment mittlerweile ist und wie viele innovative Alternativen es gibt. Genau den Brands, die diese Entwicklung weiter vorantreiben, möchten wir eine Bühne geben und ihnen helfen, bekannter zu werden. Unser Adventskalender soll Menschen dafür begeistern, Neues auszuprobieren und vielleicht auch die eine oder andere Gewohnheit zu hinterfragen! 


PETA: Euer Kalender verbindet 20 Produkte von Start-ups mit vier Spendentürchen. Was sollen Menschen beim Auspacken erleben – und was soll davon nach dem 24. Dezember bleiben?

 


Adventsome

: Wir wünschen uns, dass unsere Kund:innen jeden Morgen mit echter Vorfreude ein Türchen öffnen. Das schönste Feedback ist für uns, wenn uns jemand schreibt, dass er oder sie wieder kindliche Neugier verspürt. Richtige Überraschungen sind im Erwachsenenleben so selten geworden! 


Nach Weihnachten bleiben soll zunächst einmal unsere weiterverwendbare Design-Box, die wir jedes Jahr mit einer Künstlerin gemeinsam kreieren. Außerdem hoffentlich ganz viele neue Gedankenanstöße und Perspektiven und vielleicht auch das ein oder andere Lieblingsprodukt?

author: Benji
title: Grossdemo gegen Tönnies
content:
Grossdemo gegen Tönnies

Wir demonstrieren am 21.11. in Kellinghusen

Ihr seid wütend auf Tönnies? Wir auch! Wir haben

dokumentiert

, was Schweine bei Tönnies wirklich erleiden müssen. Wir haben bei Tönnies in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert. Doch Tönnies tötet weiter. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal groß auf und demonstrieren an dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen: Kellinghusen.


Bist du dabei?


Samstag, 21.11.2026

14:00 – 17:00 Uhr

Unterer Marktplatz, 25548 Kellinghusen

Hintergrundinfos


Rideshare-Tool

Damit möglichst viele Menschen zur Demo gegen Tönnies kommen, wollen wir euch bei der Planung eurer Anreise unterstützen. Daher haben wir ein cleveres Rideshare-Tool entwickelt, mit dem ihr Fahrgemeinschaften bilden könnt. So wird die Anreise für euch günstiger, einfacher und spaßiger.


Jetzt einsteigen!

Warum demonstrieren wir?

Anlass für die Großdemo am 21. November ist unsere aktuelle Veröffentlichung „Töten im Takt – Die grausamste Maschine bei Tönnies“. Tönnies ist Deutschlands größter Schlachtkonzern und gilt als eines der mächtigsten Unternehmen der europäischen Fleischindustrie. Als Marktführer tötet Tönnies jedes Jahr 16 Millionen Schweine. Unsere Aufdeckung zeigt den grausamen Erstickungskampf der Tiere in der CO₂-Anlage. Die Schweine schreien vor Angst und versuchen zu fliehen.


Was wir bisher getan haben

Gewalt im Schlachthof aufgedeckt

Verstöße dokumentiert

Tönnies angezeigt

Eine große Welle an Presseberichten ausgelöst

Zahlreiche Interviews geführt

Eine politische und gesellschaftliche Debatte angestoßen

Bei der Tönnies-Zentrale in Rheda-Wiedenbrück protestiert

Hintergrundinfos

Und jetzt?

Die Gewalt im Schlachthaus geht unvermindert weiter! Wir sind wütend. Deshalb fahren wir jetzt nochmal ganz groß auf, bündeln unsere Kräfte an einem Termin und demonstrieren gemeinsam mit euch an genau dem Schlachthof, aus dem die Aufnahmen unserer Aufdeckung stammen:

Kellinghusen!


Unsere Forderung: Der Betrieb muss schließen!


Ablauf und Programm

14:00 Uhr: Auftakt


Wir starten mit einer Auftaktkundgebung mit Redebeiträgen auf dem Unteren Marktplatz.

Demozug


Als großer und lauter Demozug ziehen wir mit Schildern, Bannern und Fahnen durch Kellinghusen, skandieren lautstark und setzen ein starkes Zeichen.

Zwischenstopp am Schlachthof


Die Demoroute führt uns bis zum Schlachthof. Dort gibt es weitere Redebeiträge.

Abschlusskundgebung


Gemeinsam laufen wir zurück zum Unteren Marktplatz, wo die Demo nach einer Abschlusskundgebung endet.

So kannst du mithelfen

Du willst mithelfen, dass die Demo richtig groß wird? Dann unterstütze uns bei der Mobilisierung: Bring deine Freund*innen mit zur Demo, teile unseren

Content auf Social Media

 oder poste selbst unser Sharepic:


Demoregeln

Bitte beachtet unsere allgemeinen Demohinweise, damit sich alle wohlfühlen. Danke für euer Verständnis und eure Mithilfe!


1. Antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch

Einen Ansatz, die Ausbeutung der Tiere zu reformieren und somit im Grundsatz beizubehalten, verfolgen wir nicht. Unsere Forderungen sind grundsätzlich antispeziesistisch und abolitionistisch. Wir bitten deshalb ausdrücklich darum, auf der Demo vermeintliche „Zwischenschritte“ oder „Reformen“ (z. B. Biofleischkonsum oder Verbesserung der Haltungsbedingungen) nicht als Ziel zu kommunizieren.

2. Kein Platz für Menschenfeindlichkeit

ARIWA lehnt alle Formen allgemeiner und gruppenbezogener Menschenfeindlichkeit (wie zum Beispiel Ableismus, Antisemitismus, Homo- und Trans*feindlichkeit, Rassismus oder Sexismus) sowie verschwörungsideologische Denkmuster ab. Personen mit solchen Hintergründen sind bei der Demo ausdrücklich nicht erwünscht. Mehr Infos:

ariwa.org/selbstverstaendnis

3. Keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs

Bitte tragt nach Möglichkeit keine Kleidung tierischen Ursprungs und achtet darauf, dass sie auch nicht so aussieht. Denn Produkte wie Kunstpelz oder Kunstleder können missverstanden werden und für Außenstehende einen falschen Eindruck erwecken.

4. Keine Partei- oder Religionswerbung

Parteiwerbung, Werbung für religiöse Gruppierungen sowie Holocaust-Vergleiche sind nicht erwünscht.

5. Bitte keine Tiere mitbringen

Aufgrund von Lärm, Hitze und Enge bitten wir euch, keine Tiere mit zur Demo zu bringen.

title: Quorn Hunt Humiliated: Terrierman Arrested As Sabs Disrupt Opening Meet.
content:
Legendary animal liberationist Barry Horne honoured by Northants Sabs.


Just weeks after publishing damning footage of the

Quorn Hunt killing a fox and training hounds

 to attack, saboteurs descended upon their prestigious opening meet – and completely ruined it.


Quorn Killers and Horne Haunts Quorn. Banners proudly displayed by Northants Sabs at the Quorn killers opening meet, 6 November, 2026. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs.


The day saw violence and abuse by the hunt, and resulted in the arrest of a terrierman who attempted to flee from police.


The day was dedicated to Barry Horne, a legendary activist who made the ultimate sacrifice for animal liberation.


Barry was involved in numerous daring rescue operations, helping to free animals destined for experimentation. He died following a series of hunger strikes intended to pressure Tony Blair’s Labour government over its promise to hold an inquiry into vivisection.


Barry Horne, 17 March 1990, rescuing 82 beagle puppies and 26 rabbits from Harlan Interfauna in Huntingdon. The site is now associated with MBR Acres Ltd, and the long-running Camp Beagle protests against the breeding of dogs for laboratory experiments for the petrochemical, chemical and pharmaceutical industries.


The government reneged on its promise, and animal rights activists reacted with fury in Barry’s name, and thousands more animals, including cats, rabbits and guinea pigs were liberated by activists during his hunger strikes.


Barry was also formerly a member of Northants Hunt Sabs. He died on November 5, 2001. His death radicalised and mobilised countless more animal liberations in his name.

In September 2026 multiple dogs were liberated from the MBR site

.


On Friday 6 November 2026, a day after the 25th anniversary of Barry’s death, the Quorn Hunt held their opening meet at its kennels in Kirby Bellars, Leicestershire.


The day did not quite go as they may have planned.


The Quorn Hunt October 2026, kill a fox and use the body to train the hounds. Notice the huntsman blowing for the kill over the hounds as they tear the body apart. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


On the back of the horrendous footage released only weeks earlier, Northants Hunt Sabs, including personal friends of Barry’s, turned out to stop the Quorn Hunt from killing on their watch.


Part time whipper-in and terrier ‘man’ Mickey Vaughn practising for the regional gurning championship.

Image: Northants Hunt Sabs.


Northants Sabs truly smashed the day, hunt tempers flared as sabs arrived at the meet with banners and flags speaking truth about ‘trail hunting’.


Vaughan bravely attacking a woman. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


True to form, the hunters natural default for violence saw sabs attacked and pushed to the ground. Sabs stood their ground following the violent outburst and the hunt was soon put back in their box.


Vaughan being put back into his box. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


Sabs stayed on the hunt throughout the day, leaving huntsman Joe Tesseyman struggling to find opportunities to hunt foxes with saboteurs on his case.


Huntsman Joe Tessyman on the run from sabs and police alike. Image Northants Hunt Sabs


Then, near Cream Gorse, the hunter became the hunted.


A Quorn terrierman was spotted leaving the covert on a quad bike, with officers from Leicestershire Police’s Rural Crime Team in hot pursuit.


The hot pursuit began with a terrierman fleeing from police after leaving the covert. Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


Mickey Vaughan, the terrierman and occasional whipper-in, attempted to slow the pursuing officers down by positioning his horse in the road. Police moved him aside and continued after the terrierman on the quad.


The quad overturned, and the terrierman was spotted running up Pasture Lane with a police officer hot on his tail behind.


You can’t park that there, mate. Image Northants Hunt Saboteurs.


Clearly a runner he was not.


He was promptly caught, cuffed and arrested.


At first I was all like… Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


We couldn’t possibly comment on what the arrest relates to and will not speculate, but lets hope they throw “obstructing an officer” at him whilst they are at it. Same goes for Vaughan who attempted to prevent the officer from pursuing the masked terrierman.


Then I was like… Image: Northants Hunt Sabs


Meanwhile the mounted field dwindled out, no doubt many of whom left thoroughly embarrassed by the thuggish behaviour of this supposed-prestigious hunt …

title: Animal Rights Radicals Destroy Several Hunting Hides in Italy amid Controversy over Hunting Law Reform
content:
Several hunting hides in Veneto have been wrecked and covered in anti-hunting graffiti. Images released by four hunting organisations show the Animal Liberation Front (ALF) signature and messages opposing the reform of Italy’s hunting legislation.

Vandalism against hunting facilities is making headlines in Italy once again. Several hunting hides (capanni da caccia) have been destroyed in the Veneto region, with their structures covered in graffiti opposing hunting and the reform of the legislation governing it in the country.

The incidents were publicly condemned this Wednesday, 4 November, by four organisations in the sector: the Cacciatori Veneti association, CONFAVI, ACR and FCR. The organisations released a gallery of photographs showing the damage to the facilities and the inscriptions left on their structures.

The graffiti includes the familiar ALF signature, standing for Animal Liberation Front (Animal Liberation Front), alongside messages calling for a boycott of the reform of Italy’s hunting law. The symbols visible in the images match those used in previous actions attributed to this animal rights movement.

The organisations accompanied the photographs with a strongly worded message directed at those responsible for the damage: “Destroying other people’s property does not defend any cause; it only demonstrates cowardice.”

The incident comes at a time of heightened tension over the reform of Italy’s hunting legislation. The bill seeks to amend Law 157/1992, which provides the basic legal framework for wildlife protection and the regulation of hunting.

The graffiti found on the Veneto hides directly links the property damage to this legislative controversy. However, the messages written on the facilities do not, on their own, identify the people who carried out the attacks. So far, no information has been released about arrests or police investigations relating to this incident either.

The appearance of the initials ALF recalls other incidents of vandalism recorded in Italy against facilities used by hunters.

One of the most notable previous incidents occurred in December 2019 in Montorfano, in the province of Brescia. On that occasion, eleven hunting hides in the municipalities of Rovato, Cologne and Palazzolo were wrecked. The damage was accompanied by threats and graffiti bearing the Animal Liberation Front signature.

More recently, in December 2025, six hides were destroyed in the Lower Valsugana area, between the municipalities of Grigno and Ospedaletto, in the province of Trento. The structures were found knocked down and marked with offensive messages directed at hunters. The ALF signature was also found in that case.

These previous incidents show that the destruction of hunting facilities is nothing new in Italy. The repeated attacks on hunting hides reveal a problem that goes beyond the war of words between supporters and opponents of hunting.

title: A Licence to Hunt: “Cruel, Inhumane and Selfish” Lauderdale Huntswoman Sentenced: 300 Hours’ Unpaid Work and Ten-Year Dog Ban
content:
Scotland’s first conviction under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023 has resulted in a substantial community sentence for ex-huntswoman Claire Bellamy, following evidence gathered by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs.


Claire Bellamy after breaching the licence.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


Former Lauderdale Hunt master and huntswoman Claire Bellamy has been sentenced to 300 hours of unpaid work and banned from owning or keeping most dogs for ten years after being convicted of deliberately hunting a fox with hounds. 


Bellamy appeared at Paisley Sheriff Court on Monday 9th November, where Sheriff Gill imposed the maximum 300 hours of unpaid work permitted under a Community Payback Order, to be completed within 12 months. 


The sentence follows

Bellamy’s conviction in October

, the first secured under Scotland’s Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023.


The prosecution was made possible thanks to footage captured by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs, who have been documenting the ongoing illegal hunting in Scotland that has continued since the new licensing system became law. 


On the 4th January 2025 – almost 2 years after the new law came into force – Bellamy was hunting with approximately 17 hounds near Kirkton Woods, between Houston in Renfrewshire and Kilmacolm in Inverclyde.


The hunt had obtained a licence from NatureScot, the public body responsible for administering Scotland’s licensing scheme.


However, the licence did not give the hunt unrestricted permission to hunt foxes. It was also strictly restricted to a certain geographical area.


“The recording of the fox being chased by multiple hounds was particularly harrowing to watch.” Sheriff Gill


Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


Footage captured by sabs, showed hounds hunting a fox into an open field beyond the boundaries specified in the licence. The dogs were not under control – also a requirement of the licence.


During the trial Sheriff Gill described the footage as harrowing and rejected Bellamy’s claim that she had not deliberately hunted the fox. 


A member of the Glasgow Hunt Sabs filming the hunt as they breach the NatureScot issued license.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs. 


At sentencing the sheriff praised the evidence of the witnesses, singling out the hunt sab who recorded the pursuit.


In contrast, Sheriff Gill addressing Bellamy directly described her actions as “

cruel, inhumane and selfish

”.


“Cruel, inhumane and selfish” – words used by Sheriff Gill to describe Bellamy during her sentencing hearing.  Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


The court heard that Bellamy had taken part in approximately 1,500 hunts during her ‘career’ as a fox-killer. Despite this, she had shown no responsibility for what occurred that day.


A background report prepared by probation services for sentencing recorded that Bellamy believed she had done nothing wrong, showed no empathy towards the hunted fox, and considered herself to be the victim of an example being made.


The hounds chasing the fox.


“What you don’t understand is that the law is the law, and you are bound by the law.” Sheriff Gill.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


She also complained that Scotland’s legislation made hunting foxes more difficult, to which Sheriff Gill’s response was an astonished

“Ms Bellamy, that is the purpose of the legislation

”.


The court also made it clear that Bellamy was bound by the law regardless of whether she personally agreed with it.


The belief among the hunting community that their traditional animal cruelty should take precedence over legislation designed to protect wildlife was shattered in Paisley Sheriff courts.


Bellamy escaped a custodial sentence, although Sheriff Gill made it clear that prison was a genuine possibility.


Claire Bellamy hunting the fox in breach of the licence.

Image: Glasgow Hunt Sabs.


The Community Payback Order requiring 300 hours of unpaid work was imposed as a direct alternative to imprisonment. Bellamy was further warned that failing to comply with the order could result in her returning to court and potentially receiving a custodial sentence. 


Bellamy was also disqualified from keeping dogs for 10 years, though there is an exemption which allowed her to retain her pet terrier (it would be a terrier wouldn’t it), and the collies she uses in her shepherding work.


Whilst Bellamy is no longer master of the Lauderdale Hunt, this didn’t stop the Lauderdale recently advertising a

‘Newcomers to Trail Hunting Week’

, which was quickly removed …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: 160 Climate Scientists Warn BAAJA Would Destroy US Chances of Reaching Net Zero
content:
The bill would effectively lock in current levels of fossil fuel infrastructure and usage forever, they warn.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

A group of over 160 climate scientists is urging the House to block the major bipartisan permitting reform bill from passage, warning that its entrenchment of fossil fuel infrastructure could likely prevent the U.S. from ever reaching net zero emissions, which would be disastrous for the climate.

In a letter published Tuesday, the scientists express “deep concern” that the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), which passed the Senate on Friday, would drastically weaken key environmental laws like the National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA), while granting fossil fuel companies powerful tools to ensure its influence never wanes.

“BAAJA’s extensive changes to existing laws would make it almost impossible for a court to enjoin an action based on a violation of NEPA or of the National Historic Preservation Act, in effect pulling the teeth from these very important laws,” the letter says.

“Furthermore, we are concerned that BAAJA’s creation of the new ‘Disparate Treatment’ standard for energy permitting will prevent the rapid and nearly total phase out of coal, oil, and fossil gas from the U.S. and global energy systems. Without this phase out, and the subsequent reduction of emissions to (net) zero, the world will be unable to halt global heating,” the scientists wrote.

The letter effort was led by top climate scientists, including Michael Mann, of the University of Pennsylvania; Michael Oppenheimer, at Princeton University; and Robert Brulle and J. Timmons Roberts of Brown University, who have done critical research on the fossil fuel industry’s work to block action on the climate crisis.

The letter effort was necessary because “of the speed with which this deeply problematic bill seems headed toward passage without the due diligence and scrutiny any such far-reaching bill demands,” Mann told Truthout, “pushed through in the proverbial dark of night of the Thanksgiving holiday lull of a lame duck congressional session, and backed by a veritable who’s who of bad fossil fuel and dark money actors.”

The “disparate treatment” standard in the bill, the letter explains, empowers fossil fuel companies to file lawsuits to defang or overturn climate legislation. Under the standard, companies would be able to sue if they are being granted permits at a lower standard than in previous years, with the potential to reclaim up to 100 percent of projected construction costs plus damages and legal fees — footed by the American taxpayer.

At the same time, the bill would majorly hamstring federal agencies in their ability to revise or revoke rules and permits in the interest of public health or the climate, barring “immediate” harm.

Taken together, these provisions would prevent the U.S. from ever taking steps to meaningfully reduce its greenhouse gas emissions, they warn.

“As environmental law scholar David Bookbinder notes, this effectively insulates not only the construction but the operation at normal capacity of all existing fossil fuel infrastructure. Such a lock-in of extant fossil-fuel infrastructure would effectively prevent the U.S. from ever reaching (net) zero emissions,” the letter says.

The scientists also cite research finding that BAAJA would cause emissions to rise and contribute to air pollution-related mortality.

“[A]s written the bill would prevent the rapid and nearly total phase out of coal, oil, and fossil gas from the U.S. and global energy systems, which science says we must do if we’re going to halt global heating,” said Genevieve Guenther, founding director of End Climate Silence and organizer of the letter. The disparate treatment standard, Guenther said, “means that it effectively makes the current balance of energy sources permanent.”

“BAAJA is not progress. It is a step in the wrong direction, away from a (net) zero economy,” Guenther warned.

The climate concerns are the latest to be brought up against BAAJA, which opponents have warned would also help fast track data center construction and majorly sideline Tribal sovereignty. Critics have also noted several corruption concerns in relation to the bill, including former Sen. Kyrsten Sinema’s role in lobbying for the bill, and reports that a natural gas pipeline …

title: Nachhaltigkeit oder Müllproblem? Billig-Kleidung/Fast Fashion – was Mode zum Klimafaktor Nummer 1 macht
content:
Dossier


“… Die Schränke sind voll, die Modeindustrie boomt: Seit dem Jahr 2000 hat sich der Absatz an neuer Kleidung mehr als verdoppelt. Es wird immer billiger und immer schneller produziert. Fast Fashion heißt dieses Phänomen. (…) Dieser Konsum hat seinen Preis. Den bezahlen nicht wir, sondern andere, rechnet uns Thomas Seibert vor. (…) „Sie können mit der Baumwolle anfangen, mit den Pestiziden, die gebraucht werden, mit dem ungeheuren Wasserverbrauch. Jede Menge Flüsse und Seen sind mittlerweile einfach umgekippt, wegen der Einleitung von Abwässer aus der Produktion. Video und Beitrag von Anke Heinhaus vom 12.03.2020 beim Hessischen Rundfunk

 


, siehe dazu:


Black Friday: Wer zahlt den wahren Preis für die billige Mode? Stoppt Fast Fashion!


„

Black Friday – ein schwarzer Tag für die Umwelt. Immer billiger, immer mehr, immer schneller. Lass uns das ändern!


Rabatte, Schnäppchen, Kaufrausch. Doch hinter den vermeintlichen Angeboten steckt ein System, das uns mit aggressiven Marketingstrategien, künstlichem Zeitdruck und psychologischen Tricks immer mehr Kleidung kaufen lässt. Die Folgen: riesige Mengen Textilmüll, Ressourcenverschwendung und massive Umweltbelastungen. Während Modekonzerne profitieren, zahlen Mensch und Umwelt den Preis. Ultra-Fast-Fashion – die bunten Plastiktüten in gewebter Form – ist eines der größten Umweltprobleme unserer Zeit geworden.


Das kann so nicht weitergehen: Die Hersteller müssen endlich für Überproduktion, Textilmüll und Umweltschäden geradestehen und langlebige, reparierbare Mode zum Standard machen.


Wir fordern: Schluss mit Fast Fashion, Schluss mit der Wegwerfmode! Unterschreibe jetzt unsere Petition und fordere Carsten Schneider auf, ein starkes Textilgesetz auf den Weg zu bringen!

…“

Kampagne und Petition von Deutsche Umwelthilfe e.V.

 


Shein und Co.: Frankreich erhebt Sondergebühr für Wegwerfmode


„

Zwölf Euro Abgabe pro Jacke, neun Euro für eine Jeans, zwei Euro für ein T-Shirt: Frankreich will die Verbreitung von Billigmode mit Strafzahlungen einschränken. In den kommenden Jahren sollen sie noch weiter angehoben werden.


Eine Billigjacke eines Onlinehändlers wie Shein oder Temu kostet in Frankreich künftig bis zu zwölf Euro mehr. Die Regierung veröffentlichte am Freitag im Amtsblatt die neuen Regeln, die die Verbreitung sogenannter Wegwerfmode einschränken sollen und ab dem 1. September gelten. Im laufenden Jahr werden demnach auch 50 Cent für Unterhosen oder Socken, zwei Euro für ein T-Shirt und neun Euro für Jeans fällig, die bestimmten Kriterien entsprechen. Frankreich wolle auf diese Weise gegen ein Geschäftsmodell vorgehen, »das darauf beruht, dass ein Kleidungsstück in Rekordzeit von der Ladenfläche in die Mülltonne wandert«, schrieb der Umweltstaatssekretär Mathieu Lefèvre im Onlinedienst X.


»Die schädlichen Auswirkungen der Ultra-Fast-Fashion auf unsere Umwelt und unsere Wirtschaft sind bekannt und dokumentiert«, fügte er hinzu. Die Kriterien sind so formuliert, dass sie in erster Linie asiatische Onlinehändler wie Shein und Temu treffen, nicht aber Ketten wie Zara, H&M oder Uniqlo, die in Frankreich Arbeitsplätze bieten. Entscheidend ist die Menge der Modelle, die auf den Markt gebracht werden, und deren Preis im Verhältnis zu einer Reparatur.


Anstieg programmiert


Die Strafzahlungen sollen bis 2030 ansteigen und dann etwa zwei Euro für Unterhosen und 19,50 Euro für eine Jacke erreichen. Das Geld soll in einen Fonds fließen, mit dem vorbildliche Unternehmen unterstützt werden sollen. Dazu sind bislang keine Details bekannt

author: James Crump
title: Israel Has Turned Gaza Into a ‘Toxic Wasteland’, Report Finds
content:
Israel’s destruction of Gaza has poisoned the water, soil and air, turning the enclave into a “toxic wasteland” which threatens the population’s survival,

a new report has found

. 


According to Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory, heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings and raw sewage have potentially contaminated more than 99% of the territory.


Oxfam International’s executive director, Amitabh Behar, said: “Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza includes military assaults on its environment, which are environmental war crimes threatening life now and for generations to come.”


“Raw sewage is pouring into the sea and leaking into the ground, while the destruction of Gaza’s sanitation systems leaves people with little protection from the contamination around them,” he said, adding that pregnant women and children are among those facing the highest risks.


“In an area as small, oppressed and densely populated as Gaza, continuous exposure is inevitable, with people surrounded by waste and sewage, spreading pests and the risk of disease growing.”


Oxfam’s report, which was compiled using satellite imagery and other open-source data, 

gives the most comprehensive overview of environmental damage in Gaza to date. 


The UN Environment Programme estimates that Israel’s genocide has generated 61 million tonnes of debris from pulverised infrastructure, or 29 tonnes for every person in Gaza. Much of that material includes hazardous substances, according to Oxfam. 


Gaza’s displaced population is currently facing catastrophic winter conditions, with heavy rain affecting more than 106,000 people and recently causing tents and makeshift shelters to flood and latrines to overflow.

author: Önder Algedik
title: COP31 collapsed in Türkiye. The hosts’ fossil ties did not
content:
The COP31 talks in Antalya ended on November 22 without a decision. It was the first such failure since Copenhagen in 2009. In Australia, the argument is about Chris Bowen.

Here is what the argument leaves out.

Saudi Arabia kept a fixed position through the second week: The text must not mention fossil fuels and should boost carbon capture, delegates told Reuters. NPR reports that Saudi Arabia and Russia blocked fossil fuels from the final agreement. The European Union (EU) also hardened its position, according to Reuters.

The rejection came from the other side.

The EU, several small island states and other vulnerable countries said they could not accept a text that failed to mention oil, gas and coal. Ireland’s climate minister, speaking for the EU, said the COP was “hijacked by some oil states”.

Vanuatu’s delegation called the silence on fossil fuels unacceptable. Least developed countries and the African Union also objected over finance, accusing the EU of failing to honour past commitments. The Marshall Islands delegation said the Pacific was “let down on all sides”.

The people who said no to a text without fossil fuels were the people most exposed to them. They are not the people who wrote it that way.

Saudi, Chinese and Russian officials frequently visited the presidency offices, as Saturday became Sunday, delegates told Reuters, while other groups struggled to secure meetings.

Negotiators from Europe, small island states, Latin America, Asia and Africa said Saudi Arabia had disproportionate access. The Turkish presidency said no group or country received preferential treatment!

I cannot prove a link between what Türkiye signs and who gets a meeting. The ties themselves are public. Türkiye and Saudi Arabia signed a renewable energy agreement worth about US$2 billion in February. It entered into force on October 21 and a further memorandum was signed in Antalya on November 10, witnessed by President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.

On November 5, four days before COP31 opened, the Turkish parliament ratified the Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, by 279 votes to 119.

Then, the day after the COP31 talks collapsed, the Russian gas corporation Novatek’s chairperson said in China that it had signed an liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply contract with Türkiye. The counterparty, volume and term were not disclosed.

Türkiye presided over COP31, through Murat Kurum, its environment, urbanisation and climate change minister. Australia led the negotiations, through the Climate Change and Energy Minister Bowen, with “exclusive authority ” over them.

That matters more than the blame game in Canberra suggests.

Bowen’s 18-page draft of November 16 called for a phase-out of fossil fuels. By Thursday, it was nine pages without fossil fuels and the Pacific Resilience Facility Australia had championed.

Bowen presented the final text with Kurum. The ABC’s Laura Tingle reported that he conceded red lines on fossil fuels and finance had blocked a deal. She also noted that Türkiye effectively set the conditions while Australia carried the negotiating burden.

Coalition Opposition leader Angus Taylor, who wants Australia to scrap its already weak net zero targets, said Bowen should resign. Albanese answered by invoking the national interest. Nobody mentioned the coal and gas mine expansions.

Australia was named Fossil of the Day as the first draft came out, with the Climate Action Network counting 38 coal and gas approvals since 2022. On October 14, the federal government approved 30 million tonnes more coal at Boggabri, until 2040.

Most emissions from such projects occur overseas.

One host approves projects. The other signs contracts. The units differ; an approval is not a contract. The direction is the same.

By my count, Türkiye has signed 19 fossil fuel agreements since September 2025, plus six nuclear and mining deals, which I count separately. Novatek would be the 20th. In the venue, 103 fossil fuel and polluting organisations registered. Sixty were fossil fuel interests and 45 came as Türkiye’s guests.

For the Pacific and the vulnerable countries, the talks’ collapse is a loss they can name. For the fossil order it costs nothing. It can lose a text. It cannot afford to lose a mine, a pipeline or a contract that runs for decades and none of those were on the table in Antalya. A text decides what governments agree to say. Approvals and contracts decide what they do.

So the useful measure of COP31 is not …

Special Envoy

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Scientists study climate change impact on Baffin Bay ice
content:
An expedition aboard the Canadian Coast Guard research icebreaker Amundsen to study sea ice in Baffin Bay is nearly complete after departing from Iqaluit on Oct. 29.


Aboard the vessel with coast guard staff are 39 scientists from Canada, Switzerland, and France who are studying how climate change is altering the formation of sea ice in western Baffin Bay, said Dany Dumont, who is leading what’s being called the Cascades Expedition.


“We went up to 72 degrees north [latitude], chasing ice where it was forming,” Dumont said in an interview Thursday from the ship, sheltered off the coast of Brevoort Island.


The expedition also included visits to three other sites along Baffin Island’s east coast, located at 71, 74 and 75 degrees north, and will conclude Nov. 25 in Quebec City.


Dumont said it’s the first time the Canadian Coast Guard has allowed scientists to access the region this late in the season when sea ice freezes up, calling it a “one-of-a-kind expedition.”


He said the crew has mostly observed what he called “new ice” — ice that formed this season, as opposed to older ice that has lasted at least one summer or longer.


“Eventually, in a warmer climate — as it is the case in Antarctica for example — the old ice will likely disappear, and only new, first-year ice will be present,” said Dumont, who is also a professor at the University of Quebec at Rimouski’s oceanography department.


“This new ice is very vulnerable to melting, and that explains the warm temperatures and warm ocean that we see, and how little ice we see.”


Scientists used drones and small craft to study a number of variables from each site they visited, such as the temperature and salinity of the ocean’s surface, the characteristics of newer and older ice, and the formation of ocean waves, Dumont said.


Researchers also carried out sampling aimed at better understanding the relationship between sea ice and ocean ecosystems.


The second leg of the Cascades Expedition, taking place in November, represents a collaboration among the Institut nordique du Québec — a group of Quebec experts in the field of northern and Arctic research — the Swiss Polar Institute, and the French Polar Institute. In August, the same crew carried out a similar expedition from the icebreaker along the west coast of Greenland to study melting glaciers.


Jean-Éric Tremblay, the project leader for the expedition, said the release of freshwater from glaciers is important to study because it impacts the extent to which sea ice hardens in Baffin Bay.


The findings of the research will also aid scientists in making more accurate predictions about sea ice and climate change in the Arctic, Tremblay said. Those models are useful for governments and coastal communities who need forecasts about sea ice cover for use in navigation.


“We expect that with climate change, eventually all the glaciers will have receded on land, so in a way it provides us with a window into the future,” he said.

author: La Zarzamora
title: Comunicado público de José Melgarejo Calbullanca, PPM del caso Grollmus en Huelga de Hambre
content:
Pu Machi, pu Lonko, pu Wuenen, pu Werken, pu Weichave, pu Kona.

Rekuluwaiñ ka yavuluwaiñ ni ta tuvachi weichan.

Inche José Melgarejo Calbullanca, tañi lov Lleu-lleu mapu, comunidad Nicolás Calbullanca, territorio lavkenche, Lago Lleu-lleu.

Doy a conocer mi situación como preso político mapuche, recluído en la cárcel CP Biobío, llevando ya 2 años y medio, de una condena de 7 años y medio y de otra por el llamado Caso del Molino Grollmus, por el cual fui juzgado por el Tribunal de Cañete y condenado a 86 años de prisión, juicio al que actualmente estamos apelando en la Corte Suprema, exigiendo su anulación y del cual me declaro, como lo he hecho anteriormente, inocente de los hechos que se me imputaron y por los que fuí condenado a esta altísima condena.

Por este motivo es que junto a otros ppm, hemos decidido iniciar una Huelga de Hambre de carácter indefinido, exigiendo 3 puntos principales:

Kiñe: Nulidad del juicio viciado y racista que nos condenó.

Epu: La creación de un módulo comuneros mapuche en el Cp Biobío.

Por esto hago un llamado a las comunidades, territorios, organizaciones, Hogares Mapuche, Estudiantes y a los demás prisioneros políticos, a que nos apoyen en este proceso. Estaremos eternamente agradecidos de su apoyo fraterno.

También aprovecho de agradecer a todas las personas que me han apoyado, a mi como a los demás ppm, todo este tiempo.

Desde acá me siento con alto newen para seguir luchando por nuestros justos derechos como pueblo nación Mapuche.

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: Groups decry abduction attempt on Lumad youth activist in Davao City
content:
Lumad youth activist Mawing Pangadas answers questions from members of the media during a candle-lighting activity at Freedom Park in Davao City on the 2nd death anniversary of New Bataan 5 on February 24, 2024. Photo from Panalipdan Youth Davao’s Facebook page

Progressive groups condemned the alleged abduction attempt on Lumad youth activist Mawing Pangadas in Davao City.

The Hands Off Mindanao Youth Activists (HOMYA) Network reported that around 10 to 12 individuals wearing all-black clothing and caps allegedly pursued the 24-year-old youth activist along Upper Madapo Hills, Barangay 8-A, on November 17 while he was on his way home.

“[They] tried to corner him and said, ‘This is him. Do not run’,” the network stated in its alert released on November 19.

Pangadas who belongs to the Indigenous Manobo reportedly was able to escape. He lost his phone and slippers and sustained injuries after he tripped and fell down during the pursuit which reportedly lasted for three hours.

The HOMYA network said that this incident reflects the continuing attacks and harassment faced by activists. “These acts of intimidation inflict serious mental, emotional, and psychological distress not only on Mawing, the direct target of these fascist attacks, but also on his family and loved ones who are forced to live under constant fear and anxiety.”

Read: Groups slam PNP official’s apology after tagging Mindanao activists as ‘wanted persons’

Lara Felescoso, spokesperson for Resist! Campaign, a human rights advocacy initiative, also considered the abduction attempt as an attack against Lumad youth and Indigenous community members who fight for their ancestral lands and fundamental rights.

Pangadas, who hails in Talaingod, Davao del Norte, was a former student of the Salugpongan Ta Tanu Igkanogon Community Learning Center, a now-defunct alternative school teaching Indigenous children in the Davao region. He was a relative of the late Manobo leader Bai Bibyaon Ligkayan Bigkay.

Fifty-five Salugpongan schools across the region were shut down in 2019 for allegedly violating Department of Education (DepEd) regulations and for training children to become members of the New People’s Army (NPA), an accusation that has been debunked by the school administration and human rights organizations.

Read: Groups urge gov’t to prioritize reopening of Lumad schools in Mindanao

During a protest in Davao City for the State of the Nation Address (SONA) of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in 2022, Pangadas and his older brother Ismael were arrested by the police and faced criminal charges for alleged human trafficking. They were acquitted from these cases.

Read: Court acquits Lumad brothers, 3 teachers from human trafficking charges

Pangadas serves as the education and research officer of the environmental advocacy group Panalipdan Youth Davao and convenor of HOMYA, a network that has been established due to continuing attacks and harassment against activists in Mindanao.

With such circumstances, the HOMYA network did not rule out the possibility that the alleged abduction attempt might be state-perpetrated, raising suspicion that it is linked to the government’s counterinsurgency operations.

Various progressive groups and youth-led organizations demanded an immediate and impartial investigation to identify the perpetrators and hold them accountable. (DAA)
