author: Rizomatica
title: Comunicado inicio huelga de hambre Presos Políticos Mapuche del caso Grollmus
content:
«Comunicado inicio huelga de hambre ppm caso grollmus, 23/11/2026.


Marimari kom pu che, pu logko, pu werken, pu machi, pu weychabe, pu lob.


El día de hoy, nosotros, los abajo firmantes, venimos a informar a la opinión publica nacional e internacional, que tras largos procesos de discusión entre nosotros, prisioneros políticos mapuche lavkenche, y nuestros lov y comunidades, hemos tomado la decisión de iniciar una movilización consistente en una huelga de hambre de carácter seca e indefinida, esto como medio para exigir el petitorio que detallamos a continuación:


1) Nulidad y absolución para nosotros, los 18 Presos Políticos Mapuche recientemente condenados injustamente por el Caso Molino Grollmus. El tribunal de Cañete resolvió una pena ponderada de 1055 años, resolución judicial morbosa basada únicamente en 4 relatos de testigos protegidos y sin absolutamente ninguna prueba técnica o científica de corroboración.


2) Creación de un Modulo para Prisioneros Políticos Mapuche en el CP Biobio, para condenados e imputados, donde se garanticen no privilegios sino derechos internacional y nacionalmente consagrados.


• Este módulo garantizará espacio de cocina e ingreso tolerante y mayor de alimentos en la lista de providencias.


• Derecho a practicar ceremonias mapuche (acceso de pu machi, pu logko y pu werken )


• 100 cupos de enrolamiento por comuneros.


• Mayor encomienda, días de visita y venusterio.


• Garantía de usar vestimenta tradicional


• Acceso a Salud Intercultural (machi, lawentuchebe, ngutamchebe, pewmatube)


3) Plan de intervención con profesionales mapuche, con competencias culturales y profesionales, dupla psicólogo y trabajador social intercultural.


4) Área laboral donde se garantice acceso a talleres de trabajo para condenados e imputados.


5) Área educacional, talleres de mapudugun y cultura por profesionales competentes.


Las demandas anteriormente expuestas son justas y legitimas y deberán garantizarse mediante las firmas de las autoridades competentes. Llamamos de forma activa a nuestro pueblo a la solidaridad y movilización por la libertad y mejores condiciones carcelarias para los presos políticos mapuche. Creemos que el camino de la Unidad Nacional dotara a nuestro pueblo de la fuerza social para continuar luchando por la recuperación de nuestro territorio, así como por la retirada de las fuerzas de ocupación del Gulumapu, por la autonomía y autodeterminación del Wallmapu.


Finalmente exigimos el traslado de vuelta a Concepción del comunero Federico Astete Catrileo, recluido en la cárcel de Valdivia, y el fin a su injustificado régimen de alta seguridad y aislamiento.


Nelson Alonso Llempi


Rodrigo Valenzuela Canullan


Felipe Paineo Antiman


Jose Melgarejo Calbullanca


David Mariñan Millahual


Javier Mariñan Millahual.


¡Marichiwew!


CP Bío Bío


Lunes 23 de noviembre de 2026″.


*Enviado a la radio


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

.

author: Rizomatica
title: Comunicado público de José Melgarejo Calbullanca, Preso Político Mapuche del caso Grollmus
content:
«COMUNICADO PÚBLICO DE JOSÉ MELGAREJO CALBULLANCA, PPM CASO GROLLMUS


Pu Machi, pu Lonko, pu Wuenen, pu Werken, pu Weichave, pu Kona.


Rekuluwaiñ ka yavuluwaiñ ni ta tuvachi weichan.


Inche José Melgarejo Calbullanca, tañi lov Lleu-lleu mapu, comunidad Nicolás Calbullanca, territorio lavkenche, Lago Lleu-lleu.


Doy a conocer mi situación como preso político mapuche, recluído en la cárcel CP Biobío, llevando ya 2 años y medio, de una condena de 7 años y medio y de otra por el llamado Caso del Molino Grollmus, por el cual fui juzgado por el Tribunal de Cañete y condenado a 86 años de prisión, juicio al que actualmente estamos apelando en la Corte Suprema, exigiendo su anulación y del cual me declaro, como lo he hecho anteriormente, inocente de los hechos que se me imputaron y por los que fuí condenado a esta altísima condena.


Por este motivo es que junto a otros ppm, hemos decidido iniciar una Huelga de Hambre de carácter indefinido, exigiendo 3 puntos principales:


Kiñe: Nulidad del juicio viciado y racista que nos condenó.

Epu: La creación de un módulo comuneros mapuche en el Cp Biobío.

Küla: Mi traslado

author: Esperanza
title: RED ESTUDIANTIL TEMUCO: «Nos interesa generar una alianza social que sea capaz de soportar la arremetida neoriberal que estamos viviendo en este Gobierno».
content:
Tras conocer el proyecto de presupuesto de gobierno para el 2027, se registraron diversas manifestaciones para expresar el descontento social en algunas ciudades del país. Temuco fue una de ellas y en ese contexto conversamos con uno de los representantes de la Red Estudiantil Temuco.


Giordano Leonelli, estudiante Sociología Ufro y parte de la Red Estudiantil Temuco, una alianza entre la Universidad Católica de Temuco, La Universidad de La Frontera y estudiantes secundarios para activar movilizaciones en la ciudad de Temuco.


Hace algunas semanas, se vieron concentraciones y marchas que recorrieron el centro de la ciudad, convocadas por el sector estudiantil. Movilizaciones que surgen principalmente como respuesta tras conocerse los anuncios de recortes en el área de educación para el próximo año. 


«Sabemos las consecuencias que van a tener, van a ser despidos de funcionarios, peores condiciones para estudiar, peor infraestructura. Así como un debilitamiento de la educación pública, lo que nos parece bastante problemático». Giordano Leonelli, Red Estudiantil Temuco.


Como Red, ven la necesidad que el movimiento estudiantil se debe volver a rearticular, tal como en años anteriores. En esa misma línea realizaron un pliego de demandas para presentar un petitorio a nivel Temuco y sumado a ello se levantó un petitorio con alcance a nivel nacional que no solo reúne demandas sobre los recorte a la educación, sino también considera problemáticas asociadas a la salud, el medioambiente, el trabajo, la criminalización a la protesta popular, entre otros puntos.


«Nos interesa generar una alianza social que sea capaz de soportar la arremetida neoriberal que estamos viviendo en este Gobierno». Leonelli describe que trabajan por una articulación social, no partidista,que responda a los intereses de la población.


Se espera que para inicio de 2027 surjan nuevas movilizaciones con la consigna de frenar los recortes, todo en medio de un complejo escenario económico que enfrenta el país, en lo inmediato, la

Red estudiantil Temuco llama sumarse como bloque a la Jornada de Protesta Nacional convocada por profesores y sindicatos de trabajadores para el martes 24 de noviembre, en la Plaza del Hospital en Temuco, desde las 16:30 hrs.

title: Donald Trump extorts the Philippines
content:
The latest boast of lame duck US President Donald Trump that the Philippines has agreed to source all of its energy and food imports from the US is as credible as his claim that the Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni pleaded for a photo with him, or his insistence with Russian President Vladimir Putin that the Israelis adore him as to name a plaza in his honor, forcing Putin to deliver a snarky riposte: “Donald, Israel should rename their country after you.” Trump didn’t understand the insult, which was not lost in the translation.


Perhaps as worse was the yarn that Mexico had permitted US forces to operate within its territory, which President Caludia Sheinbaum debunked, saying US troops should stick to their US bases, or the brag of years past that Mexico would pay for the thousands of kilometers of durable and impenetrable fence he was building to separate it from the US. Americans paid for the few kilometers of the overpriced fence built by Trump minions.


Trump is a media hog, like the

bangka

 in a drinking spree who conjures stories the way Rodrigo Duterte does, and the usual result is that out of the 10 stories dished out, 11 are false. Trump was battered worldwide for insulting Meloni and Italy and the Mexican people made him the butt of jokes for years for being such a *puerile, reckless and bad storyteller. First of all, he cannot be serious about anything or anybody, save perhaps for his nanny Natalie Harp, and he can hardly understand what he is punishing the media industry with.


As in the case of Fox News before, the defense was that audiences knew that Tucker Carlson was not credible, so it is their call whether to believe him or despise him. Trump is worse that Carlson since the more he talks, the deeper he burrows in his rabbit hole. The guy simply is a congenital liar. Believe him at your peril. So when this clown spewed his latest insult, that the Philippines agreed to buy all its energy and farm imports from the United States otherwise the Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) cannot be invoked to defend the country from a possible Chinese attack, Malacanang should have taken a forceful response.


The retort to this extortion by Trump was a pablum, with the Palace saying Manila only tackled possible energy imports, noting that the Philippines doesn’t import gas from the US. As the US is saying it would export LNG, it is time for Manila to join the fun. Government is not saying that the US already exports shiploads of farm commodities to the country, from potatoes to specialty rice (with so many hundredweights—59.09 kilos each), as well as wheat, milk, meat and others. The response was **anodyne, not meant to be an underhanded compliment to a court jester and not a double-bladed

beinte nuebe

The administration should have been forthright to tell Trump that a global trading system operates in which the Philippines takes part and that the parity rights ended in 1974, when the Marcos dictatorship that Trump supported to the hilt was in its full bloom. Seventeen years later, the US military bases were kicked out of the Philippines for being precisely the bases of the country’s insecurity. Flashback to the confrontation with Malaysia over the Sabah issue and the US never sided with the Philippines despite the possibility of hostilities. The UK sided with Malaysia and the country was left in the lurch. The ironclad guarantee that US forces would come to fight for the Philippines evaporated.


As the late warmonger Henry Kissinger said being an enemy of the US is dangerous but being a friend of the US is fatal. The French knew it (the US hasn’t paid the money it owed Paris for supporting the US revolution against British colonialism), African countries understood it and Latin American nations had despised the Monroe Doctrine since 1823 and its latest reiteration, the Trump Latrine. By trying to make Trump look good with illogical statements, the Philippine government is massaging his fragile but galactic ego. This is like pulling blood out of stone or pulling hen’s teeth.

title: Kayyım atanan HalkTV'den nöbeti "Halk Televizyonu" devraldı
content:
Halk TV'ye 14 Ekim'de kayyım atanmasının ardından kanaldan ayrılan gazeteciler, Halk Televizyonu adıyla yeni bir yayın platformu kurdu. İlk canlı yayın, gazeteci Gökhan Kayış'ın sunumuyla 23 Kasım akşamı gerçekleştirildi.


Kayış, açılışta Uğur Dündar, Serhan Asker, Dinçer Gökçe ve avukat Seraf Özer'i ağırladı. Yayına gazeteciler, siyasetçiler ve meslek örgütü temsilcileri de canlı bağlantılarla katıldı.


Kayış, yeni yayın girişiminin nasıl ortaya çıktığını şu sözlerle anlattı:


“Kayyum atandıktan sonra dedik ki kardeşim bu memleketi bırakıp gidecek halimiz yok. Umutsuzluğa kapılacak halimiz de yok.”


Gazeteciliği sürdürebilecekleri yeni bir alan oluşturduklarını belirten Kayış, “Biz de bütün her şeye inat, bütün kayyum uygulamalarına inat Halk Televizyonunun macerasını başlattık” dedi.


Uğur Dündar: “Halkın gerçekleri öğrenme hakkına hizmet" 


Açılış yayınına katılan Uğur Dündar, gazeteciliğin temel işlevinin kamuoyunu bilgilendirmek olduğunu vurguladı:


“Gazeteciliği kaba anlamıyla tanımlarsak halkın gerçekleri öğrenme hakkına yapılan bir hizmettir gazetecilik mesleği.”


Dündar, iktidarların kamuoyunun gerçeklere ulaşmasını engellemeye çalışabildiğini belirterek araştırmacı gazeteciliğin karşılaştığı baskılara dikkat çekti.


“Görevimiz bu işi yaptığımız sürece doğruları, sadece doğruları, sonuna kadar doğruları söylemektir. Ve bunu yaparken de evrensel meslek ilkelerimize sıkı sıkıya bağlı kalmaktır.”


Dündar, yeni girişimin ekonomik dayanışma boyutuna da değindi. Halk TV'den ayrılan çalışanlar arasında ciddi geçim sıkıntısı yaşayanlar olduğunu belirterek YouTube gelirlerinin bu kişilere destek amacıyla kullanılabileceğini söyledi.


“Eğer bu kanal YouTube'dan para kazanırsa, ne kadar çok kazanırsa kazansın lütfen bana tek kuruş vermeyin. İhtiyacı olan arkadaşlarımıza dağıtın.”


TGC: “Basın hürdür, sansür edilemez”


Türkiye Gazeteciler Cemiyeti temsilcisi Sibel Güneş, canlı bağlantıyla katıldığı yayında medya kuruluşlarına yönelik kayyım uygulamalarını eleştirdi.


Güneş, son iki yılda çok sayıda televizyon kanalının yayınlarının sona erdiğini belirterek Halk TV, Tele1 ve Sözcü TV çalışanlarının karşılaştığı sorunlara dikkat çekti.


Anayasa'nın 28. ve 30. Maddelerini hatırlatan Güneş, şöyle konuştu:


“Anayasa 28. maddesi basın hürdür, sansür edilemez diyor. 30. madde de çok net basın araçlarının işletilmekten alıkonulamayacağını ifade ediyor.”


Güneş, Halk TV'ye yönelik soruşturmanın doğrudan yayın içerikleriyle ilgili olmadığını, buna rağmen yayınların durdurulduğunu söyledi.


“Biz haberin serbest dolaşımını istiyoruz ve sizler gibi değerli meslektaşlarımızın, üyelerimizin görevlerini yapabilir olmasını istiyoruz.”


“Bu yaptığınız şey bir yumruk sıkmaktır”


Yayına katılan gazeteci Zafer Arapkirli de yeni girişimi basın üzerindeki baskılara karşı bir dayanışma örneği olarak değerlendirdi.


“Bu yaptığınız şey bir yumruk sıkmaktır Gökhan. Yani baskıya karşı, istibdata karşı, faşizme karşı, bağımsız medyanın gırtlağını sıkmaya çalışan o kötü güçlere karşı bir yumruk sıkmaktır.”


Arapkirli, bağımsız haberciliğin farklı mecralarda sürdürülmesi gerektiğini belirterek şöyle devam etti:


“Bugün Halk Televizyonu, öbür gün başka bir kanal, başka bir gün başka bir kanal.”


Serhan Asker ise Halk TV'de yaptığı programların izleyicilerle kurduğu ilişkiye dikkat çekti. Kayyım sonrasında eski programlarının yayımlanmaya devam ettiğini, buna karşılık çalışanların iş ve sosyal haklarına ilişkin sorunların çözülemediğini söyledi.


“Yani işten çıktık, haklı fesihle ihtar gönderdik. Görüşelim, konuşalım diyoruz. Bir görüşme iklimi de bulamadık ne yazık ki.”


İlk yayında 100 bin abone


Açılış yayını sırasında kanalın YouTube abone sayısı hızla yükseldi. Yayının başlangıcında yaklaşık 39 bin olarak açıklanan sayı, programın üçüncü saatini geçmesinin ardından 100 bine ulaştı.


Kayış, yayın sırasında izleyicilere teşekkür ederken yeni platformun yalnızca bir gelir kaynağı olarak görülmemesi gerektiğini söyledi:


“Gerçekten vazgeçmememizin sebebi memleket meselesi. Sadece gelir kapısı olarak bakmıyoruz.”


Halk Televizyonu ekibi, haber ve programlarını YouTube ile sosyal medya hesapları üzerinden sürdürmeyi hedefliyor.


(AEK)

title: Even Hegseth’s Former Chief of Staff Says It’s Time for Him to Be Ousted
content:
The secretary’s former top aide blasted the Iran war as a “shitshow.”

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s former chief of staff has said that the secretary should resign over his handling of the Iran war and internal Pentagon affairs, adding to calls for Hegseth’s ousting after he narrowly survived an impeachment attempt earlier this month.

In an interview with Politico, former top Hegseth aide Joe Kasper said that the secretary has become obsessed with his ego and image, as well as his mission to drastically remake the Pentagon in his violent, white supremacist image. Hegseth’s focus on boosting himself and his “showmanship” are getting in the way of his “ability to be effective,” Kasper said.

Kasper, who was Hegseth’s chief of staff for the first three months of President Donald Trump’s current term, rattled off a list of what he feels are Hegseth’s failures. For one, the U.S. war on Iran, in which the U.S. has killed thousands of civilians in Iran, has been a “shitshow,” he said — a popular view even among some Republicans in Congress and in the administration.

The Iran War was a major focus of Rep. Thomas Massie’s (R-Kentucky) impeachment attempt earlier this month. Massie’s articles accused Hegseth of violating the law in waging the war without Congress’s approval while violating civilian protection laws both in strikes on Iran and in the U.S.’s boat strike campaign.

Massie’s impeachment articles narrowly failed, after several Democrats missed the vote, but Democrats are preparing to target him again when they take over Congress.

Meanwhile, Kasper also criticized Hegseth for gutting top leadership at the Pentagon, seemingly specifically targeting senior Black and female figures in the military.

“At almost every high-profile position, or every senior leader position, there’s a vacancy,” he said.

Those fired included three top Pentagon officials who were dismissed last year, during Kasper’s time in the Pentagon, over supposed leaks to the media. Kasper said there was no evidence that those officials had ever leaked any information at all — and Hegseth recently subjected dozens of members of the Joint Staff to polygraph tests in order to seek out more alleged leakers.

Interestingly, Kasper seems to have been personally involved in those three officials’ ousting, even though he now says that there was no evidence of leaks. Last year, Politico reported that Kasper was a major player in their dismissals, done in “an attempt to consolidate power.” Kasper denied that claim, which came from sources familiar with the matter.

Kasper departed the Pentagon shortly after those dismissals, without any public bad blood between him and Hegseth, who sang his praises after he left.

Kasper also criticized Hegseth for a recent incident in which Hegseth and his staff were reprimanded for laughing at a Veterans Day ceremony at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier; “distractions” like his testosterone testing and supplement initiative; and his inability to work with other figures on Capitol Hill, like those in Congress.

“He’s not just burned bridges up on the Hill,” Kasper said. “He’s napalmed them.”

He predicted that Hegseth is going to be ousted in one way or the other. “He’s going to be suffocated, and it’s not like it’s going to be a slow suffocation. It’s going to be a quick asphyxiation.”

author: Christopher Read
title: Letters from 1914 reveal worry that Shoal Lake water rights would cripple Winnipeg aqueduct
content:
A century-old exchange of letters between senior government officials is at the heart of a $2 billion lawsuit alleging Indigenous water rights were sacrificed to ensure Winnipeg could draw its drinking water from

Shoal Lake

.


In 1914, Ontario deputy minister of lands, forests and mines Aubrey White warned federal Indian Affairs deputy superintendent general Duncan Campbell Scott that honouring existing legislative commitments to First Nations could “cripple” Winnipeg’s proposed aqueduct project.


The letters were uncovered by a historian hired by lawyer Julian Falconer’s firm.


“Completely out of sight of the First Nations, completely in secret, the deputy minister in a letter that we now have, says, if we follow through on this it would cripple, and that’s the word he used, cripple the Winnipeg water project,” says Falconer.


Falconer’s firm is representing Iskatewizaagegan (Shoal Lake) No. 39 Independent First Nation in litigation heading to trial against the City of Winnipeg and Ontario.


A statement of claim filed in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice in 2024, alleges ecological, cultural and financial impacts resulting from Winnipeg’s aqueduct intake in Shoal Lake and seeks $2 billion in damages.


In a letter responding to White’s warning, Scott agrees that White has raised “important” points, but recommends that “we should say nothing about water or fisheries, but leave those questions to be decided as the cases arise.”


The following year, Ontario passed legislation that in effect eliminated the issue White had raised concerns about. The legislation governed reserve lands in Treaty 3 territory, and removed a provision from an 1894 agreement between Ontario and Canada that had recognized certain waters and lakebeds between projecting headlands as part of First Nations reserves.


Lawyer Julian Falconer at a presentation for Shoal Lake No.39 citizens. Photo: Christopher Read/APTN.


In its statement of defence, the city of Winnipeg denies Ontario altered the law for Winnipeg’s benefit, arguing the changes arose from a separate dispute.


The lawsuit also points to a provision in a 1913 Ontario Order in Council approving  Winnipeg’s Shoal Lake aqueduct that requires compensation be made to “all private parties whose lands or properties may be taken, injuriously affected or in any way interfered with.”


In 2019, before filing Shoal Lake 39’s lawsuit, Falconer asked the court for a ruling on whether the provision applied to the First Nation.


“We applied to a court to ask a simple question: Does Iskatewizaagegan number 39 constitute a private party for the purposes of this compensation provision? The court answered yes,” says Falconer.


The ruling did not determine whether Winnipeg is liable for the damages the First Nation alleges.


Winnipeg acknowledges the compensation provision exists but denies causing the damage alleged.


In its statement of defence, the city says other dams and overfishing are responsible for many of the environmental changes Shoal Lake 39 has identified.


Not so, says Shoal Lake 39 Chief Gerald Lewis.


According to Lewis, the aqueduct intake doesn’t just take in water.


“It also includes fish, and the fish eggs,” says Lewis.


Iskatewizaagegan litigation committee chair Rachel Green at the edge of Shoal Lake. Photo: Christopher Read/APTN.


For Iskatewizaagegan citizen Rachel Green, the lawsuit is also an opportunity to reclaim a history she believes has been largely told by others.


She’s the chair of her community’s litigation committee and a graduate student writing a master’s thesis at the University of Winnipeg. Her research is closely tied to Falconer’s team’s investigation into how Winnipeg’s aqueduct project came to be.


“My whole motivation for doing this research is because the Iskatewizaagegan water issue, our story, has only been told from the perspective of the government, a colonial perspective, and has never, ever been told from our perspective,” says Green.


Her concern about the issue is also rooted in deeply held beliefs about the water of Shoal Lake.


“When it comes to the water coming to Winnipeg from Shoal Lake, it’s used as a commodity, as a source to make revenue from,” says Green, “whereas us that are from Shoal Lake, having that spiritual bond and connection to the water, water is a relative.”


She is alluding to Winnipeg’s practice of diverting dividends generated by its water utility to subsidize the city’s general revenue.

title: Elektronik belge uygulamalarında yeni düzenleme Resmi Gazete'de

Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı (GİB) tarafından hazırlanan "Vergi Usul Kanunu Genel Tebliği'nde Değişiklik Yapılmasına Dair Tebliğ" Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı.

"Bilgi Fişi" tanımını yürürlükten kaldıran düzenleme, e-Arşiv Fatura uygulamasına dahil olmayan mükelleflere yeni belge düzenleme seçenekleri sundu. Bu mükellefler, 1 Ocak 2027'den itibaren faturalarını Güvenli Mobil Ödeme ve Elektronik Belge Yönetim Sistemi, Taksi Mali Cihazlar veya izin verilen Yeni Nesil Ödeme Kaydedici Cihazlar (YN ÖKC) üzerinden e-Arşiv Fatura olarak düzenleyebilecek.

Yerli ve yabancı film gösteren sinema işletmeleri, belirlenen usul ve esaslar doğrultusunda e-Bilet uygulamasına geçerek giriş biletlerini elektronik ortamda düzenlemek zorunda olacak.

İlgili bölümün başlığı, sinema işletmelerinin e-Bilet kullanma zorunluluğunu esas alacak şekilde değiştirildi. Yeni nesil ödeme kaydedici cihazlardan düzenlenen e-Bilet bilgi fişi ve aylık satış raporuna ilişkin ifadeler kaldırıldı.

e-Bilette eğlence vergisine ilişkin bölümde de bilgi fişleri ve aylık satış raporlarına yönelik atıflar çıkarıldı.

Elektronik belge düzenlenmesine izin verilen yeni nesil ödeme kaydedici cihazların arızalanması veya çalınması, kağıt belge düzenlenebilecek durumlar arasına alındı.

Bu imkânın kullanılabilmesi için arıza veya hırsızlık durumunun ispatlanması ya da belgelendirilmesi gerekecek.

Serbest meslek faaliyeti yürüten hekimlerden, e-Serbest Meslek Makbuzu uygulamasına dahil olan ve 593 sıra numaralı tebliğ kapsamında bu makbuzu düzenleyen yeni nesil ödeme kaydedici cihaz kullananlar, cihazlarını iş yerlerinde bulundurmaları şartıyla POS cihazlarını bulundurmak ve kullanmak zorunda olmayacak.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Christian Ferrer: A Testimonial
content:
The World’s Grand Guffaw


Diego Sztulwark


Lobo Suelto

, 22/11/2026


The very recent death of Christian Ferrer deepens our affection for him and allows us to revisit a host of conversations, readings and moments with a sense of gratitude. It is not a bad place to start: the nobility of the sentiments from which one thinks and writes — his rejection of resentment and bad faith — was a decisive matter for him.


Like so many other students at the Faculty of Social Sciences at the University of Buenos Aires (UBA) in the 1990s, I first learnt of Christian through the magazine

El Ojo Mocho

. Those of us who were not studying Communication—and were therefore not his students—came into contact with him through his articles, rather than through that soft, measured tone with which he captivated endless cohorts of students. As a student activist in the mid-1990s, I did not have any particular fondness for him. Although I read his work with keen curiosity, I was drawn to that libertarian streak (please, let’s not get sidetracked by the infamous connotations of that little word; we’re being serious here) and his penchant for all manner of strange objects.


One summer in the second half of the 1990s – I can’t remember whether it was ’96 or ’97 – I bumped into

Horacio González

 and Christian on a lovely beach in Rocha, Uruguay: Punta del Diablo. I’d just started as a teaching assistant in

Rubén Dri

’s philosophy department, and I was racing against the clock, reading Hegel as much as I possibly could. One afternoon, Horacio and Christian, who were strolling along while arguing, came into the cabin where I was studying. One of the topics of their dispute was the university. Horacio, with a sardonic tone, was of the view that one should not consider the university in terms of admission or assessment criteria, and made mocking remarks such as “with anarchists, you always end up discussing order”. On one of those days, Christian advised me to abandon my utopian attempts to understand Kant and Hegel and to devote my efforts instead to reading Nietzsche. His work was more vital. It’s not a question, he said, of learning theoretical systems, but of having real conversations with genuinely provocative, powerful interlocutors. I tried to ignore him, but I failed.


In a sense, it was always like that with Christian. Whenever I tried to get closer to him, to share my concerns with him in militant language, I found myself faced with someone who, while listening, would lay down his own conditions: “Where you say “politics”, I hear “power””. He wasn’t interested in militant ideology, but he was interested in the country, Argentina, and history, the world. He could talk about that with great erudition, for hours on end. In that sense, listening to Christian was a learning experience. I tried to ignore his political anarchism, but – once again – I failed. Not because it made me change course, no. But it did create the conditions within me to become an attentive reader of his ideas. A reader, in the sense of needing to weigh up my own thoughts against his. A few days ago,

Santiago López Petit

 was in Buenos Aires, reminding us that it is one thing to “engage in politics”, and quite another to “lead a political life”. The essence of the critique, which I admired in Christian, ran from the latter to the former. The weight of that distinction does not create a political system, but it does create a certain—undoubtedly virtuous—way of being. Having read Osvaldo Bayer and Gilles Deleuze, I never had any doubts about the appeal of the great libertarian ethic, nor about the superiority of what some philosophers call “ontological anarchism”: constituent praxis, set against a backdrop of a non-hierarchical nature.


But with Christian, one could not talk about theory. On one occasion he invited me to write something for a faculty journal that he edited. I think it was around 2001. He said to me, mockingly: “Write about political theory; I know nothing about that”. It was not, of course, that he was ignorant of theory; the matter simply made him sarcastic. His readings of Schopenhauer, Benjamin, Debord, Foucault and Deleuze were more incisive than many of the systematisations of those theories that are in circulation (the repetition of the conceptual system must have seemed to him like a way of thinking that was alien, not his own). Quite simply, he had no interest—for radical, profound reasons—in that realm. His reasons were set out at …

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: ICE Arrests at Airports Ahead of Holiday Draw Condemnation From Lawmakers
content:
Recent footage of ICE abducting people at a Seattle airport is “horrific” and “chilling,” said Gov. Bob Ferguson.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has abducted multiple people from airports ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday, sparking outrage among onlookers and renewed calls for the agency to be abolished.

This past weekend, masked ICE agents arrested two people on an airport jet bridge in Seattle as passengers boarded a flight to Los Angeles. Video of the arrests, which has gone viral on social media, shows multiple ICE agents dragging a passenger before restraining her, handcuffing her, and pulling her off of the jet bridge. As the arrest is taking place, the woman desperately cries out that she and her father are in the U.S. on work permits. Other passengers scream in horror and attempt to intervene — demanding that the masked agents identify themselves and show warrants — only to be shoved by agents.

The two arrested were later identified as Sofia Larrondo Hernandez Mejia and her father, Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, who is a Mexican national. A lawyer representing them stated that they were on their way to a family baptism.

Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson (D) described the footage as “horrific” and “chilling,” stating that ICE “is beyond reform” and echoing calls for the agency to be abolished.

“ICE is completely and totally out of control. Like many Americans, I’m outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities,” Ferguson said in a statement.

The November 21 incident sparked a protest at the Seattle airport on Sunday, with demonstrators calling for the abolition of ICE.

The abductions come following a separate incident on November 19, when ICE arrested a Princeton University PhD student in D.C.’s Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport as she was returning from presenting her research at a conference.

Eva Yi Xie, a third-year neuroscience student, came to the U.S. with her parents from China as a child in 2016 and has had a pending asylum application for a decade. According to her lawyer, Xie had a court date scheduled for January 2028, and a valid work permit.

ICE detained Xie in a holding center in Virginia before moving her to an immigrant jail elsewhere in the state. On Friday, a federal judge ordered ICE not to move Xie out of Virginia, and to respond to her lawyer’s petition for habeas corpus, which stated that ICE had no grounds to arrest Xie without a warrant.

In 2020, after being named a finalist in a prestigious high school research competition, Xie wrote that her parents “were compelled to flee to America to seek refuge after being politically persecuted.”

According to the Amica Center for Immigrant Rights, at least five people, including Xie, have been detained by ICE at Virginia’s Dulles and Reagan National airports in recent weeks.

This summer, ICE expanded its arrests at airports, increasingly coordinating and sharing information with TSA and targeting travelers on domestic flights — not those with deportation orders as previously targeted, but often people with expired visas or pending asylum applications. Throughout the summer, ICE arrests at airports averaged 20 to 40 per day. At the time, immigrant rights groups had advised individuals without permanent status to reconsider taking domestic flights.

Last week, prior to the recent abductions, Democratic Senators Jacky Rosen (Nevada) and Alex Padilla (California) introduced a bill to limit ICE operations at airports. The legislation would prevent ICE agents from accessing passenger data without a warrant and require ICE to notify airlines and airports ahead of their arrests.

“ICE is out of control, and these are bare minimum standards for reining it in,” said Padilla.

According to The Guardian, ICE’s arrests at airports are part of its shift in strategy from “blitzes” in major cities — like the Trump administration’s Operation Metro Surge in Minnesota — to a quieter but seemingly equally violent approach. The agency is still arresting and detaining people in record numbers, but is focused on conducting more stealthy and rapid arrests, in order to evade public pushback.

author: Cody Bloomfield
title: New Indictments of Michigan Palestine Activists Are Troubling – and Flimsy
content:
Prosecutors’ use of conspiracy charges resembles the attacks on anti-ICE protesters and Stop Cop City activists.

Prosecutors’ use of conspiracy charges resembles the attacks on anti-ICE protesters and Stop Cop City activists.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

In Donald Trump’s National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 (NSPM-7), the president set his sights on uprooting left-wing movements for liberation. What is obvious in the 14 months since the issuance of NSPM-7 is that the Trump administration has thus far failed: People continue to resist ICE, protest police brutality, and hold fast to criticisms of the U.S. national project.

But where the Trump administration has seen its campaign of widescale disruption falter, prosecutors have reached for increasingly attenuated theories of criminal liability to ensnare expanding cross-sections of the movement. On October 30, U.S. Attorneys unsealed a superseding indictment adding four defendants to a prosecution of pro-Palestine activists over the vandalism of University of Michigan campus officials’ homes and businesses with pro-divestment messages.

While the original defendants stand accused of holding the spray paint cans, none of the new defendants are charged with participating directly in the vandalism. Instead, they are charged with playing support roles, including media coordination and logistics planning. By sprawling the indictment into charges against activists accused of no substantive crime — merely conspiracy — federal prosecutors appear to be attempting to instill the type of fear capable of corroding a movement.

The superseding indictment is notable for what it omits: allegations that the new defendants were direct participants in the vandalism. Two defendants are accused of editing a Cryptpad document with a public statement. Federal prosecutors charged another defendant because he discussed locations to meet to plan an action. Still another activist’s alleged participation in the conspiracy is limited to operating a publicly-accessible police scanner. Charging conspiracy allows prosecutors to impose collective liability: Any of the new defendants could be found guilty of conspiracy to transmit interstate threats without ever a need to prove that they personally engaged in any criminal act. (In addition to the conspiracy to transmit interstate threats charges, one defendant also picked up a destruction of property to prevent seizure charge for allegedly removing the target of a search warrant from Signal chats.)

In the opinion of National Lawyers Guild Executive Director Xavier de Janon, the prosecution bears the hallmarks of NSPM-7, adding to the ranks of pending protest cases that include prosecutions of ICE protesters in Minnesota and Stop Cop City activists in Atlanta. In the first NSPM-7 case to secure a conviction, eight Prairieland protesters were convicted at trial of providing material support for terrorism after one protester nonfatally shot a police officer during a noise demonstration at an ICE detention center.

“U.S. Attorney Gorgon said that these alleged threats and attempts to terrorize government officials, businesses, and the Jewish Federation are anti-American. This so-called anti-American ideology is all over the NSPM-7 counterterrorism memorandum, and the topic of the prosecution — a free Palestine — matches its priorities,” said de Janon.

It marks an unusual escalation for federal prosecutors to take an interest in a local protest case. Most of the thousands of people arrested during campus protests against the genocide in Palestine faced minor charges in state court, or no charges at all. One of the defendants added to the indictment, Henry Mackeen-Shapiro, initially faced a state-level felony charge for resisting a police officer and a misdemeanor charge for trespassing. Both charges were dismissed in 2025.

De Janon raised the possibility that the federal charges are retaliatory. Two of the 12 defendants, including one of the newly added defendants, sued University of Michigan officials, alleging that the university violated their First Amendment rights by firing them following their participation in pro-Palestine protests.

“It’s very suspicious that the indictment came after the lawsuit,” said de Janon, noting that the lawsuit survived motions to dismiss.

Another possibility is the connection to Unity of Fields, formerly known as Palestine …

author: Amy Goodman
title: European Union Was Not a Climate Champion at COP31, Activists Say
content:
The EU may have balked at fossil fuels’ absence from the final text, but they obstructed progress on climate finance.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The United Nations climate summit in Turkey, known as COP31, collapsed on Sunday after nations failed to reach an agreement on a new climate deal. A number of countries opposed the final draft because it made no mention of fossil fuels. Many poorer countries also objected to the lack of financial commitments from richer nations to assist them in adapting to the climate crisis.

“This is not about the Global South begging for assistance and help,” says Filipino climate activist Lidy Nacpil. “The principle is that [wealthy nations] have created this problem, and they have to contribute to the solutions.”

“What we’ve seen over the past decades is the Global North are not delivering on any of their responsibilities,” says Brandon Wu, director of policy and campaigns at ActionAid USA. “That’s what’s causing the deadlock. It’s not new to this COP, but it’s becoming increasingly untenable.”

We also speak with two other leading climate justice advocates who attended COP31, Tasneem Essop of Climate Action Network International and Kathy Jetn̄il-Kijiner, climate envoy of the Marshall Islands.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now!, democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report. I’m Amy Goodman, back in New York.

In Turkey, the United Nations climate summit collapsed Sunday after nations failed to reach an agreement on a new climate deal as the Earth warms. The European Union and a number of countries opposed the final draft because it made no mention of fossil fuels. The effort to strip the text of references to coal, oil and gas was led by Saudi Arabia and joined by Russia. The United States did not participate in COP31.

This is Kathy Jetn̄il-Kijiner, the climate envoy for the Marshall Islands.

KATHY JETN̄IL-KIJINER: The Republic of the Marshall Islands objects to the adoption of the CMA text and cannot join consensus. We came to Antalya to honor our commitment to the Paris Agreement and to do what we promised our people back home. We face an inevitable overshoot of 1.5. We came here expecting the world to deliver a comprehensive and urgent response on reducing emissions, on protecting our people and on providing the finance to do this. We have been let down on all sides. We were presented with the worst possible response to overshoot: a response to enhance oil and gas. We will not be forced to accept false solutions. We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests. We will not accept an outcome that undermines our security and threatens our future.

AMY GOODMAN: Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien outlined the European Union’s opposition to the final text.

DARRAGH O’BRIEN: At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short. We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach. We will not endorse a cover decision or an Antalya pact that does not even mention fossil fuels, which is the key driver of climate change. And we will not accept negotiating backward in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel.

AMY GOODMAN: Over the weekend, climate justice activists rallied against the final text. On Friday, a Malaysian climate activist, Amalen Sathananthar, was detained after interrupting the closing plenary. He stood on a table holding a red noose around his neck and wearing a shirt that read, “You are killing the future.”

AMALEN SATHANANTHAR: You are killing the future! You are killing the future! Why don’t you just kill me now? The climate crisis is killing! … There’s no money! Just kill me now! The Global South can’t wait! The Global South can’t wait for this! And yet you just keep doing nothing, nothing at all! Racists! Kill me now! Kill me now! Kill me now! Kill me now! … You are killing the future! You are killing the future! You are killing the future! You are killing the future!

AMY GOODMAN: We are joined now by three leading climate justice …

title: Öcalan: Peace process must be strengthened through democratic law and free politics
content:
Abdullah Öcalan described the Peace and Democratic Society Process as a historic turning point and warned against attempts to obstruct political developments through provocations and anti-democratic interventions. In a new message, the Kurdish leader emphasized that the transition to a new phase can succeed only by strengthening democratic legal frameworks and ensuring freedom of political activity. He also underscored the importance of a Democratic Republic in which Kurds are legally recognized as an equal and constituent part of society.


The message was released following a visit by the Imrali delegation of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) on Sunday and reads in full as follows:


"On November 22, 2026, we, the Imrali delegation, held a meeting with Mr. Abdullah Öcalan on Imrali Island. As was publicly announced last month, we were able to confirm that Mr. Öcalan had been transferred to a newly constructed section within the prison complex. This development is clearly a positive step in terms of his working and living conditions.


The next step is to establish the necessary channels of communication to enable Mr. Öcalan to personally present to the press and the public, in its entirety, the extensive work he has undertaken over the past two years on the historic bonds between Turks and Kurds and the pursuit of peace between them.


At the current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, the bodies envisaged under the framework legislation must begin their work, and the necessary legal foundations must be established. Mr. Öcalan is determined to further intensify his efforts during this phase in his capacity as coordinator for peace and political participation. Mr. Öcalan’s assessments during the meeting can be summarized as follows:


We stand at a threshold


“We stand at a threshold of great practical significance, one that will mark a turning point in the history of the Republic. Crossing this threshold and entering a new phase requires both intensive, multifaceted intellectual engagement and effort, as well as an awareness of the dangers that exist.


Politics in Turkey must not remain trapped in a cycle of pressure, provocation, and reaction. If this cycle obstructs the political sphere in Turkey, there is a serious risk of creating conditions in which anti-democratic forces can gain ground, as they have done throughout the history of the Republic. The primary targets of such forces are always those working for peace and democracy, particularly the Kurds. To this end, they seek to destroy the social and political space.


Since this process, which we are advancing with great care, holds far-reaching potential for fundamental change in the country and the region, various centers of power will repeatedly attempt to intervene with destructive plans. The most effective way to counter such attempts is to strengthen the process through democratic law and free politics.


The Kurdish question is a question of democracy


I regard the Kurdish question as a question of democracy. A historic initiative to resolve such a question serves the interests of all political and social groups in Turkey. It runs counter, however, to racist ideologies and aspirations for a coup.


Democratic politics cannot be conducted solely on the basis of day-to-day political developments and relationships. It requires a coherent program of principles and an approach grounded in shared values. The political sphere must demonstrate its capacity to foster democracy.


Justice, the rule of law, and democracy are not demands of the Kurds alone, but of the entire people of Turkey. The Kurds stand for peace and fraternity and are prepared to embrace the Republic without reservation.


The participation of Kurds in the Republic can be realized on a secure democratic foundation. Such a republic can flourish by recognizing all identities. Those who hold a narrow understanding of the Republic and object to this approach operate according to the logic: “Better to keep it small, as long as it belongs to me.” The Democratic Republic, by contrast, will strengthen Turkey and make it a model for others.


Rights violations in prisons are a provocation against the process


In light of these far-reaching goals, certain conditions that currently prevail can neither be explained nor justified. In particular, deaths in prisons, the obstruction of prisoners’ release, and the differing practices in correctional facilities …

title: Bakırhan: Silopi's future lies in clean solar energy, not coal
content:
Tuncer Bakırhan, Co-Chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), participated in a march against the thermal power plant in Silopi (Silopiya), a district of Şırnak (Şirnex), as part of the “Budget for Bread, Peace and Justice” campaign. Bakırhan said that the plant's operations were causing environmental pollution and health problems and called for its closure.


Bakırhan claimed that 4,000 people had died of cancer in Silopi since the plant began operating in 2009, adding that cases of cancer, asthma, premature births and miscarriages had increased in the region.


Bakırhan said that ash and toxic substances from the plant were contaminating the air, water and agricultural land, while authorities had failed to respond to questions about health data.


Bakırhan demanded the appointment of an independent scientific committee to assess pollution caused by the plant and examine soil, water and agricultural products. He said that the plant's operating licence should not be renewed, and its activities should be terminated.


Criticising tree cutting, mining and energy projects in the region, Bakırhan said that Mount Cudi and the surrounding natural areas must be protected. He also pointed out that young people in Silopi were being forced to migrate because of unemployment and demanded investments that would create jobs instead of a thermal power plant.


Bakırhan said, “Silopi's future does not lie in coal or thermal power plants. It lies in clean solar energy,” and adding that energy policies must prioritise public health and the environment.


Bakırhan said that the destruction of nature was incompatible with the peace process: “Destroying nature, destroying water and issuing licences that lead to people being poisoned are, in fact, another form of war. This must come to an end. Hopefully, Mount Cudi, which protected Noah's Ark from the flood, will once again protect its own people. And its people will protect Cudi, the Hezil River, their rivers, water and plains. We hope that one day we will free our lands from these thermal power plants, geothermal power plants (GPPs), hydroelectric power plants (HPPs), solar power plants (SPPs), and the profit-driven mentality that grants licences over streams and rivers, poisoning our land.”

title: Kezban Doğan: Collective struggle against femicide is essential - Part Two
content:
As activities continue in Germany to mark 25 November, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, the Kurdish Women's Movement has launched a new campaign to strengthen the collective struggle against femicide. The preparatory phase, running from 1 November to 8 March, aims to reach different sections of society through training sessions, seminars, panels, demonstrations and other activities.


Kezban Doğan, term spokesperson for the Kurdish Women's Union in Germany (YJK-E), said that treating femicides solely as individual crimes obscures the underlying causes of the problem.


The first part of this feature can be found

here

.


'Femicide is a social problem'


Kezban Doğan stressed that femicide and violence against women are fundamentally social problems. Doğan said: "This is neither solely a women's problem nor solely a men's problem. If society does not consist of just one gender, then solving this problem requires the democratisation of both genders and the development of awareness among women and men alike. People need to be shown how they can live more peacefully, calmly, happily and joyfully. Only in this way can change and transformation be achieved."


Doğan said that responsibility for femicide could not be limited to the individual who committed physical violence, but must also extend to the system that produces the mentality behind it. She noted that women struggle to escape violent environments and access support mechanisms.


Doğan also said: "As a people, we often look at the issue this way: Whoever holds the knife is the murderer. But there is no questioning of the mentality itself. Nor is there any political questioning. We need to question that mentality, the system that gives men this understanding, lays out that path before them, directs them against women and causes them to commit violence. Yet women struggle to find a way out of violent environments. They cannot access support mechanisms and are often left helpless in these circumstances."


'Conditions in women's shelters create difficulties'


Kezban Doğan also drew attention to the problems faced by women seeking safety in German women's shelters with their children, stressing that age restrictions for boys made decisions particularly difficult for mothers.


Doğan said: "Suppose a woman finds a way out, but she is a mother with children. She must then meet the conditions of the shelter. For example, she cannot take her 12-year-old son with her to a women's shelter. As you know, a mother's emotions can unfortunately also prevent her from taking action in such situations because mothers tend to act more emotionally during these processes.


Suppose her application is accepted. There is an age limit of 11 for boys, while no such age restriction applies to girls. Normally, the state keeps the woman's location confidential. But what does the man do? There is an institution called Jugendamt, the Youth Welfare Office. He goes there and says that his children have psychological problems, that he cannot see them and that he wants contact with them. Based on his application and requests, this institution may disclose the woman's location to her husband. In effect, it paves the way for the woman to be killed, placing all the means to reach her in the man's hands."


'The obligations of the Istanbul Convention are not being fulfilled'


Kezban Doğan recalled that Germany was among the first countries to sign the Istanbul Convention, but said that its obligations had still not been implemented despite the years that had passed. She also criticised what she described as inadequate sentences for femicide and violence against women.


Doğan said: "Germany has the Istanbul Convention. Germany was one of the first countries to sign it. Yet years have passed since the convention was signed. Despite this, the obligations and conditions it contains are only now beginning to be discussed in the state parliaments outside the federal parliament. We need to look at how many women have been killed and how many have experienced violence in Germany since the convention was signed.


When we look at the sentences imposed, we do not see particularly severe punishments. On the contrary, sentences are considerably reduced. The punishments imposed on murderers are almost indulgent. When such gaps exist, it becomes possible for a man who is frustrated or unable to resolve his own problems to turn directly to killing women, committing femicide …

title: Peace Mother Nezahat Teke: We will fight for peace until the end
content:
Although each Peace Mother in Kurdistan has a different story of how she joined the struggle, the reasons that bring them together are shared. Mothers whose lives have been transformed by the state's policies of repression and violence, and who have lost their children in the struggle, are now carrying forward their children's legacy and raising their demands for peace. Nezahat Teke, one of the Peace Mothers who has struggled for 26 years to ensure that other mothers do not experience the same suffering, dedicated her life to the struggle for peace following the martyrdom of her daughter.


Nesrin Teke, the Amed (Diyarbakır) bureau representative of Özgür Halk magazine, set herself on fire on 9 July 2000 as part of the "You Cannot Darken Our Sun" protests and fell as a martyr on 11 July in the hospital where she was receiving treatment. Nezahat Teke decided to join the struggle following her daughter's martyrdom and spoke to ANF about those days.


 


Nezahat Teke said: "We were witnessing everything. But there is nothing as painful as experiencing suffering in your own home, within your own family, especially when it involves your own child," and recalling how her daughter became involved in the struggle: "Nesrin was going to school. One day, when Nesrin came home, I emptied her schoolbag to wash the collar of her school uniform. I found some magazines. One of them had a photograph of Leyla Qasim on its cover. There were also copies of Diriliş and Medya Güneşi magazines. I said to Nesrin, 'You're going to school, so why are you carrying these around? You're still young. You should finish your education.' Nesrin replied, 'If I don't start now, if I don't begin to understand things, my mind will be empty when I grow up.'


At that time, people were being taken away and held in custody for 25 days. I told my daughter, 'You're too young. Don't do this. We could also suffer because of you.' Nesrin turned to me and said, 'When you grow up a little, you'll understand these things better.' Today, I understand everything, and I've realised that this is what growing up really means."


Nesrin had prepared her mother for the struggle for peace


Nezahat Teke recalled a conversation with her daughter Nesrin about the peace bus travelling from Istanbul to Amed: "The peace bus was coming from Istanbul to Batıkent. That evening, Nesrin told me, 'Finish your work early. Let's go and see the peace bus together.' I replied, 'Why should I go? What would I do there?' My daughter said, 'They are mothers just like you.' I told Nesrin, 'They have given their children to the struggle and suffered oppression and persecution.' Nesrin replied, 'How do you know you won't experience the same thing?' We went to see them the next morning. Nesrin said, 'Look how wonderful these mothers are, how courageous they are.' I wondered whether my daughter wanted me to do something too. Nesrin wanted me to take to the streets so that people would not die."


From four mothers to hundreds


The martyrdom of Nesrin Teke on 11 July 2000 marked the beginning of a new chapter in Nezahat Teke's life. Following her daughter's martyrdom, Nezahat Teke joined the struggle for peace and helped establish the Peace Mothers' Assembly in Amed alongside Sakine Arat, Azize Yiğit and Dilşah Özgen.


Nezahat Teke said that the Peace Mothers now have 24 assemblies and dozens of members, stressing that they will never abandon their struggle for peace. She described their aims and determination: "We set out to build a democratic country. Of course, there will be difficulties. But our eyes are fixed on a brighter future. We are not asking for anything bad. We are struggling for peace, for our mother tongue and for a future where mothers no longer weep. Today, when you walk through the mountains of Kurdistan, beneath every tree and in every piece of land lie the bones of mothers' children. There are unmarked graves, mass graves and unsolved killings. Despite all this, even if we have only one hour left to live, we will continue our struggle for peace."


The most severe form of violence


Being a Peace Mother in Kurdistan means becoming a direct target of state repression. Nezahat Teke has struggled for peace for 26 years and has been detained repeatedly during this period. One of the most difficult experiences Nezahat Teke endured was spending 11 months under house arrest. Her sons, Mazlum and Tîrej, were also in prison at the time. title: Dozens of skulls and bones discovered in a three-level cave in Silvan
content:
Numerous human skulls and bones have been discovered in a remote cave in the Silvan district of the Kurdish province of Amed (Diyarbakır). During an investigation, representatives of human rights organizations came across remains in the multi-level cave that may belong to several dozen people. Some of the skulls show damage that could indicate gunshot wounds. The identities of the deceased, the causes of their deaths, and when they died remain unknown.


The cave is located between the villages of Boşat and Çîçika in a forested mountainous area and is known locally as the “Ecnebi Cave.” After the Human Rights Association (IHD) received a report about the discovery of bones, its Amed branch, the Amed Bar Association, and the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) formed a joint delegation. The Mezopotamya News Agency (MA) accompanied the investigation on November 19 and documented the findings at the site.


Hundreds of bones in a multi-level cave system


The entrance to the cave is located on a forested mountaintop, approximately 45 to 50 minutes on foot from the village of Çîçika. It is so narrow that only one person at a time can descend into it using a rope. The cave consists of at least three levels and is estimated to extend 50 meters underground. In the upper section, the team discovered several skulls and bones among the rubble. On the level below, which was completely dark, they encountered a far greater concentration of remains.


According to MA, approximately 15 to 20 skulls and hundreds of other bones were scattered across different locations on this level. Some of the unusually small skulls may belong to children. Several skulls had openings that may have been caused by gunfire, while others were fractured or severely damaged. Numerous remains were also found beneath rocks and in natural crevices.


On the second level, the reporting team also documented blackened stones and bones bearing what appeared to be burn marks. It has not yet been possible to determine whether these were caused by fire or an explosion. According to the journalists, one striking detail was that no clothing was found in any of the areas examined.


A member of the delegation also managed to reach the particularly narrow third level, where further bones were found. It remains unclear whether additional sections of the cave lie beneath this level.


“It was as though we were in a cave of death”


Fırat Akdeniz, a member of the IHD’s Commission on the Disappeared in Amed, was among those who descended into the cave. He described his impressions to MA: “The entrance to the cave is dangerous. We managed to descend only with great difficulty. On the second level, we found even more human bones. It was darker, and the smell was very strong. We saw far more human remains there than we had expected.”


According to Akdeniz, some of the bones may still be buried underground. The delegation was unable to determine either the number of deceased or their identities. “It was a painful and tragic sight. From the first level to the third, it was as though we were in a cave of death. It appeared as if people had been deliberately brought here, from conflict zones or civilian areas, and executed. We could not establish the exact number.”


Whether the cave was actually used as an execution site has yet to be established. A forensic examination of the remains is still pending.


Memories of the crimes of the 1990s


The discovery takes on particular significance against the backdrop of numerous extrajudicial executions and cases of enforced disappearance committed in Silvan and other parts of Kurdistan, particularly during the 1990s. Among those linked to these crimes are JITEM, a clandestine state intelligence and gendarmerie organization, and the Kurdish-Turkish Hezbollah, known as “Hizbulkontra,” which operated as a counterinsurgency force against the Kurdish freedom movement.


Whether the newly discovered remains date back to this period remains unclear. Following their investigation, members of the human rights delegation suggested that the bones might date from a relatively more recent period.


Akdeniz also referred to the Turkish military sieges and curfews imposed on Kurdish cities in 2015 and 2016. Reports of serious human rights violations repeatedly emerged from the areas sealed off at the time. “Our concern is that we will be confronted with more such disturbing findings,” the human rights activist said.
