author: Unknown
title: Women from Eastern Kurdistan demand legal equality
content:
In a statement issued on the occasion of November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, the Peace Mothers in Eastern Kurdistan drew attention to the human rights violations faced by women around the world.


Emphasizing women’s rights to freedom, independence, and decision-making, the statement said that crimes and murders committed against women in Iran stem from discriminatory laws, patriarchal attitudes, and the indifference of the authorities.


It noted that, decades after the murder of the Mirabal sisters, gender-based violence continues and perpetrators of crimes committed in the name of “honor” continue to escape punishment.


The statement pointed out that fathers, brothers, and husbands are involved in acts of violence against women, including cases of self-immolation and armed attacks, and identified legal inequality and patriarchal relations as the underlying causes of persistent systemic discrimination.


Criticizing the laws of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the statement pointed out that legal restrictions imposed on women in matters such as family life, marriage, divorce, child custody, and personal independence are among the primary factors perpetuating violence against women.


The statement further highlighted the lack of safe living spaces for women, specialized support centers, independent legal and psychological services, and economic opportunities.


Stressing the need to end femicide, the statement emphasized that the government’s responsibility does not begin only after crimes have been committed and that the necessary preventive measures must be taken.

author: Unknown
title: Guerrillas: Kurdish people recognized their existence with the founding of the PKK
content:
Through 48 years of resistance, the PKK (Kurdistan Workers’ Party) has made significant gains and brought the Kurdish people onto the stage of history. It has brought the Kurdish people’s right to freedom to international attention. Heavy sacrifices have been made in this struggle, and many people regarded as heroes have given their lives. Each of them has become part of the Kurdish people’s legacy of a life in freedom. Thousands of young people headed for the mountains of Kurdistan to embrace the cause and waged a determined struggle despite immense difficulties.


Today, the struggle of the Apoist Movement under the leadership of Abdullah Öcalan has achieved success. On the occasion of the 48th anniversary of the PKK’s founding on November 27, 1978, guerrillas from the HPG (People’s Defense Forces) and YJA Star (Free Women’s Troops) shared their views with ANF.


Bahar Goyî: Millions of people embraced the PKK movement


YJA Star guerrilla Bahar Goyî began by celebrating November 27, saying: “This day is very important to us. When our movement was founded, Kurds, Turks, and Arabs were part of it, and many other peoples also lent their support. The struggle of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] had an impact on all peoples. Comrade Haki Karer is an example of this. He was Leader Apo’s hidden spirit. To honor the memory of Comrade Haki, Leader Apo founded the PKK in the village of Fîs in Amed (tr: Diyarbakır) in 1978. After its founding, the PKK spread throughout Kurdistan and across the world. Millions of people embraced the movement, and thousands of young people headed for the mountains of Kurdistan. Thousands of heroic young people who spearheaded the struggle for freedom embraced martyrdom with great courage. Today, our people are turning out in large numbers to honor the comrades whose martyrdom has recently been announced and to keep their legacy alive. This is deeply meaningful and valuable to us.”


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/54921811_20261119103421_2026-11-21-behdinan-bahar-goyi-gerilaya-yja-star-bi-avabuna-pkk-hebuna-xwe-naskir-1.mp4


The YJA Star guerrilla continued: “Honoring our martyrs means standing by Leader Apo. We are truly happy when we see our people honoring their martyrs. This is a sacred stance. It also demonstrates how deeply committed we are to our Leader. At present, our primary concern is securing Leader Apo’s physical freedom. To achieve this, we must take our martyrs as our example. If we follow in their footsteps, we will make significant gains. When we achieve a free and shared life, we will dedicate it to our people and our Leader. Whether the process moves forward or not, we will continue to stand by our Leader and our martyrs. On this basis, we will carry on our struggle with great enthusiasm.”


Dilgeş Farqîn: The attacks and oppression brought us closer to the PKK movement


HPG guerrilla Dilgeş Farqîn stated that enemy forces had established control over Kurdistan and the Kurdish people had been subjected to genocidal attacks before the founding of the PKK.


Dilgeş Farqîn said: “The occupying forces were attacking the Kurdish people with extreme brutality. Tens of thousands of Kurds were killed in these attacks. All the social and cultural values of the Kurdish people were being destroyed. At that time, many established Kurdish organizations approached the Kurdish people’s cause with fear. However, with the emergence of Leader Apo, the darkness imposed on the Kurdish people was overcome. Leader Apo recognized the need to establish a Kurdish movement. For this reason, he founded the PKK movement in 1978. I consider myself very fortunate to have come to know this movement."


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/d524cddc_20261119154002_2026-11-21-behdinan-dilges-farqin-gerilaye-hpg-bi-avabuna-pkk-hebuna-xwe-naskir-1.mp4


The HPG guerrilla continued: "The attacks and oppression brought us closer to the PKK movement. The acts of heroism we witnessed before our eyes had a profound impact on both me and the society in which I lived. This influence led me to join the PKK Movement. Today, I am proud to be part of such a movement. At its core, the PKK is a movement of revenge. Following the martyrdom of Comrade Haki, the PKK continued its struggle in a spirit of revenge. Leader Apo inspired many heroes who went on to write epic chapters in the PKK’s history. As Leader Apo himself has said, the PKK has fulfilled its historical role. In particular, it has achieved significant …

author: Unknown
title: Remains of PKK guerrilla Celal Gök returned to his family after nine years
content:
PKK member Celal Gök (Nom de Guerre: Rüstem Serhed) lost his life in a clash in Dersim in 2017. His body was buried at the time in the Seyrantepe Cemetery for the Nameless in the Tuşba district of Van.


His family, who had traveled to Van and provided DNA samples shortly after receiving news of his death, were informed that a DNA match had been confirmed nine years later.


Following the notification, the family traveled to Van and received their son’s remains together with representatives of the Van branch of MEBYA-DER (Association for Solidarity and Assistance with Families Who Have Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations).


The remains were received with chants of “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs are immortal). In a brief speech at the gathering, Gök’s elder brother, Güven Gök, extended his condolences to PKK founder Abdullah Öcalan and the people of Kurdistan.


Celal Gök’s remains were then taken to his home village of Rüstem Gedik (Kopa), in the Korkut district of Muş, for burial.

author: Unknown
title: Doctor tells prisoner with cancer: “Go back to prison and wait to die”
content:
Evin Zapsu, a prisoner diagnosed with stage-four cancer, was reportedly subjected to inhumane treatment by a doctor during a medical examination at Kayseri City Hospital. According to her family, the doctor told her: “Your cancer has spread throughout your body. Go back to prison and wait to die.”


Zapsu is being held at Kayseri-Bünyan Closed Women’s Prison. She was diagnosed with stage-four cancer on November 16. Four days later, on November 20, she was taken to the gynecologic oncology department of Kayseri City Hospital for treatment. A medical report was issued there stating that she was no longer fit to remain in prison.


During her weekly phone call with her family, Zapsu recounted the treating doctor’s remarks. Her husband, Mecit Zapsu, reacted with outrage. He said that a doctor’s duty, particularly when treating a seriously ill patient, was to stand by and support her rather than confront her with such statements. “We do not accept such an attitude,” he said. The family announced that they would file a criminal complaint against the doctor over the incident.


Evin Zapsu was imprisoned in December 2016 amid a political crackdown on the Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) in the southern city of Mersin. She was sentenced to 15 years in prison on charges of “membership in a terrorist organization.” The mother of three was initially held at Bakırköy Women’s Prison in Istanbul before being transferred to Kayseri.

author: Unknown
title: Koçyiğit: Prison administrations act as though there is no peace process
content:
Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit, Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), criticized the ongoing rights violations in Turkish prisons. At a press conference in parliament in Ankara, she accused the relevant authorities of ignoring developments in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. “Prison administrations are operating entirely independently of this process. It is as though there has been no Peace and Democratic Society Process in this country for the past two years,” Koçyiğit said.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/20f92c94_20261123140019_2026-11-23-ankara-gulistan-kilic-kocgun-cezaevi-idareleri-surecten-bagimsiz-yuryor_1.mp4


Seriously ill prisoners denied adequate treatment


The DEM Party politician drew attention to the cases of Evin Zapsu, Newroz Bozkurt, Devrim Ayık, Fatma Toprak, and Emrah Nebioğlu, whose health conditions are a cause for serious concern. She said that these prisoners continued to face difficulties obtaining adequate medical treatment despite suffering from severe illnesses. Zapsu, who is being held at Kayseri-Bünyan Women’s Prison, was diagnosed with stage-four cancer on November 16. On November 20, a hospital determined that she was unfit to remain in prison.


Koçyiğit also criticized practices such as conducting medical examinations while prisoners are in handcuffs and carrying out searches of their mouths. She noted that the Ministry of Justice and the General Directorate of Prisons and Detention Houses have left inquiries concerning these rights violations unanswered. Referring to Tuncay Sağlam, who recently died in custody, Koçyiğit recalled the state’s obligation to protect the right to life. “Families of seriously ill prisoners are now protesting outside the Ministry of Justice and demanding concrete measures,” the politician said.


Call for implementation of the peace law


Regarding the next political steps, Koçyiğit stated that the DEM Party expected the parliamentary monitoring committee to be established and begin its work soon. At the upcoming meeting of the National Security Council, she said, a decision must be made to officially verify and acknowledge the steps taken by the Kurdish side in the peace process. “We reiterate our expectation that this decision will also pave the way for the implementation of the law adopted on August 10 with overwhelming support. It must be brought into force swiftly, without further delay. The verification and confirmation phase must also be completed promptly.”


Allow journalists to visit Imrali


Responding to questions about possible visits by journalists to Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan on the prison island of Imrali, Koçyiğit stated that no names had yet been finalized. “We expect media professionals to be able to travel to the island as soon as possible. At the same time, the Committee for Peace and Political Participation must be announced without delay. Conditions must be established that allow journalists and other individuals to visit the island. However, no specific names have been determined so far. At least, we have received no information to that effect.”

author: Unknown
title: International conference in Belfast: Ending armed conflict does not constitute peace
content:
An international conference titled “Combating Impunity, Memorialisation, and Transitional Justice Under Threat” has begun in Belfast, the capital of Northern Ireland, bringing together human rights defenders, legal professionals, academics, and representatives of international institutions from around the world.


The two-day conference, held at Riddel Hall at Queen’s University Belfast, is jointly organized by the Northern Ireland-based Committee on the Administration of Justice (CAJ), the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), and Queen’s University Belfast.


The conference addresses conflict and peace processes in various regions, particularly Northern Ireland, South Africa, Argentina, Colombia, Brazil, Ukraine, the Basque Country, and Kurdistan, as well as human rights violations committed by states in the past, policies of impunity, the pursuit of truth, and the preservation of collective memory.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/b2e7a3da_20261123162236_2026-11-23-belfast-baris-ve-adalet-konferansi-catismazlik-tek-basina-baris-degil-1.mp4


UN Special Rapporteur and international human rights defenders also in attendance


The event opened with a speech by Professor Matthew Moran, Director of the Institute for Peace, Security and Justice at Queen’s University Belfast, followed by a presentation on the conference’s objectives by Daniel Holder, Director of the Committee on the Administration of Justice (CAJ) and Vice-President of FIDH. Among the prominent participants is Bernard Duhaime, the United Nations (UN) Special Rapporteur on the promotion of truth, justice, reparation and guarantees of non-recurrence.


Other participants include María José Guembe, President of CELS, from Argentina; Luís Guillermo Pérez Casas, former Secretary-General of FIDH, from Colombia; South African human rights lawyer Kayan Leung; former UN Special Rapporteur Professor Fionnuala Ní Aoláin; Professor Kieran McEvoy, an expert on peace and transitional justice; Chief Constable of the Police Service of Northern Ireland Jon Boutcher; and Kurdish lawyer Reyhan Yalçındağ Baydemir, former Vice-President of the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH).


The conference, which also brings together representatives of the UK government, addressed the threats to human rights gains posed by the rise of far-right and populist movements, impunity for state crimes, efforts to establish the fate of missing persons, and the pursuit of justice in post-conflict societies.


Human rights violations in Kurdistan and the peace process discussed


Speaking at the session titled “Transitional Justice Processes Under Threat,” moderated by Dr. Brian Dooley, Reyhan Yalçındağ discussed the peace process in Turkey and the historical background of the Kurdish question. Emphasizing that ending armed conflict does not, in itself, constitute peace, Yalçındağ stated that lasting peace could only be achieved by constitutionally guaranteeing fundamental rights and freedoms and confronting serious crimes committed in the past.


Drawing attention to human rights violations committed in Kurdistan during the 1990s, including enforced disappearances, torture, extrajudicial executions, and the burning of villages, Yalçındağ stressed the need to establish mechanisms for truth and justice. She stated that the failure to investigate past crimes perpetuates impunity, adding: “Confronting the past is not an obstacle to peace; on the contrary, it is a fundamental prerequisite for peace.”


‘Peace must be advanced through concrete steps toward democratization’


Reyhan Yalçındağ noted that the steps taken in the peace process were important but insufficient, emphasizing the need to enshrine the fundamental rights of Kurds in the constitution and remove obstacles to participation in democratic politics. Criticizing the continued operations against journalists, the imprisonment of seriously ill prisoners, and the appointment of state trustees to replace elected mayors, Yalçındağ stated that peace must not be limited to political declarations but must be advanced through concrete steps toward democratization.


Drawing attention to the role of women in the peace process, Yalçındağ stated that the Kurdish women’s movement should not merely support the process but should be a direct participant and a driving force in shaping it. author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump, With Tens of Millions Invested in Nvidia, Told Board to Reinstate Huang
content:
The reinstatement of the disgraced CEO has sent Nvidia’s stock roaring back, rising 30 percent.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

President Donald Trump personally intervened to get the disgraced Jensen Huang to be reinstated as CEO of Nvidia on Monday — in turn, sending the company’s stock and, potentially, Trump’s personal portfolio soaring.

The tech company’s board announced that Huang has been reinstated immediately after members made the decision at a meeting on Monday, less than 10 days after he resigned in disgrace. The board directly cited the U.S. government’s involvement in the decision, saying that the board “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.”

The reference to “senior levels” of the government appears to refer at least in part to Trump, who spent Monday morning boasting about his role in the decision.

In an interview with CNBC, Trump said he “convinced them” and “made the deal” for the board to reinstate Huang. He said that Huang, accused of having an affair with a woman with alleged ties to Chinese intelligence and with two of his subordinates at the company, “did nothing wrong.”

“I’m very, very happy that the company had the courage and the board had the courage to do the right thing, and they suffered for two weeks, and the company suffered greatly,” Trump said.

Indeed, Nvidia’s stock has been falling for weeks since Huang’s affair with the alleged spy was first uncovered. But the stock surged as much as 36 percent on Monday after the board’s announcement, recovering a huge amount of the losses.

Congressional Democrats vowed to investigate the reinstatement when they take the majority. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-New York) said that the administration “will wield their full power to investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump Administration, Jensen Huang, other NVIDIA executives, and anyone selling out our national security for financial gain.”

This may well include Trump himself, who is under scrutiny for his trading activity in relation to Nvidia this year.

According to analyses of Trump’s financial disclosures, the president held between $13 million and $62 million in Nvidia stock as of the end of August. He may have far more, as he has made a huge amount of trades in the company this year; according to CNBC, his investment accounts bought or sold Nvidia stock at least 103 times as of August, involving stocks worth at least $27 million and up to $97 million.

The White House has repeatedly said that Trump does not personally manage his stocks, while he has refused to stop his prolific stock trading.

Trump and the White House celebrated Huang’s reinstatement, boasting about the president’s influence.

“President Trump was totally involved and this is a great decision by the NVIDIA board. We have to protect our geniuses,” said Steven Cheung, White House communications director, to Semafor.

Trump made several posts praising the decision on Truth Social, calling it “correct and proper” and saying that Jensen’s leadership will help “ensure the Success and Prosperity of not only the Company, but the American Economy.”

Trump also posted a seemingly AI-generated image mimicking the photo of himself raising his fist after his attempted assassination in 2024, but with a triumphant Huang, in front of an Nvidia flag in place of the U.S. flag, raising a fist clutching a bra.

Truthout is funded almost entirely by readers — that’s why we can speak truth to power and cut against the mainstream narrative. But independent journalists at Truthout face mounting political repression under Trump.

author: Julia Conley
title: 99 Percent of Gaza Is Polluted With Toxins Due to Israel’s Genocide, Report Says
content:
Oxfam found extensive toxic contamination throughout the strip’s air, soil, groundwater, and surface water.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

US government officials and commentators from both sides of the political aisle have insisted for years that Israel’s assault on Gaza is targeted at Hamas fighters and have bristled at accusations that Israel, with U.S. backing, is intentionally attempting to ethnically cleanse the exclave of Palestinians and make it uninhabitable for the population.

But one advocate for Palestinian rights said Monday that the “environmental war crimes” described in a new report on how Gaza’s air, soil, and water have become toxic due to more than three years of relentless bombing — despite a ceasefire deal reached last year — are “also known as genocide.”

The report by Oxfam International and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS) — titled “Environmental War Crimes: How Israel’s Military Assault Has Turned Gaza Into a Toxic Wasteland, Threatening Human Survival”—finds that while Israel’s military onslaught has directly impacted about 78% of Gaza’s land area, a spatial analysis identified indicators of potential contamination from heavy metals, residue from explosives, asbestos from destroyed buildings, dioxins, and biological contaminants across almost the entirety of Gaza — more than 99% of the exclave.

“Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza includes military assaults on its environment, which are environmental war crimes threatening life now and for generations to come,” said Amitabh Behar, executive director of Oxfam. “The destruction and contamination of Gaza will have fundamentally degraded the environmental conditions necessary for human safety and survival. This would breach Israel’s legal obligations under international humanitarian and human rights law.”

PRESS RELEASE: More than 99 per cent of #Gaza shows indicators of environmental contamination from Israel's military assault READ HERE: https://t.co/nIx81uPiPV pic.twitter.com/1k8QkTzMzU

The organizations used satellite imagery, remote sensing, scientific analysis, and other open-source data — including the United Nations Environment Program’s estimate that Israel’s U.S.-backed assault had generated more than 61 million tons of debris across Gaza — to build a comprehensive picture of the exclave’s contamination.

The highest levels of potential contamination were identified in Gaza City, Khan Younis, Rafah, Jabalia, and the Salah al-Din Road, which correspond closely “with the areas subjected to the most sustained bombardment, ground military operations, infrastructure destruction, and debris accumulation.”

The destruction of buildings, wastewater treatment facilities, industrial and energy facilities, and waste-management systems “has released a complex mixture of contaminants,” reads the report, including explosive residue, perchlorates, asbestos fibers, crystalline silica, persistent organic pollutants, and pathogens — all of which can then move through the air, soil, groundwater, and surface water.

“The population is likely to have been exposed to contaminants through multiple and interconnected pathways,” the report continues.

Contamination described in the report include:

Fecal coliforms, which indicate disease-causing pathogens in water, detected at a rate nearly 10 times more than that reported in 2021, with the coliforms found in 19% of 79 groundwater wells sampled across Gaza;

40,000m³ of raw sewage being pouring into the Mediterranean Sea each day due to the fact that only 19% of sewage pumping stations remain functional and 30% of the wastewater network is operational;

Heightened risks of long-term soil contamination in Beit Hanoun, Wadi Gaza, and the Khan Younis area due to their clay-rich soils — potentially threatening the safety of food crops when agricultural production resumes;

High risks of air contamination in Gaza City, Jabalia, and the North Gaza Governorateas pollutants from the intensive bombardment are resuspended due to vehicle movement and debris clearance;

High risks of drinking-water contamination in North Gaza, Gaza City, and Deir al-Balah, where remaining operational wells and desalination overlap with highly vulnerable groundwater systems and areas of heavy bombardment; and

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Man shot by police said he was ‘sick of life,’ coroner’s inquest hears
content:
The jury in a coroner’s inquest into the death of a 21-year-old Rankin Inlet man fatally shot by police in 2021 heard phone call recordings Monday in which the man said he was “sick of life” and wanted to end his life.


The recordings were from calls between Trey Angootealuk and Peter Crockford, the negotiator who called on the phone from Iqaluit in an attempt to de-escalate the situation.


In each call, Angootealuk swore at him before hanging up. In one call, he was heard saying that he wanted to die.


On Nov. 6, 2021, Angootealuk hijacked a truck and shot at officers in an area outside of town before he was fatally shot by police the next morning. The standoff lasted several hours.


The Ottawa Police Service, which investigated the shooting, later determined there were no grounds to believe any officer committed a crime.


The inquest by Nunavut Chief Coroner Marianna Cervantes will determine the circumstances surrounding Angootealuk’s death. It began Monday morning at the Siniktarvik Hotel and is scheduled to last until Friday.


Coroner’s inquests are mandatory under Nunavut law for all deaths involving an on-duty police officer. They do not determine the guilt or innocence of anyone involved.


Cody Autet, who was acting corporal of the detachment at the time, was among the officers Angootealuk shot at.


Autet testified that he saw Angootealuk hijack the truck, heard him scream “I can’t take this,” and witnessed his death.


The inquest’s first witness, former RCMP constable Kyle Amsel, described calling on Angootealuk multiple times to drop his gun before he entered the truck but did not receive a response.


“It was freezing cold,” Amsel, who was among the two officers who initially responded to the call, told the jury. “We thought he was just going to get cold and give up.”


He then watched from afar as Angootealuk shot toward police.


He said he was not present at the time of the fatal shooting, because his shift had ended.


Sixteen witnesses are expected to testify at the inquest, Jessi Casebeer, counsel for the chief coroner, told the jury.


Among them are RCMP officers, emergency response team members, and the investigator from the Ottawa Police Service.


Family members may also provide testimony, Casebeer said.


The inquest is scheduled to resume Tuesday at 9:30 a.m. CT.

author: Natalia Viana
title: Mais mulheres ministras, menos orgias no Supremo
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Xeque na Democracia, enviada toda segunda-feira, 12h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui.


“Cadê nossas norueguesas!? Rs”, “Vamos ter que mandar alguém lá buscar”, “Eu busco. Mande contato”. 


“Emprestei quarto do lado para ministro com 5 menina”. 


“Sobrou uma Ukraniana aqui. Gatinha. Vamos fazer a guerra no Brasil” “Eba. Nessa guerra tem que sobrar alguma refugiada pra mim”.


“Tipo gostosa! Vc conhece o q a gente gosta. Me manda as fotos. Tem q ser novidade.”


Todos esses diálogos foram proferidos por homens de poder da nossa República, ou seus assistentes mais fiéis. 


A primeira foi enviada pelo senador Irajá (PSD-TO), filho da ex-ministra da agricultura Kátia Abreu, logo depois de conhecer o banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro pessoalmente, em 11 de outubro de 2024. Segundo

reportagem

 de Lauro Jardim, seguiram-se um convite para uma viagem a Dubai e um camarote para o jogo Brasil X Colômbia no estádio Mané Garrincha, uma festinha em um imóvel de luxo em Saint Tropez, na França, e muito lobby pela aprovação de um PL que libera jogos de azar no Brasil, incluindo cassinos, bingos e jogos do bicho (Irajá é o relator). 


A segunda, pelo mordomo do banqueiro, após uma noitada preparada por ele em um triplex no Itaim Bibi na noite de 28 de fevereiro de 2025 para o ministro do STF Kássio Nunes,

detalhada

 pela revista Piauí. Vorcaro alistou dois motoristas, um chefe de cozinha, um mordomo e uma faxineira para a festa privada. Pagou R$10 mil para uma das cinco meninas. Cinco dias antes, Nunes Marques havia desempatado na Segunda Turma do STF um julgamento que ameaçava uma carteira de precatórios no valor de mais de R$10 bilhões do Master, pertencentes à destilaria Alcídia. 


O terceiro diálogo demonstra como Vorcaro tratava as “agenciadas” pela empresa do qual foi sócio oculto, segundo excelente

reportagem

 de Natália Portinari, do Uol. As jovens – de 19 anos para frente – eram chamadas de “creche” e “escravas” e usadas para “confiança e surubinha privê” junto com políticos e juízes ou para “eventos de volume” maiores, cujos convidados eram invariavelmente homens de poder. O ano era 2024; havia dois anos que o país da refugiada urcaniana de 19 anos estava em guerra e naquele ano morreram pelo menos 67 mil pessoas no conflito. A menina fugiu durante 14 horas de ônibus para sair do país, enquanto a mãe enviava áudios de bombardeios na sua cidade natal e pedia que ela não retornasse. 


O quarto recado foi escrito pelo então sócio do senador da República Flávio Bolsonaro a uma agenciadora quando tentava marcar uma “outra festinha igual a do grand hyatt”, que contaria com a presença do ex-candidato à presidência – o sócio o chamava de “meu filho”. As festinhas registradas na reportagem do PlatôBR ocorreram no começo de 2022 em um dos quartos mais privativos, cuja diária chega a cerca de R$3 mil, com varanda e vista panorâmica para a Lagoa de Marapendi. Flávio Bolsonaro era, na época, filho do presidente da República. 


Ao longo dos últimos meses, quem acompanha notícias teve o desprazer de ler repetidos conteúdos de teor semelhante, provenientes do celular do ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro ou de outros vazamentos, como o do ex-sócio de Flávio Bolsonaro.


A lambança do caso Master é tamanha – apenas na semana passada, relatórios da PF

detalharam

 relações do banqueiro com 4 ministros, 40% da corte – que a sua característica mais aberrante tem passado batido. Aquela que faz com que meu estômago embrulhe. 


Que faz com que 51,5% da população brasileira tenha nojo dos homens que nos governam.

 


Não exagero. Em grupos de discussão que participo, uma integrante mandou a seguinte proposição: “Eu tenho uma proposta de movimento cívico: nomear mulheres para o STF. Temos garantia que essa simples recomendação traria um retorno claro: diminuir as orgias envolvendo membros do Supremo.” A mensagem é absolutamente razoável, mas rendeu apenas alguns “kkk”s num grupo majoritariamente formado por homens; foi esquecida rapidamente. 


Ela vem do mesmo tipo de revolta que eu sinto, que muitas de nós sentimos durante este ciclo noticioso, ao perceber que, para os homens, o poder é associado a sexo, e sexo é associado a “ter”, “consumir” e “controlar” mulheres.

Não existe poder masculino, ainda hoje, dissociado do controle a corpos femininos. 


Mulher é propina. Buceta é propina. Buceta europeia é mais propina ainda.


E isso é tão …

Senator John Fetterman, one of Israel’s most uncompromising advocates in Congress, is facing a primary challenge from a Palestinian American writer born in Gaza.

Ahmed Moor had little name recognition when he launched his campaign for the U.S. Senate seat in Pennsylvania on November 9. But in less than two weeks, he has generated growing enthusiasm and acquired thousands of donations from across all 50 states, according to his campaign.

Moor says his Senate bid is motivated by the genocide in Gaza, but he stresses that the U.S. support for Israel’s atrocities in Palestine is a byproduct of “corruption” and the capture of public policy by special interest groups — a problem that ails all aspects of the U.S. political system. “My campaign is not only viable. “We’re running on anti-corruption,” Moor added. “We’ve seen that in America, people are highly, highly motivated by the idea of cleaning up our civics. We have the capacity for renewal in this country. That’s what my campaign is about.”

Moor’s candidacy for the 2028 Democratic Senate nomination in Pennsylvania follows a string of significant victories by pro-Palestine progressives this year, including the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the U.S. Senate in Michigan and Peggy Flanagan in Minnesota. Left-wing State Representative Chris Rabb was also elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in Moor’s hometown of Philadelphia.

As rejecting U.S. support for Israel transforms from a taboo to a widely accepted position in U.S. politics, more progressives seeking public office are centering the issue in their campaigns. And they are connecting Washington’s foreign policy to problems at home, including affordability, cruel immigration enforcement, and access to health care.

The U.S. war on Iran, which Donald Trump has launched jointly with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, has made the link between domestic and foreign policy more potent, further strengthening the argument of pro-Palestine progressives. The war, which saw Tehran restrict passage through the Strait of Hormuz, has sent energy prices spiraling and fueled inflation in the U.S. economy.

Moor told Truthout that the U.S. public does not want to be implicated “in the mass murder of children.” (Israel has killed more than 20,000 children in Gaza, according to local health authorities.) The Senate candidate added that Americans also care about the issue because “certain policy items contribute to the corrosion of American democracy and the diminishment of our quality of life over time.”

“The whole idea that there’s a foreign policy and a domestic policy is a mischaracterization of how things work,” he told Truthout. “There’s one budget and a funded line item here means something else isn’t getting funded elsewhere. For Moor, the unlimited campaign spending by special interest groups, such us the pro-Israel lobby group AIPAC (American Israel Public Affairs Committee), to pressure policy outcomes that they prefer is at the root of the problem. Moor also invoked the war with Iran.

“We’ve gone and funded a war for Benjamin Netanyahu in Iran, which has driven up the price of diesel, which has caused cascading inflation throughout our economy, which is making everybody who lives here poorer, the people of Pennsylvania poorer,” he said.

Fetterman, who has received public praise from AIPAC, has been one of the most outspoken supporters of Israel on Capitol Hill, regularly appearing on Fox News to defend the country’s leaders and attack its critics on the left. He has also voted against bills to rein in Trump’s power to continue the war with Iran and threatened to leave the Democratic Party over Israel. These positions appear to have alienated many voters. A recent Quinnipiac University poll suggested that only 13 percent of Democrats have a favorable opinion of the Democratic senator.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: DNC Mandates 2028 Presidential Hopefuls Reject Dark Money for Debate Eligibility
content:
Sen. Bernie Sanders celebrated the decision and called for it to be expanded to all Democratic primaries.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The Democratic National Committee (DNC) has announced that it is requiring 2028 presidential candidates to reject “dark money” spending in order to qualify for the primary debate stage, potentially taking a step toward reducing the impact of super PACs and billionaires on elections.

The committee said that it is planning to hold 12 debates over the course of the presidential primaries, with the first taking place in June and July of 2027, and the final one taking place in March 2028.

In order to qualify for these debates, the committee is requiring candidates to sign a pledge that bars campaigns from reaching out to super PACs or 501(c)(4) groups to solicit spending on their behalf. It also requires candidates to “denounce” such spending done to back them on television, radio, digital, billboard, or mail advertising if it was done without their knowledge.

Spending that is not by a 501(c)(4) special interest group or super PAC — which are two of the largest vehicles for outside spending — or spending on a “different form of media” is still allowed.

If a candidate violates those rules, they are barred from participating in debates until they’ve denounced, reimbursed, or terminated the spending, depending on the nature of the violation.

On its website, the DNC says that the primary goals of the pledge are to limit party spending during the primary elections in order to “avoid cannibalizing” such spending in a general election, as well as to “[l]imit the influence of dark money and outside spending in the Democratic presidential primary.”

“In the wake of the Citizens United Supreme Court decision, dark money and independent spending have exploded, increasing the influence of special interests in politics,” the committee wrote on its website. “While the DNC does not have the legal authority to ban super PACs or dark money groups, we are requiring our candidates to denounce their involvement in the Democratic presidential primary, in line with Democratic party values and our 2024 Platform, in order to qualify for the debate stage.”

The announcement of the Fair Campaign Practices Pledge represents a small step toward the longtime progressive call for the Democratic Party to ban super PAC and other outside spending in any of its primaries.

Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vermont), who has led these calls for years, celebrated the DNC’s announcement, while calling for the party to do much more.

“The DNC announced that 2028 presidential candidates must reject dark money and disavow Super PAC spending on their behalf. Excellent!” Sanders said in a post on social media. “Now let’s expand those restrictions to Democratic Senate and House primaries. Billionaires shouldn’t be able to buy our elections at ANY level.”

Outside spending played a major role in several races this election cycle, perhaps most notably in the bitter primary race between Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Michigan) and Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Michigan). Corporations and pro-Israel interests spent $60 million backing Stevens and opposing El-Sayed in the primary; AIPAC, through its super PAC, spent over $30 million in the primary, then turned around and gave millions to back El-Sayed’s Republican opponent in the general election.

Sanders has previously said that the Democrats must undertake a total ban on dark money spending in primary elections, while also calling for Congress to pass legislation to overturn Citizens United v. FEC, which has allowed billionaires and corporate interests to pour billions of dollars into influencing elections and candidates.

author: David Venn
title: Defence Department plans Iqaluit ‘engagement session’
content:
This week, the Department of National Defence plans to host a public engagement session in Iqaluit about its plans to build infrastructure to modernize Norad and to beef up Arctic defence.


The event is planned for 7 to 9 p.m. on Thursday at the cadet hall, media advisory from the department says.


Government officials will provide an overview of the forward operating location in Iqaluit and North American Aerospace Defence Command modernization plans. They will also answer residents’ questions.


Earlier this year, Prime Minister Mark Carney’s Liberal government made a flurry of funding announcements about military and Arctic defence spending.


In March, the prime minister visited Iqaluit to announce

$32 million

 to upgrade forward operating locations in Goose Bay, Inuvik, Iqaluit and Yellowknife. The work will include airfield improvements, new hangars, ammunition and fuel facilities, and warehouses.


Forward operating locations hold fighter aircraft and have storage facilities, maintenance buildings and airstrips. They are used to send aircraft into remote locations across the Arctic.


Iqaluit’s was built in the mid-1980s and features hangars for six jets, with accommodations for up to 200 support personnel.


In March 2025, Carney announced

$6 billion

 for Canada’s Arctic over-the-horizon radar system, part of the government’s plan to modernize NORAD.


The system is

being developed

 with Australia and defence contractor BAE Systems Australia. It will be able to detect targets hundreds of kilometres beyond the scope of conventional radar.


The federal government expects the project will add an estimated $290 million annually to Canada’s gross domestic product and about 2,270 jobs annually between 2026 and 2033.

author: Mag
title: Italiens Gewerkschaften gegen steigende Lebenshaltungskosten und Sparmaßnahmen der Meloni-Regierung
content:
Dossier


„

Menschen verbrennen öffentlich ihre Gas- und Stromrechnungen, Bäcker und Bauern gehen wegen der Preise auf die Straße. Die designierte Regierungschefin Meloni steht vor einem Berg an Problemen. (…) Nicht nur Italiens Agrarsektor protestiert. Kurz zuvor hatten auf Neapels zentraler Piazza del Plebiscito die Bäcker der umgebenden Region Kampanien demonstriert. Sie erwarten eine Verfünffachung des Brotpreises durch die hohen Energiekosten. Und die Bewegung „Wir zahlen nicht“ – italienische Variante des britischen Modell „Don’t pay UK“ – schaffte es am Montag, in fünfzehn Städten, darunter Turin, Mailand, Bologna und Rom, Demonstrationen auf die Beine zu stellen. Dabei wurden Strom- und Gasrechnungen verbrannt und zur eigenständigen „Preisminderung“ aufgerufen, sollte der Preisgalopp nicht anders aufzuhalten sein

…“

Artikel von Andrea Dernbach vom 06.10.2022 im Tagesspiegel online


 („

Bäcker, Bauern, Bürger – alle protestieren

„) – siehe die wachsene Streik- und Protestbewegung auch in 2023 und 2024 etc.:


Nicht alle der bis zu 1,5 Millionen protestierenden Arbeiter*innen und Jugendlichen in rund 100 Städten Italiens folgten am 20. November dem Aufruf der CGIL


Kleiner Generalstreik, große Proteste


„

In Italien legte der Gewerkschaftsbund CGIL seinen Ausstand auf den Protesttag der Studierenden – die marschierten lieber getrennt


Beim Generalstreik gegen den Haushalt der Regierung Meloni waren am Freitag mehr als eine Million Menschen in über hundert Städten auf der Straße, lautete die Erfolgsmeldung des größten italienischen Gewerkschaftsbunds CGIL. Die Zahlen klingen plausibel. Die Beteiligung am Streik selbst fiel erwartungsgemäß bescheidener aus. Wenn auch in Betrieben mit starken Gewerkschaften vielerorts die Produktion stand, etwa bei Electrolux in Treviso. Dass die Straßen voll waren, lag am europäischen Aktionstag der Schüler und Studierenden gegen Krieg und Aufrüstung. Seit Wochen werden in ganz Italien Hunderte Schulen immer wieder besetzt. Man könnte meinen, die Confederazione Generale Italiana del Lavoro hätte sich endlich den laufenden Kämpfen angeschlossen, um ihnen neuen Schwung und eine Perspektive zu geben. Tatsächlich aber zogen die Jugendlichen in Rom, Mailand, Bologna und allen größeren Städten getrennt von der CGIL durch die Straßen, oft sogar in ausdrücklicher Opposition zu ihr.


Warum, zeigt schon die Wahl des Streiktermins. Mitte Oktober legte die CGIL ihren Streik bewusst auf den Tag der europäischen Mobilisierung der Studierenden – obwohl die USB und andere Basisgewerkschaften bereits für den 30. Oktober zum Streik aufgerufen hatten. Der wurde ein großer Erfolg, die Beteiligung war wohl noch höher als am vergangenen Freitag. »Die USB ist zur Gewerkschaft geworden, die die Plätze füllt«, titelte Il Fatto Quotidiano, eine der großen Zeitungen des Landes. (…)


Die CGIL hätte diese Proteste unterstützen und sich dem Streik der Basisgewerkschaften anschließen können. Das aber wäre wohl zuviel verlangt gewesen. Sie zog es vor, die Proteste mit der Mobilisierung für den 20. November zu schwächen. Das passte zu ihrer Haltung bei den Transportblockaden: Sie sorgte sich um die Folgen für die Produktion und um die »Bürger als Verbraucher«. Später verurteilte sie Gewaltausbrüche und rief zu einer gemeinsamen Kundgebung mit den Institutionen der Stadt für den »sozialen Zusammenhalt« auf.


Verständlich also, dass die Studierendenbewegung sich der Vereinnahmung entziehen wollte. »Außerhalb und gegen« hieß es in der Erklärung, die Cambiare Rotta und andere Organisatoren des Aktionstags unterzeichnet hatten. Zumal sich bei der CGIL erwartungsgemäß die »befreundeten« Parteien einfanden: der Partito Democratico, der für »Rearm Europe« gestimmt hat, und seine Bündnispartner, die eine stärkere europäische Armee fordern. Das passt schlecht zu einer Bewegung, die sich offen gegen die NATO und jede Militärausgabe wendet.


Als wäre ihre Lage damit nicht schon schwierig genug, brachte die CGIL noch ihre eifrigsten Fürsprecher in Verlegenheit. Am 12. November unterzeichnete sie mit CISL, UIL, Confindustria und weiteren Unternehmerverbänden eine Vereinbarung über gewerkschaftliche Vertretung und Löhne. Als wäre die Schwierigkeit der Beschäftigten, ihre Interessen durchzusetzen, eine juristische Detailfrage, die sich im Einvernehmen mit Regierung und Unternehmern klären ließe.


Am Vorabend eines Streiks zur Verteidigung der Löhne traf die CGIL eine Vereinbarung zur Lohnregelung. Die Anpassung …

author: Aspen Ford
title: SpaceX Lab Workers Allegedly Dried Metal Part in Employee Breakroom Toaster Oven
content:
Elon Musk’s trillion-dollar company is fighting Washington state over three health violations and a $6,000 fine.

Elon Musk’s trillion-dollar company is fighting Washington state over three health violations and a $6,000 fine.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Elon Musk’s multitrillion-dollar company is fighting with Washington state over a $6,000 labor fine, fending off allegations of an unsafe workplace.

In November 2024, the Washington Department of Labor and Industries opened a chemical exposure investigation at the Redmond headquarters of Starlink, the division of SpaceX that makes satellites.

The state had received complaints stating the customer service department was connected to an engineering lab that didn’t have proper ventilations. Workers were experiencing eye irritation and headaches and dust was accumulating on their desks.

Unlike the lab workers, the customer service department didn’t wear protective equipment, according to a complaint. The two teams shared a breakroom.

The complaints weren’t news to SpaceX management. Customer service workers had filed dozens of internal complaints alleging chemical exposure symptoms that stemmed from an adjacent production lab. Management did not act until Labor and Industries opened its investigation, InvestigateWest reported.

The agency’s inspection took place in an unassuming office complex in Seattle-area suburbia. Tenants of the building included a pediatric clinic, a pediatric dentistry office, a “holistic” medical clinic, a mortgage lender and the Starlink customer service department, which adjoined two small Starlink labs.

After detecting a high level of lead on a work bench, the state issued SpaceX a violation and the $6,000 fine.

The department issued a second violation because SpaceX had not evaluated their employees’ potential exposure to chemicals. For that, there was no fine.

The third violation was unexpected.

In the middle of the investigation, a state compliance officer received multiple photos of a toaster oven. Cooking inside of it was a small piece of metal laying on top of aluminum foil. Workers feared anyone who used the toaster oven might have been exposed to harmful chemicals.

The officer issued a third violation for not keeping eating areas “safe and healthy.” No fine.

SpaceX is contesting all three violations. After Labor and Industries rejected the initial appeal, SpaceX appealed again.

The matter is now before a judge with the Board of Industrial Insurance Appeals, a quasi-judicial agency independent of Labor and Industries. Potential outcomes range from affirming the fine and the three violations to vacating them, with numerous variations in between.

On Nov. 18 and 19, during a trial-like hearing conducted over Zoom, SpaceX attorney Skylar Sherwood and Assistant Attorney General Diane Cornell examined witnesses familiar with the investigation. Judge Magda Baker presided.

Haley Laing, former SpaceX environmental health and safety manager who was subpoenaed for testimony, described the layout of the customer service department as a “very open space” with two labs conducting lead-based work adjoining one side.

The labs were former conference rooms. They had windows and the doors were not airtight. SpaceX did not post signage to caution workers that toxic substances were used inside, Laing said.

The state compliance officer, Richard Caldwell, was not permitted to photograph inside the labs; SpaceX had a contract with “DARPA,” the federal government’s Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, he said during testimony. To some employees, the labs were known as ‘Starshield,’ a type of satellite made for national security, InvestigateWest reported.

The labs’ proximity to the customer support department was supposed to be temporary; the compliance officer said he was told they would be moved to another site in 2025. It’s not clear whether that happened.

One lab was about the size of a storage closet, “probably 80 to 100 square feet,” Laing said. The other, “probably 250 square feet.” Inside, lab technicians cured parts in industrial ovens and assembled hardware onto circuit boards.

In December 2023, a year before the state investigated and prior to Laing’s employment, SpaceX safety employees reported a lab in the customer service building did not have “proper ventilation” for lead soldering and that lab workers had to “keep the door open.” They recommended …

author: infolibre
title: Οι συνδικαλιστικές Ενώσεις στα ΜΜΕ “βλογάνε τα γένια τους” και συνεργάζονται με το Μαξίμου
content:
Χωρίς κανέναν αγωνιστικό προσανατολισμό, χ

ωρίς καμιά απόφαση για απεργιακή διεκδίκηση συλλογικής σύμβασης εργασίας μετά από 17 χρόνια

που ο κλάδος παραμένει έρμαιο της εργοδοτικής και κυβερνητικής ασυδοσίας και χωρίς καμία συζήτηση για τα ουσιαστικά προβλήματα των εργαζόμενων που σε ιδιωτικά και δημόσια ΜΜΕ βιώνουν ένα καθεστώς εργασιακής γαλέρας και οικονομικής ένδειας – όπως έδειξε ακόμα και η έρευνα του ΙΝΕ ΓΣΕΕ – ολοκληρώθηκε άλλο ένα

Γενικό Συμβούλιο της ΠΟΕΣΥ στην Καλαμάτα παρουσία των προέδρων όλων των δημοσιογραφικών ενώσεων και των ασφαλιστικών ταμείων του κλάδου.


Αντίθετα περίσσεψαν οι δηλώσεις αυταρέσκειας των μεγάλων παρατάξεων που στηρίζονται από ΝΔ, ΠΑΣΟΚ, και διασπάσεις του πρώην ενιαίου ΣΥΡΙΖΑ

ότι όλα βαίνουν καλώς από μέρους τους, τα φληναφήματα με τον κυβερνητικό εντεταλμένο ΓΓ Επικοινωνίας και Ενημέρωσης,

στην κυβερνητική εκδήλωση για την «ασφάλεια» των δημοσιογράφων. Η Ημερίδα του Μαξίμου-με ομιλητή ανάμεσα σε άλλους και υπαστυνόμο της ΕΛΑΣ και παρουσία αστυνομικού διευθυντή- συνδιοργανώθηκε με δύο συνδικαλιστικές ενώσεις, την ΕΣΠΗΤ και την ΕΣΗΕΠΗΝ. Αυτό ντράπηκε να το ανακοινώσει επίσημα η ΠΟΕΣΥ, το ανακοίνωσε όμως η Γενική Γραμματεία με το δικό της δελτίο Τύπου. Φυσικά και ήταν σύμπασα η παρουσία των προέδρων.


Η πλειοψηφία που ελέγχει την ΠΟΕΣΥ φυσικά …δεν απέκλεισε απεργίες στο αόριστο μέλλον αλλά

καταψήφισε την πρόταση για συμμετοχή του κλάδου στην πανεργατική απεργία της 25ης Νοεμβρίου

 επικαλούμενη δήθεν την έλλειψη προετοιμασίας – κι ας έχει εξαγγελθεί εδώ και εβδομάδες– και προεξοφλώντας τα «χαμηλά ποσοστά στον κλάδο».


Οι τρεις εκλεγμένοι εκπρόσωποι του Μετώπου για την Ανατροπή στα ΜΜΕ

με την παρουσία και τις παρεμβάσεις τους αναφέρθηκαν στα κρίσιμα προβλήματα των κόσμου της εργασίας συνολικά αλλά και στα ΜΜΕ,

τους χαμηλούς μισθούς, τις σκληρές συνθήκες εργασίες και την ανάγκη ουσιαστικού και από τα κάτω οργανωμένου απεργιακού αγώνα για να σπάσει η αδιαλλαξία των εργοδοτών

– εκδοτών και ιδιοκτητών ΜΜΕ που είτε αρνούνται κάθε συζήτηση για ΣΣΕ είτε παίζουν «κρυφτούλι» επικαλούμενοι ότι δεν είναι… εργοδοτικές ενώσεις (όπως π.χ. η ΕΝΕΔ) και πως είναι εκτός δικαιοδοσίας τους η υπογραφή συμβάσεων.


Το “Μέτωπο για την Ανατροπή”(Πρωτοβουλία για την Ανατροπή/ΕΣΗΕΑ, Ασύνταχτος Τύπος/ΕΣΗΕΜΘ, Αριστερή Πρωτοβουλία για την Ανατροπή/ΕΣΠΗΤ, Ανένταχτοι αγωνιστές) κατέθεσε δύο ψηφίσματα,

ένα για τις ΣΣΕ με λογική αγώνα,

 γενικών συνελεύσεων και από τα κάτω απόφαση διεκδικητικού πλαισίου με ουσιαστικές αυξήσεις και μέτρα προάσπισης των εργασιακών δικαιωμάτων, ενώ ασκήθηκε έντονα κριτική στο ζήτημα του ΟΜΕΔ, ότι είναι όργανο του κράτους και όχι φιλοεργατικός οργανισμός, και ότι η προσφυγή σε αυτόν από τις ενώσεις του κλάδου είναι μια εύκολη φυγή όταν δεν επιλέγεται ο απεργιακός αγώνας διαρκείας με τον κλάδο προετοιμασμένο και αποφασισμένο για μια τέτοια μάχη, αν θέλει να ξανακερδίσει ΣΣΕ. Η πρότασή μας καταψηφίστηκε από τις κυρίαρχες παρατάξεις.


Την ίδια μέρα το απόγευμα πραγματοποιήθηκε εκδήλωση για τα 100 χρόνια ΕΣΗΕΠΗΝ…


Κατατέθηκε επίσης και ένα δεύτερο ψήφισμα για την πάλη κατά του πολέμου και του φασισμού και τη στάση των ΜΜΕ απέναντί τους, το οποίο υπερψηφίστηκε από την πλειοψηφία των συμβούλων.

[θα δημοσιευθεί σε άλλη ανάρτηση]


Το Μέτωπο για την Ανατροπή μαζί με τους συμβούλους της ΔΑΣ/ΠΑΜΕ ήταν οι μόνες παρατάξεις που ψήφισαν υπέρ της απεργίας στις 25 Νοέμβρη, πρόταση η οποία απορρίφθηκε από όλες τις άλλες παρατάξεις.


Την επόμενη ημέρα του ΓΣ της ΠΟΕΣΥ το Μέτωπο για την Ανατροπή έκανε παρέμβαση στην ημερίδα «Διαβούλευσης» για την «ασφάλεια των δημοσιογράφων» που διοργάνωση η ΓΓΕΕ σε συνεργασία με ΕΣΠΗΤ και ΕΣΗΕΠΗΝ, στον ίδιο ακριβώς χώρο διεξαγωγής του Γενικού Συμβουλίου, μοιράζοντας προκήρυξη με σύνθημα «

Δεν συζητάμε για την ασφάλειά μας με αυτούς που την απειλούν – Δημοσιογραφία στο πλάι της κοινωνίας και όχι της εξουσίας».


…και έκθεση αρχειακού υλικού εφημερίδων.


Στην παρέμβαση τους τονίζουν μεταξύ άλλων ότι «σε μία χώρα στην οποία η ασφάλεια των δημοσιογράφων και των εργαζομένων στα ΜΜΕ απειλείται από το ίδιο το κράτος, το οποίο επανειλημμένα έχει επιτεθεί φυσικά και ηθικά στους εκπροσώπους του κλάδου, οι Ενώσεις και η Ομοσπονδία μας επιλέγουν να αποδεχτούν ως βασικό συνομιλητή για το ζήτημα την… κυβέρνηση» και δηλώνοντας  «την κατηγορηματική μας αντίθεση με τη διεξαγωγή αυτής της ημερίδας με παρουσία των ενώσεων, και τονίζουμε ότι εάν η εργασία μας, η σωματική μας ακεραιότητα και η ασφάλειά μας απειλούνται από κάπου, δεν είναι από την κοινωνία, αλλά ακριβώς από …

title: Deutsche Bank financiou armamentos para Israel atacar Gaza
content:
Vazamento mostra escândalos de um dos maiores bancos do mundo. A

 Pública

 é o único parceiro no Brasil. Leia o especial

Inside Deutsche Bank


aqui.


Vazamento mostra escândalos de um dos maiores bancos do mundo. A

Inside Deutsche Bank


aqui.


Em janeiro de 2022, um comitê na sede do Deutsche Bank, em Frankfurt (Alemanha), se preparava para discutir se o banco deveria levar adiante operações que poderiam prejudicar sua reputação.


Na pauta da reunião de 12 de janeiro estava uma garantia de pagamento antecipado de 11,4 milhões de euros para a fabricante alemã de equipamentos de defesa Renk GmbH, destinada a financiar um contrato com o Ministério da Defesa de Israel, que se estenderia até 2027.


A Renk fabricaria caixas de transmissão para os tanques Merkava 4

, com a primeira entrega dos equipamentos prevista para setembro de 2024.


Um

documento

 que avaliava a operação estava nas mesas dos responsáveis pelas decisões do Deutsche Bank desde 16 de dezembro de 2021.


Entre os que apresentaram suas avaliações estava um dos advogados-gerais adjuntos do banco. Na sua opinião,

 a operação envolvia um “produto convencional de financiamento comercial, que, por si só, não apresenta nenhum risco reputacional relevante, segundo a RepRisk”.


Ele afirmou que

a probabilidade de a operação se tornar pública era “muito baixa”.

 Mas acrescentou que o risco seria ainda menor se as garantias de financiamento fossem emitidas por um banco israelense, em nome do Deutsche Bank.


As caixas de transmissão, acrescentou, não eram consideradas armamentos nos termos da Lei Alemã de Armas Militares, e a Renk obteria uma licença para exportá-las.


“Sou favorável à transação”, afirmou. A operação foi adiante.


Tanques contra civis


Dois anos depois, em janeiro de 2024, Hind Rajab, uma menina palestina de seis anos, estava ao telefone com os serviços de emergência, implorando para ser resgatada. Rajab e seis familiares tentavam fugir dos ataques israelenses em Gaza quando o carro em que viajavam foi alvejado. Naquele momento, ela era a única sobrevivente.


Após horas de negociações para garantir uma passagem segura, uma equipe de ambulância que seguia para resgatar a menina foi interceptada. O veículo levaria dias para chegar aos corpos dos socorristas, de Hind e de seus familiares. Ao todo, foram encontradas 335 marcas de bala no carro da família.


Inicialmente, o governo israelense afirmou que suas forças não estavam no local. Depois, alegou que as marcas de bala eram resultado de fogo cruzado. No entanto, uma

análise de imagens de satélite e gravações de áudio

 do incidente, realizada pela Forensic Architecture, grupo de pesquisa da Universidade de Londres, identificou apenas a presença das Forças de Defesa de Israel (IDF, na sigla em inglês) no local. 


Em petição apresentada ao Tribunal Penal Internacional em outubro de 2025, a Fundação Hind Rajab alegou que os tanques envolvidos eram do modelo Merkava 4. Um

projétil de tanque

 foi encontrado entre os destroços da ambulância da equipe que tentou resgatar Rajab.


Em 19 de agosto de 2026, mais de dois anos após o incidente,

as IDF

confirmaram

 que seus soldados haviam disparado contra o carro em que Hind Rajab estava e contra a ambulância de resgate.

As forças israelenses atribuíram os disparos a “falhas na coordenação do deslocamento da ambulância do Crescente Vermelho Palestino”, alegação contestada pela própria organização. As IDF afirmaram que abririam uma investigação criminal.


Esse não foi o primeiro episódio documentado de uso de Merkava — os principais tanques empregados em Gaza — contra civis desde janeiro de 2022, quando o comitê de revisão reputacional do banco deu seu aval à operação.


Entre os casos de maior repercussão envolvendo tanques Merkava estão o cerco ao hospital Al Shifa, em Gaza, em novembro de 2023, e o ataque fatal contra civis que aguardavam ajuda alimentar na rotatória de Al Tahliya, em junho de 2025, quando a fome em Gaza se agravava.

O episódio ocorreu cerca de nove meses após a data prevista para a entrega das novas caixas de transmissão fabricadas pela Renk e um mês depois de as IDF publicarem fotos das caixas de transmissão da empresa sendo preparadas para instalação.

author: James Crump
title: US Inflated Claims About Pro-Palestine Millionaire for Extradition Request
content:
The US Department of Justice (DoJ) has admitted that it altered evidence translated to Spanish in its attempts to have James ‘Fergie’ Chambers extradited.


The translation included a reference to fire that never happened, whilst in one instance “direct action” was changed to “direct violence”. 


The DoJ was forced to admit that it had changed the translation after the Guardian

reported

 on the issue. The Spanish authorities were notified midway through the extradition proceedings. 


Following the admission of errors by the DoJ, the pro-Palestinian activist and millionaire was released on conditional bail last Friday. 


“I think the fact that the US recognises what it has done shows that they were trying to fool the judges,” said Aitor Martínez, a member of Chambers’ defence team. “This should touch the pride of the Spanish justice system.”


Chambers faces charges of riot and conspiracy to riot in the US, relating to a protest outside an Elbit Systems site. He is also accused of laundering money and using the funds to support Hamas.


The request is the first known case of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas. Chambers has donated more than $1m to humanitarian causes in Gaza and paid legal fees for some members of Palestine Action, his lawyers say.


Speaking in front of Spanish prosecutors at the extradition hearing, Chambers denied having any links to Hamas. “I’ve never had any contact with any terrorist organisation, I’ve certainly never financed any terrorist organisation,” he said.


Chambers’ wife Stella Schnabel joined

Novara Live

 last week to discuss the case, saying that “there is zero evidence for their made up allegation that the money was used for anything but financing a soccer team in Tunisia.” She added: “This was a created charge to actually extradite him.”


At the hearing, Chambers spoke about the toll the extradition process has had on him and his family, telling the court: “My family has been torn apart. I missed my grandmother’s funeral last week.


“My five-year-old son asks where I am every day and my wife will give birth, God willing, in March and I don’t know if I will be by her side.”

title: Συγκέντρωση Αλληλεγγύης για τους/τις συλληφθέντες/είσες της πορείας στις 31/10, Τρίτη 24/11 στις 9:00 στα δικαστήρια Ευελπίδων
content:
Κάλεσμα για συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στα συλληφθέντα συντρόφια της πορείας μνήμης και αγώνα για τον αναρχικό σύντροφο Κυριάκο Ξυμητήρη και την υπόθεση των Αμπελοκήπων στις 31/10/2025


Την Παρασκευή 31 του Οκτώβρη καλέστηκε η Πανελλαδική πορεία μνήμης και αγώνα για τον αναρχικό σύντροφο Κυριάκο Ξυμητήρη και την υπόθεση των Αμπελοκήπων με την συμμετοχή σχεδόν 1.000 συντροφιών, της οικογένειας του Κυριάκου και τη στήριξη δεκάδων αναρχικών ομάδων. Με σημείο συγκέντρωσης τα Προπύλαια, το οργανωμένο και περιφρουρημένο μπλοκ στάθηκε πίσω από το πανό «Κυριάκος Ξυμητήρης Παρών στους αγώνες για την κοινωνική επανάσταση – Λευτεριά στα προφυλακισμένα συντρόφια» και πορεύτηκε στους κεντρικούς δρόμους της Αθήνας γεμίζοντας τους με τρικάκια και συνθήματα για την υπόθεση. Οι δυνάμεις καταστολής αν και εξ αρχής είχαν αναπτυχθεί πέριξ της πορείας με δεκάδες διμοιρίες των ΜΑΤ κράτησαν μια στάση αναμονής μέχρι το Σύνταγμα όταν και άρχισαν τις πρώτες προστριβές με συντρόφους, χωρίς ωστόσο να δημιουργηθεί μεγαλύτερη ένταση. Κατά την επιστροφή της πορείας και ενώ είχε επιλεχθεί αυτή να καταλήξει στο μνημείο της Μεσολογγίου παρατηρήσαμε κάτι σπάνιο για τις επιλογές της ΕΛ.ΑΣ. Με την είσοδο μας στα Εξάρχεια και τη στροφή του σώματος στην Μπενάκη, οι διμοιρίες πλησίασαν σε απόσταση αναπνοής, φόρεσαν τις μάσκες τους και ξεκίνησαν να απειλούν τον κόσμο. Σε δευτερόλεπτα χωρίς να έχει προηγηθεί οποιαδήποτε ένταση από την πλευρά μας, οι μπάτσοι επιτέθηκαν λυσσαλέα, με σκοπό να τραυματίσουν, τρομοκρατήσουν κυρίως και να συλλάβουν (σε μικρότερο βαθμό) όσο περισσότερους συντρόφους ήταν δυνατόν. Η μανιασμένη επίθεση τους με χτυπήματα, δακρυγόνα και κρότου λάμψης έγινε από όλες τις πλευρές με αποτέλεσμα το μεγαλύτερο μέρος της πορείας να εγκλωβιστεί στην οδό Μπενάκη και να προσπαθεί να φτάσει μέχρι την οδό Ακαδημίας όπου άλλες διμοιρίες επιτέθηκαν εκ νέου. Η περιφρούρηση προσπάθησε να αμυνθεί για λίγο και να δώσει χρόνο στους υπόλοιπους συντρόφους και συντρόφισσες να κατευθυνθούν προς τα Εξάρχεια. Οι καφρίλες των μπάτσων συνεχίστηκαν για αρκετές ώρες και μέσα στα Εξάρχεια με επιθέσεις στον πεζόδρομο της Μεσολλογίου και τους γύρω δρόμους σε περαστικούς, κατοίκους και συντρόφους. Δεκάδες αλληλέγγυοι χτυπήθηκαν με αρκετούς από αυτούς να καταλήξουν με ανοιγμένα κεφάλια και διασείσεις στο νοσοκομείο ενώ πραγματοποιήθηκαν και δεκάδες προσαγωγές. Το δόγμα της «μηδενικής ανοχής» συνεχίστηκε και έξω από τη ΓΑΔΑ όπου προσήχθησαν σύντροφοι/ισσες που προσέγγισαν την αντανακλαστική συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης. Πέντε εκ των αρχικών προσαγωγών, μετατράπηκαν σε συλλήψεις, με τις πλημελληματικού τύπου κατηγορίες να περιλαμβάνουν για όλα διατάραξη κοινής ειρήνης, βία κατά υπαλλήλων, νόμο περί όπλων, απόπειρα σωματικής βλάβης και κατά περίπτωση φθορά και τετελεσμένη σωματική βλάβη. Οι σύντροφοι αφέθηκαν κρατήθηκαν για 3 ημέρες στη ΓΑΔΑ και έπειτα αφέθηκαν ελεύθεροι. Οι κατηγορίες των συλληφθέντων είναι 5 πλημμελήματα στα τέσσερα άτομα και 4 στο ένα που είναι ανήλικο. Αξίζει να σημειωθεί ότι κατά την πρώτη ορισμένη δικάσιμο τον Μάρτιο του 2026 όταν και εν τέλει η δίκη αναβλήθηκε, οι μπάτσοι που είχαν προσέλθει ως μάρτυρες κατηγορίας ήταν ιδιαίτερα προκλητικοί ακόμη και απέναντι στην ίδια την οικογένεια του συντρόφου Κυριάκου.


Τα συντρόφια θα δικαστούν την Τρίτη 24/11 στις 9πμ στα δικαστήρια της πρώην σχολής Ευελπίδων.


Το σκηνικό έντασης που έστησαν οι μπάτσοι και το σημείο καθώς και ο βαθμός που επέλεξαν να μας επιτεθούν δεν μας προκαλεί εντύπωση. Είναι προφανές ότι η επιλογή τους να επιτεθούν εντός των Εξαρχείων είχε μια ξεκάθαρη πολιτική στόχευση μιας προληπτικής «εκκαθάρισης» της περιοχής, στέλνοντας ένα μήνυμα ενάντια στη ριζοσπαστικοποίηση της γειτονιάς και κάθε εξεγερσιακής συνθήκης. Η τεράστια δυναμική που φάνηκε να έχει το κίνημα αλληλεγγύης και τις δύο πρώτες ημέρες του τριημέρου μνήμης και αγώνα, θορύβησε το κράτος και με αυτόν τον τρόπο επέλεξε να του επιτεθεί, επιχειρώντας την τρομοκράτησή του. Οι μπάτσοι και οι πολιτικοί τους προϊστάμενοι δεν έχουν την ικανότητα να κατανοήσουν πως μέσα από αυτή τους την προσπάθεια, το μόνο που κατάφεραν είναι η συσπείρωση, η συνειδητή απόφαση για συνέχιση του αγώνα και το πείσμα για την Υπόθεση από ολόκληρο το κίνημα αλληλεγγύης. Έναν αγώνα για τον οποίο ο σύντροφός μας έδωσε την ίδια του τη ζωή και για τον οποίο άλλοι βρίσκονται πίσω από τα κάγκελα των φυλακών. Μια Υπόθεση που κόντρα στην ακραία καταστολή του κράτους, την καταδυνάστευση των ζωών μας από το καπιταλιστικό σύστημα και την ματαίωση από την ιδιώτευση, παραμένει …

author: dev
title: La bataille du futur a commencé
content:
Un mois après le 17 octobre, force est de constater que la stupeur qui a saisi les gouvernants comme tout le commentariat politique s'est passablement dissipée. Le

Comité pour le maintien du dix-sept octobre

 nous a transmis ses analyses quant aux forces qui, selon lui, ont concouru à ce que nous ne quittions finalement pas l'époque contemporaine. Depuis là, il propose les pistes nécessaires à l'avènement d'un 18 octobre.


Le 17 octobre, nous sommes sortis de l'impuissance qui nous condamnait à attendre passivement la séquence électorale du printemps prochain. Contre toute attente et contrairement à ceux qui nous gouvernent ou y aspirent, nous avons tenu notre promesse : nous nous sommes levés et nous avons opposé à la terreur policière l'insurrection la plus joyeuse et la plus joueuse que ce pays ait connue. Ce jour-là, les monstres étaient en uniforme et les héros en déguisement.


Que se passe-t-il ?


Nous voilà jetés dans une bataille

existentielle

. Les revendications ne suffisent plus à exprimer la rage et le désir de

s'arracher à

 ce monde. Aucun programme ne semble à la hauteur de cette

fin d'époque contemporaine

, et si certains prétendent incarner la rupture par les urnes, d'autres ont cherché à la réaliser en actes pendant cet automne chaud. Ce n'est pas une lutte économique pour une meilleure répartition de la richesse, pour le droit d'accumuler et la garantie d'une survie un peu plus confortable que celle de son voisin. Nous avons dépassé la question de la quantité pour poser celle de la

qualité de la vie –

 vivre, pas survivre. Plus qu'une révolte contre la vie chère, une révolte pour la vie belle. C'est une lutte politique contre la répartition actuelle du pouvoir au sein de la société qui trouve ses symboles dans la Révolution française et qui prolonge sa haine du privilège et du mépris ; qui semble décidée à

prendre au mot

la vieille devise révolutionnaire pour en demander la réalisation

immédiate

. Sa devise (Liberté, Égalité, Fraternité – ou la mort) a survécu aux siècles et aux régimes monarchiques, impériaux et républicains. Elle semble désormais faire peser sur la démocratie moderne la menace de son propre dépassement. C'est cette menace qu'entend bien conjurer la contre-révolution préventive, par le renforcement d'une forme de républicanisme de guerre, compris comme synthèse des modes de gouvernement par l'assentiment – le réformisme, la division des pouvoirs, le recours au vote – et l'anéantissement – le fascisme, l'état d'exception, la guerre. Pour le dire simplement, ce républicanisme est l'aboutissement du sarkozysme, qui a trouvé dans le macronisme son digne héritier, jusqu'à sa mue en macro-lepénisme. Les forces qui espèrent encore pouvoir réformer la République se drapent d'illusions. Elles refusent de voir que la fille de la Révolution s'est muée en son ennemie la plus féroce. Le progressisme n'est jamais que l'aile gauche du conservatisme.


Il suffit de regarder de plus près le jeu auquel s'adonnent les organisations historiques du mouvement ouvrier, qui ont été critiquées

à raison

comme des forces de récupération et de neutralisation de la révolte ; si tenté qu'on puisse encore parler de « force » pour désigner ces organisations, marginalisées dans le monde du travail et dépourvues de réel pouvoir – tant de victoire réelle que de trahison consciente – dans ses tractations avec le gouvernement. Après la journée de grève du 29 septembre, l'intersyndicale a refusé d'appeler au 17 octobre – comme ce fut le cas pour le 10 septembre 2025 et, avant ça, pendant le mouvement des gilets jaunes. Elle a préféré donner rendez-vous le 5 novembre. Mais, confrontée à la résilience de la révolte et à sa reconduction quotidienne dans les lycées, les universités et dans la rue le samedi, elle n'a rien trouvé d'autre à proposer que la reconduction des cortèges attendus et encadrés, dernière proposition réelle encore

à sa hauteur

. Les 24 et 31 octobre, ces défilés se sont vus relégués aux boulevards des Maréchaux et à l'extérieur des centres-villes, sur des parcours

périphériques

 pour désarmer la masse de manifestants que le déploiement sécuritaire consécutif au soulèvement du 17 octobre n'avait pas convaincu de rentrer à la niche, et rendre invisible à nouveau la colère qui avait défiguré les centres-villes. Les syndicats ont cédé au chantage des Préfectures pour préserver leur rond de serviette à la table des négociations, bien qu'aucune chaise ne les y attende plus depuis …

content:
Sta per iniziare la “Gira por la vida” capitolo Messico, 4 anni dopo il viaggio in Europa.


Da Nodo Solidale


Più di 1500 delegat* zapatist* partiranno a breve in carovana dal Chiapas per arrivare a Città del Messico dove incontreranno decine di collettivi e le organizzazioni de las

Madres Buscadoras

. Un viaggio per abbracciare chi da troppo tempo sta lottando e cercando la verità verso una persona cara o un affetto scomparso, i e le

desaparecidas

, in quella che è la faccia più drammatica e odiosa della guerra contro la vita oggi in Messico.


Questo podcast è il primo contributo prodotto dal Nodo Solidale per iniziare a raccontare questo importantissimo evento che durerà più di un mese e che sta coinvolgendo nell’organizzazione una buona parte dei movimenti dal basso di tutta la capitale messicana e non solo.

title: Will Democrats Pour More Fuel on the Fire in Ukraine?
content:
By Medea Benjamin and Nicolas J. S. Davies, World BEYOND War, November 23, 2026


As Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January, they face a critical choice on Ukraine: Will they help bring an end to a devastating war that is killing and wounding hundreds of thousands of people, or will they double down on a failed strategy of sending more weapons, pouring billions more dollars into the war, and rejecting opportunities for diplomacy?


While Trump has renewed efforts to seek a negotiated solution to the war, which he had promised to solve on the first day of his second term, Democrats in Congress appear ready to reject diplomacy and increase support for the war. The likely incoming House committee chairs Gregory Meeks (Foreign Affairs), Adam Smith (Armed Services) and Jim Himes (Intelligence) have

pledged legislation

to compel Trump to provide greater military, economic and intelligence support to Ukraine.


Democrats are

reportedly

 considering a new Ukraine aid package of up to $15 billion, even as Trump has requested no new Ukraine funding in his 2027 military budget. The effort has bipartisan backing, with Republicans such as Rep. Joe Wilson and Sen. Roger Wicker pushing for continued military aid and tougher sanctions on Russia. Congress could also seek to reverse Trump’s easing of sanctions, setting up a confrontation over whether Washington should increase pressure on Russia or prioritize a negotiated settlement.


Meanwhile, a new series of

 talks

 between the U.S., Russia and Ukraine began in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11. As in previous talks, they agreed on another prisoner exchange, but there was no breakthrough on ending the war.


As Ukraine suffers mounting loss of life, widespread destruction and economic devastation, Russia bears full responsibility for launching its illegal invasion and continuing its brutal attacks. NATO leaders, whose military officers shape and support Ukraine’s war strategy from their joint

headquarters

 at the Wiesbaden US air base in Germany, blame the ongoing conflict solely on Russia, relying on a thick fog of propaganda to evade accountability for their own roles in Ukraine’s destruction.


When the Democrats take charge in Congress, they will find that neither President Zelenskyy nor his European allies have budged from the no-negotiations policy that the Biden administration and then British prime minister

 Boris Johnson

 pressured Ukraine and NATO into adopting in April 2022. After only six weeks of war, Johnson marched into Kyiv and told Zelenskyy to stop negotiating with Putin and commit to a long war, with the ill-defined goal of “weakening” Russia.


Johnson persuaded Zelenskyy to abandon

peace talks

 in Istanbul, where Russia had already agreed to the broad terms of a Ukrainian peace proposal. Falsely claiming to speak for the “

collective West

,” Johnson refused to back any agreement with Russia, and promised Zelenskyy that the UK was “in it for the long run.”


Four and a half years later, some responsible party in the western world must fess up to the reality that this policy has failed miserably, militarizing and strengthening Russia instead of weakening it. Then they must take a fresh, unbiased look at where the war stands and what can be done to end it, if they are to save the Ukrainian people from the catastrophe of a brutal war of attrition fought to the bitter end. It is one thing to condemn Russia for launching a devastating war; it is quite another to prolong that war in an effort to punish Russia, at the cost of countless Ukrainian lives.


According to an October Rating Group poll reported by the Ukrainian news agency UNN, more than 80% of Ukrainians now support a

 negotiated

 peace with Russia, while 56% say they would agree to territorial concessions if they are linked to security guarantees. Only 21% now support an unlimited war to try to restore Ukraine’s pre-2014 borders.


Former UN Assistant Secretary General Michael von der Schulenburg, now a European Member of Parliament from Germany, is

 warning

 that Ukraine is close to collapse, and that the US and Europe’s refusal to face that reality risks making the final stages of the war even more disastrous.


While Ukraine has inflicted serious damage inside Russia, including destroying a major section of the Kerch Strait bridge between Russia and Crimea, Russia has intensified its attacks on bridges across the Dnipro River, which could effectively cut Ukraine in …
